TSM.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd
TSM.address_business: No. 8, Li-Hsin Road 6, Hsinchu Science Park, Hsinchu
TSM.address_mailing: No. 8, Li-Hsin Road 6, Hsinchu Science Park, Hsinchu
TSM.profile_html:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited is a dedicated semiconductor foundry that manufactures integrated circuits for customers based on their proprietary designs. The company provides wafer fabrication services using complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor processes and offers additional services including design support mask making advanced silicon stacking packaging and testing. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited operates manufacturing facilities in Taiwan the United States China Japan and Germany focusing on logic mixed signal radio frequency embedded memory and specialty technologies for diverse applications.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited generates revenue primarily from semiconductor wafer fabrication and related foundry services. The company earns income by manufacturing semiconductors on silicon wafers using its advanced process technologies for customers who provide proprietary circuit designs. Revenue is derived from the production of logic mixed signal radio frequency embedded memory and specialty semiconductors across platforms including high performance computing smartphones internet of things automotive and digital consumer electronics. The company serves a global customer base consisting of fabless semiconductor companies system companies and integrated device manufacturers headquartered in North America Asia Pacific China Japan and Europe Middle East and Africa.

The company operates through the following segments:

  • High Performance Computing segment focuses on manufacturing semiconductors for data centers artificial intelligence cloud infrastructure and high performance applications including AI accelerators central processing units graphics processor units field programmable gate arrays and server processors using advanced nodes such as 2-nanometer 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer FinFET and Nanosheet technologies.
  • Smartphone segment provides logic process technologies for premium and mainstream mobile applications offering nodes from 2-nanometer to 28-nanometer FinFET with embedded specialty technologies such as radio frequency power management image sensors and display chips to support application processors and system-on-chip designs for mobile devices.
  • Internet of Things segment delivers ultra low power logic and specialty technologies for connected devices including sensors microcontrollers and battery powered products featuring 6-nanometer and 12-nanometer ultra low power FinFET services planar transistor based ultra low leakage technologies and comprehensive specialty offerings for radio frequency analog memory sensing and power management to enable AIoT and Edge AI applications.
  • Automotive segment supplies semiconductor technologies for advanced driver assistance systems in vehicle infotainment zonal controllers and next generation vehicle architectures offering 3-nanometer to 16-nanometer FinFET nodes embedded flash memory radio frequency for millimeter wave CMOS image sensors light detection and ranging sensors and power management ICs to support safer smarter and greener automotive systems.
  • Digital Consumer Electronics segment provides technologies for 8K 4K video streaming AI features power efficiency and connectivity in smart TVs set top boxes streaming media devices and digital cameras utilizing 5-nanometer to 22-nanometer FinFET and ultra low power technologies to enable superior performance in consumer entertainment and imaging products.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited holds a leading position in the global semiconductor foundry industry as the largest dedicated foundry by revenue and capacity. The company competes primarily with other pure play foundries and integrated device manufacturers offering foundry services. Its competitive advantages include technology leadership in advanced nodes such as 2-nanometer and 3-nanometer volume production extensive manufacturing scale strong customer relationships and a comprehensive service portfolio spanning design to testing. The company maintains its edge through sustained investment in research and development and close collaboration with customers equipment suppliers and ecosystem partners.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited serves a diverse global customer base that includes many of the world's leading semiconductor companies. Specific customers include fabless innovators in high performance computing mobile and automotive sectors system companies designing processors and accelerators and integrated device manufacturers outsourcing specialty production. The company's customers span multiple industries and geographies relying on its foundry services to manufacture semiconductors for applications ranging from data centers and smartphones to automobiles and industrial equipment.

LLY.address_business: Lilly Corporate Ctr, Drop Code 1094, Indianapolis, 46285 Indiana, US
LLY.address_mailing: Lilly Corporate Center, Drop Code 1094, Indianapolis, 46285 Indiana, US
LLY.profile_html:
Eli Lilly and Company discovers, develops, manufactures, and markets human pharmaceutical products. The company aims to unite caring with discovery to create medicines that improve life for people worldwide. It operates in approximately 90 countries and maintains manufacturing sites in the United States, Europe and Asia. Eli Lilly and Company focuses its research and development efforts on cardiometabolic health, oncology, immunology and neuroscience to address unmet medical needs. The company’s portfolio includes insulin analogs, glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists, anticancer agents, immunomodulators and neuroscience therapeutics. Its products are distributed through a network that reaches hospitals, clinics and retail outlets in nearly all major markets.

Revenue is generated primarily from the sale of its pharmaceutical products to wholesalers, pharmacy benefit managers, insurers, plan sponsors, employers, managed care organizations, group purchasing organizations, government and long term care institutions, hospitals and retail pharmacies. In the United States, 3 wholesale distributors, McKesson Corporation, Cencora, Inc., and Cardinal Health, Inc., each accounted for a significant portion of consolidated revenue in 2023, 2024 and 2025. The company also earns revenue through collaborations and licensing agreements with other biotechnology and pharmaceutical firms that collaborate to develop and market certain products. The company’s collaborations with Boehringer Ingelheim for Jardiance and with Incyte for Olumiant generate milestone payments, royalties and profit sharing. LillyDirect, a direct to patient platform, enables select medicines to be shipped from third party pharmacies to patients while offering adherence support tools and disease education resources. International sales are supported by local sales forces and third party distributors that adapt marketing and distribution to meet regional regulatory requirements.

The company operates through the following segments:

  • Human pharmaceutical products: This segment discovers, develops, manufactures, and markets medicines across therapeutic areas including cardiometabolic health, oncology, immunology, and neuroscience.

Eli Lilly and Company ranks among the largest global pharmaceutical companies, competing with firms such as Pfizer, Merck, Novo Nordisk, and Roche. Its competitive advantages stem from a deep pipeline of innovative medicines, strong intellectual property protection, extensive global manufacturing footprint, and strategic collaborations with other biotechnology firms. The company’s ability to bring differentiated products to market quickly helps it maintain relevance in highly therapeutic areas where effectiveness, safety, and payer coverage are critical. Lilly’s sustained investment in research and development, which employed approximately 12,000 scientists and technical staff at the end of 2025, fuels a steady flow of new drug candidates and line extensions. The firm’s scale enables it to negotiate favorable terms with suppliers and payers while maintaining a diversified geographic revenue base that reduces reliance on any single market. The company’s pipeline includes candidates such as insulin efsitora alfa and orforglipron, which are under regulatory review for diabetes and obesity. Continuous investment in manufacturing capacity has expanded production sites in the United States, Europe and Asia to meet growing demand.

The company serves a diverse customer base that includes major wholesale distributors such as McKesson Corporation, Cencora, Inc., and Cardinal Health, Inc.; numerous pharmacy benefit managers; insurers; hospitals; physicians; and patients. Through its LillyDirect platform, Eli Lilly and Company also reaches individual consumers seeking home delivery of prescribed medicines. Long term care facilities, managed care organizations and government agencies constitute important purchasers for therapies addressing chronic conditions such as diabetes and cancer. Physician offices and academic medical centers serve as key prescribers who influence product adoption through clinical guidelines and formulary recommendations. Retail pharmacies and chain drug stores provide final dispensing points that connect Lilly’s medicines with everyday consumers. No single customer other than the 3 major wholesalers accounted for more than 10% of consolidated revenue in recent years.

JPM.profile_html:
JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a leading financial services firm based in the United States with operations worldwide that offers investment banking consumer and small business banking commercial banking financial transaction processing and asset management services.

The firm generates revenue through interest earned on loans and deposits fees from investment banking underwriting and advisory services trading revenues and asset management fees charged to clients.

The company operates through the following segments Consumer & Community Banking Commercial & Investment Bank and Asset & Wealth Management.

  • Consumer & Community Banking offers retail banking products such as checking and savings accounts mortgages credit cards and small business loans to individual consumers and small enterprises.
  • Commercial & Investment Bank delivers investment banking services including underwriting mergers and acquisitions advisory lending and treasury solutions to corporations governments and institutional clients.
  • Asset & Wealth Management provides investment management wealth planning and private banking services to high net worth individuals families and institutions.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. ranks among the largest banks in the United States competing with firms such as Bank of America Citigroup Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs and benefits from a diversified business model a strong global brand extensive distribution network and deep relationships with corporate and institutional clients.

The firm serves millions of individual consumers small businesses corporations governments and institutional investors across the United States and internationally.

XOM.address_mailing: 22777 Springwoods Village Parkway, Spring, 77389 Texas, US
XOM.profile_html:
ExxonMobil Holdings Corp operates as an integrated energy and petrochemical company engaged in the exploration, production, refining, and marketing of oil and natural gas, as well as the manufacturing and sale of chemical and specialty products. The company conducts its operations through four primary business segments: Upstream, Energy Products, Chemical Products, and Specialty Products. These segments encompass activities ranging from hydrocarbon extraction to the production of fuels, lubricants, performance chemicals, and advanced materials.

The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of crude oil, natural gas, refined petroleum products such as gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, and heating oils, as well as a broad range of petrochemicals including olefins, polyolefins, and performance chemicals. Specialty Products contribute revenue from the sale of advanced materials such as Proxxima™ systems, carbon materials, and lithium-based products. Sales are made to a diverse customer base including industrial manufacturers, transportation companies, utilities, and wholesale distributors across global markets.

The company operates through the following segments: Upstream, Energy Products, Chemical Products, and Specialty Products.

  • Upstream: This segment focuses on the exploration, development, and production of crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids, bitumen, and synthetic oil. Operations span key regions including the Permian Basin, Guyana, and liquefied natural gas projects. The segment leverages advantaged assets and projects to drive volume growth and improve returns.
  • Energy Products: This segment is responsible for the refining, supply, trading, and transportation of petroleum products. It produces gasoline, naphthas, heating oils, kerosene, diesel, aviation fuels, heavy fuels, and other energy products. The segment emphasizes advantaged volume growth through capacity expansion, asset optimization, and the production of lower-emission fuels and performance products.
  • Chemical Products: This segment manufactures and markets olefins, polyolefins, aromatics, and a variety of performance chemicals. It benefits from North America ethane feed advantages and focuses on high-margin specialty chemical products. The segment serves industries requiring plastics, elastomers, solvents, and chemical intermediates for applications in packaging, automotive, construction, and consumer goods.
  • Specialty Products: This segment produces advanced materials including Proxxima™ systems, carbon materials, lithium, and low-carbon data center solutions. It also develops hydrogen, ammonia, and plastic waste feedstock for advanced recycling. The segment supports ExxonMobil’s lower-emission initiatives through innovation in materials science and sustainable technology development.

ExxonMobil Holdings Corp holds a leading position in the global energy and petrochemical industries, competing with major integrated oil companies and specialized chemical producers. Its competitive advantages stem from scale, technological expertise, integrated operations across the value chain, and disciplined capital allocation. The company maintains strong financial flexibility and invests in advantaged projects that deliver superior returns, supported by its proprietary research and development capabilities.

The company serves a broad customer base that includes industrial manufacturers, transportation and logistics companies, utility providers, refining and marketing companies, and distributors of fuels and chemicals. Specific customer relationships are not disclosed in the filing, but the company’s products are used globally in sectors such as automotive, aviation, construction, agriculture, and consumer goods manufacturing.

V.address_mailing: P.O. Box 8999, San Francisco, 94128-8999 California, US
V.profile_html:
Visa is one of the world’s leaders in digital payments. The company facilitates secure reliable and efficient global commerce through its proprietary network VisaNet.

Visa generates revenue primarily from fees paid for processing transactions on its network. Service revenue is earned for providing support such as authorization clearing settlement and value added services related to issuing and acceptance. Data processing revenue comes from authorization clearing settlement and other maintenance services that enable money movement. International transaction revenue is derived from cross border payment processing and currency conversion. Other revenue includes license fees for the Visa brand and fees for advisory and other services.

The company operates through the following segments: Consumer Payments, Commercial and Money Movement Solutions, and Value Added Services.

  • Consumer Payments focuses on strengthening card based payment acceptance and expanding non card based options such as digital wallets and real time payments while offering credit debit and prepaid products and promoting innovations like Tap to Everything token technology and services for affluent consumers.
  • Commercial and Money Movement Solutions includes Visa Commercial Solutions for business to business payments and Visa Direct for person to person business to consumer and government to consumer money movement aiming to digitize commerce across B2B B2C G2C and P2P flows.
  • Value Added Services comprises Issuing Solutions Acceptance Solutions Risk and Security Solutions and Advisory and Other Services providing cardholder engagement merchant acceptance risk management fraud prevention and advisory expertise to financial institutions merchants and partners.

Visa ranks among the largest global payment networks processing billions of transactions each year and competes with companies such as American Express Mastercard UnionPay and JCB while maintaining advantages from its extensive brand acceptance worldwide its secure VisaNet infrastructure and its ongoing investment in tokenization and emerging technologies like stablecoins and AI.

The company serves a broad base that includes approximately fourteen thousand five hundred financial institutions hundreds of millions of merchants and billions of cardholders as well as governments fintechs and non governmental organizations worldwide.

JNJ.profile_html:
Johnson & Johnson is a global healthcare company engaged in the research development manufacture and sale of a broad range of products related to human health and well being. The firm operates through subsidiaries that conduct business in virtually every country worldwide. Its core activities include discovering new therapies producing medical devices and delivering products to hospitals clinicians and patients. Johnson & Johnson was incorporated in the State of New Jersey in 1887 and today employs approximately 138 200 people. The company's mission is to improve health outcomes through innovation and responsible business practices.

Revenue is generated primarily from the sale of pharmaceutical products and medical technology devices. The Innovative Medicine segment sells prescription medicines directly to retailers wholesalers distributors hospitals and healthcare professionals. The MedTech segment sells products such as cardiovascular devices orthopaedic implants surgical instruments and vision care items to wholesalers hospitals retailers and eye care professionals. Key contributors to total sales include DARZALEX STELARA TREMFYA XARELTO and the ACUVUE contact lens line. Additional revenue comes from licensing agreements royalties and collaborative development arrangements with external partners.

The company operates through the following segments: Innovative Medicine and MedTech.

  • The Innovative Medicine segment focuses on therapeutic areas including oncology immunology neuroscience pulmonary hypertension infectious diseases and cardiovascular and metabolism. Key products in this segment include CARVYKTI (ciltabtagene autoleucel) a CAR T cell therapy for relapsed refractory multiple myeloma DARZALEX (daratumumab) a treatment for multiple myeloma DARZALEX FASPRO (daratumumab and hyaluronidase fihj) a treatment for multiple myeloma and light chain AL amyloidosis ERLEADA (apalutamide) a next generation androgen receptor inhibitor for the treatment of patients with prostate cancer IMBRUVICA (ibrutinib) a treatment for certain B cell malignancies or blood cancers and chronic graft versus host disease RYBREVANT (amivantamab) a fully human bispecific antibody for adults with EGFR mutated non small cell lung cancer and LAZCLUZE (lazertinib) an oral brain penetrant EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor for non small cell lung cancer RYBREVANT FASPRO (amivantamab and hyaluronidase lpuj) a subcutaneous therapy for patients with non small cell lung cancer TALVEY (talquetamab tgvs) a bispecific antibody for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple CII a treatment for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder INVEGA SUSTENNA/XEPLION (paliperidone palmitate) for the treatment of schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder in adults INVEGA patients and for thromboprophylaxis in pediatric patients following the Fontan procedure. Many of these medicines were developed in collaboration with strategic partners or are licensed from other companies and maintain active lifecycle development programs.
  • The MedTech segment develops and manufactures a broad portfolio of products used in cardiovascular orthopaedics surgery and vision supporting physicians hospitals eye care professionals and healthcare systems across a wide range of acute and elective procedures. These products are designed to address disease states where procedural intervention plays a central role in treatment and patient outcomes. The Cardiovascular portfolio includes electrophysiology products used to diagnose and treat heart rhythm disorders mechanical circulatory support technologies (Abiomed) used in patients with cardiogenic shock or those undergoing a high risk percutaneous coronary intervention circulatory restoration products (Shockwave) for the treatment of calcified coronary artery disease and peripheral artery disease and neurovascular care that treats stroke and other conditions. These offerings are primarily delivered through minimally invasive catheter based approaches and are used by interventional cardiologists electrophysiologists and neurointerventional specialists. The Orthopaedics portfolio includes products and enabling technologies that support joint reconstruction trauma spine sports related injuries and others. The Surgery portfolio includes a range of surgical products and enabling technologies for use across open laparoscopic and robotic surgical procedures. This portfolio includes instrumentation energy devices stapling systems wound closure biosurgery products and digital and robotic technologies designed to support procedural consistency and efficiency across multiple surgical specialties. MA.address_mailing: 2000 Purchase Street, Purchase, 10577 New York, US
MA.profile_html:
Mastercard is a technology company in the global payments industry that connects consumers, financial institutions, merchants, governments, digital partners, businesses and other organizations worldwide by enabling electronic payments and making those payment transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. The company operates a payments network that provides choice and flexibility for consumers, merchants and its customers by switching (authorizing, clearing and settling) payment transactions. Mastercard offers consumer and commercial payment products, capture new payment flows and provides services and solutions including security solutions, consumer acquisition and engagement services, business and market insights, digital and authentication, processing and gateway and other solutions.

Mastercard generates revenue from a wide range of payments solutions provided to its customers. The company classifies its net revenues into two categories: payment network and value-added services and solutions. Within the payment network, revenue is primarily generated from charging fees to customers based on gross dollar volume on cards carrying its brands and for providing switching and other network-related services. Within value-added services and solutions, revenue is generated primarily from security solutions, consumer acquisition and engagement services, business and market insights, digital and authentication solutions, processing and gateway, and other solutions including ACH batch and real-time account-based payments and solutions, bill payments, cross-border services and open finance.

The company operates through the following segments:

  • Payment Network: This segment includes switching authorization, clearing and settlement of payment transactions, providing interoperability among stakeholders through its global payments network and franchise model, enabling transactions in more than 150 currencies and across more than 220 countries and territories, and offering account-based payments capabilities including ACH batch and real-time account-based payments.
  • Value-Added Services and Solutions: This segment includes security solutions designed to safeguard the payments and digital ecosystem from fraud and cyber-attacks, consumer acquisition and engagement services that drive customer activation and loyalty, business and market insights providing data analytics and advisory services, digital and authentication solutions enabling secure digital commerce, processing and gateway offerings that support e-commerce and secure online payments, and other solutions such as ACH batch and real-time account-based payments, bill payments, cross-border services and open finance.

Mastercard holds a leading position in the global payments industry as one of the major general purpose payments networks competing worldwide with Visa, American Express, JCB, China UnionPay and Discover. The company's competitive advantages include its global network, highly adaptable and world-class payments infrastructure, franchise model establishing rules and bearing financial risk, multi-rail capabilities offering choice, globally recognized and trusted brands, data and AI products and services incorporating responsible design principles, world-class talent and culture guided by the Mastercard Way, leading-edge technology advancing solution quality and diversity, and local presence and government engagement enabling service to a broad array of participants.

Mastercard serves a diverse customer base including consumers, financial institutions, merchants, governments, digital partners, businesses and other organizations worldwide. The company enables account holders to use its products at hundreds of millions of acceptance locations and digital access points globally, working with issuers and acquirers around the globe to facilitate transaction switching.

ABBV.address_mailing: 1 North Waukegan Road, North Chicago, 60064 Illinois, US
ABBV.profile_html:
AbbVie Inc. is a global, diversified research-based biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the development and commercialization of innovative medicines and therapies for complex and serious diseases. The company focuses its efforts on immunology, neuroscience, oncology, and aesthetics, leveraging its expertise in research and innovation to address significant unmet medical needs worldwide. AbbVie integrates research and development, manufacturing, commercialization, and sales into a cohesive global operation aimed at delivering advanced therapeutic solutions to patients and healthcare providers.

AbbVie generates revenue primarily through the sale of its pharmaceutical products across therapeutic areas. Key revenue drivers include immunology treatments such as Skyrizi, Rinvoq, and Humira; neuroscience products like Vraylar, Botox Therapeutic, Ubrelvy, and Qulipta; oncology therapies including Imbruvica, Venclexta, and Elahere; and aesthetics offerings such as Botox Cosmetic and the Juvederm Collection. The company also earns revenue from eye care products like Ozurdex and Lumigan/Ganfort, as well as other key products such as Mavyret for hepatitis C, Creon for pancreatic insufficiency, and Linzess/Constella for gastrointestinal conditions. AbbVie sells its products globally to wholesalers, distributors, government agencies, healthcare facilities, specialty pharmacies, independent retailers, and directly to physicians and licensed healthcare providers for certain products.

AbbVie operates as a single global business segment dedicated to the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization, and sale of innovative medicines and therapies.

  • AbbVie's single global segment encompasses the discovery and development of new compounds, the manufacturing and supply of products, and the coordination of commercial efforts including marketing, sales, and distribution of its medicines and therapies across immunology, neuroscience, oncology, aesthetics, and eye care.

AbbVie holds a strong competitive position in the biopharmaceutical industry, particularly in immunology where its Skyrizi and Rinvoq products have demonstrated leadership in treating autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, and inflammatory bowel disease. The company faces competition from other research-based pharmaceutical and biotechnology firms developing IL-23 inhibitors, JAK inhibitors, biosimilars, and targeted therapies in oncology. AbbVie maintains advantages through its robust pipeline, deep expertise in biologics and small molecules, significant investment in research and development, and intellectual property protection for key products such as risankizumab and upadacitinib, with composition of matter patents expected to expire in 2033. Additionally, its diversified portfolio across high-need therapeutic areas reduces reliance on any single product or market.

AbbVie serves a diverse customer base including physicians, external experts, healthcare providers, managed care organizations such as health maintenance organizations and pharmacy benefit managers, hospitals, and state and federal government agencies including Medicaid programs, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the Department of Defense. The company also engages in direct-to-consumer marketing for certain products where appropriate and permitted by regulation. AbbVie's products are distributed through wholesalers and distributors, with McKesson Corporation, Cardinal Health Inc., and Cencora Inc. accounting for substantially all of its pharmaceutical product sales in the United States.

ORCL.profile_html:
Oracle Corporation provides products and services that address enterprise information technology needs. The company develops and delivers enterprise applications and infrastructure offerings through on premise, cloud based, and hybrid deployment models. Its core activities include licensing software, providing cloud subscriptions, selling hardware systems, and offering professional support services. With a global workforce of approximately 162,000 employees and a presence in more than 175 countries, Oracle serves a broad range of industries from finance to healthcare.

Oracle generates revenue from the sale of software licenses and cloud subscriptions for its applications and infrastructure technologies. It also earns income from hardware products such as engineered systems, servers, and storage, and from professional services including consulting and advanced customer support. Additionally, customers frequently purchase license support and hardware support contracts, which provide recurring revenue streams. Cloud services revenues accounted for 43% of total revenues in fiscal 2025, reflecting the growing shift to subscription based models. In fiscal 2025, the company invested $9.9 billion in research and development to enhance its existing portfolio and develop new technologies.

The company operates through the following segments: cloud and license, hardware, and services.

  • Cloud and License: This segment offers Oracle Cloud Applications such as Fusion Cloud ERP, EPM, SCM, HCM and NetSuite, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure services including compute, storage, networking and Autonomous Database, and related license and support offerings for applications, database, middleware and Java technologies, while providing flexible deployment options for public cloud, private data center or hybrid environments, and integrating emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning into its portfolio.
  • Hardware: This segment provides Oracle Engineered Systems, enterprise servers, storage solutions, and industry specific hardware products, along with hardware support contracts that deliver maintenance, repairs and technical assistance, while enabling seamless integration with Oracle Cloud services and offering deployment flexibility for on premise, cloud based, and hybrid environments.
  • Services: This segment delivers consulting services, advanced customer services, Oracle Cloud Operations, and other professional services that help customers implement, manage and optimize Oracle applications and infrastructure, while assisting customers in migrating to the cloud, optimizing performance, and leveraging Oracle's expertise in enterprise software, hardware and cloud infrastructure.

Oracle holds a strong position in the enterprise software market, competing with companies such as Microsoft, Amazon, International Business Machines, SAP, and Salesforce. Its competitive advantages stem from a broad portfolio of integrated cloud and on premise products, flexible deployment models, significant investment in research and development, and a global sales and partner network. The company’s scale, deep expertise in database and middleware technologies, and ability to offer end to end solutions from applications to infrastructure further differentiate it from rivals.

Oracle serves a diverse customer base that includes businesses of various sizes, government agencies, educational institutions, and resellers. Specific customers mentioned in the filing include an AI product company using OCI for generative AI models, a global technology company relying on OCI for logistics and mobile applications, a multinational financial institution running banking applications on Oracle Exadata Cloud@Customer, and a global consumer products company utilizing Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP for accounting, risk management, supply chain, and financial planning. The company’s customer base spans North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East, reflecting its global reach.

CVX.name: Chevron Corp
CVX.profile_html:
Chevron Corporation manages its investments in subsidiaries and affiliates and provides administrative financial management and technology support to U. S. and international subsidiaries that engage in integrated energy and chemicals operations. Upstream operations consist of exploring for developing producing and transporting crude oil and natural gas processing liquefaction transportation and regasification associated with liquefied natural gas transporting crude oil by major international oil export pipelines transporting storage and marketing of natural gas carbon capture and storage and a gas-to-liquids plant. Downstream operations consist of refining crude oil into petroleum products marketing of crude oil refined products and lubricants manufacturing and marketing of renewable fuels transporting crude oil and refined products by pipeline marine vessel motor equipment and rail car and manufacturing and marketing of commodity petrochemicals plastics for industrial uses and fuel and lubricant additives.

The company generates revenue primarily from the sale of crude oil natural gas natural gas liquids refined petroleum products lubricants renewable fuels and petrochemicals. Revenue is earned through the production and marketing of hydrocarbons the refining and distribution of petroleum products and the manufacturing and sale of specialty chemicals and performance additives. Customers include industrial users transportation firms utilities and individual consumers worldwide.

The company operates through the following segments: Upstream Downstream and Chemicals.

  • Upstream activities involve exploration development production and transportation of crude oil and natural gas including liquefied natural gas projects carbon capture and storage initiatives and gas-to-liquids facilities.
  • Downstream activities include refining crude oil into gasoline diesel jet fuel and other petroleum products marketing of fuels lubricants and renewable fuels as well as manufacturing and marketing of commodity petrochemicals plastics and additives.
  • Chemicals activities focus on developing manufacturing and marketing performance additives for lubricating oils and fuels producing olefins polyolefins and aromatics through joint ventures and investing in the specialty chemical and specialty plastics markets.

Chevron holds a strong position in the global petroleum and petrochemical industries competing with fully integrated majors such as ExxonMobil Royal Dutch Shell BP and TotalEnergies as well as independent refiners marketers and national oil companies. Its competitive advantages stem from a large diversified asset base integrated upstream downstream and chemicals operations technological expertise in deepwater and shale development and a commitment to lower carbon intensity through carbon capture renewable fuels and hydrogen initiatives.

The company serves individual consumers through its branded Chevron Texaco and Caltex service stations transportation firms utilities industrial manufacturers and aviation customers. Specific customer names are not disclosed in the filing.

Caterpillar Inc. is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines, and diesel-electric locomotives. Operating in highly competitive global markets, the company designs, manufactures, and markets machinery and power systems while providing financing solutions through its financial products segment. With $67.6 billion in sales and revenues in 2025, Caterpillar serves industries critical to infrastructure development, resource extraction, and energy production, supported by a vast independent dealer network spanning 190 countries.

The company generates revenue through the sale of machinery, engines, and power systems, as well as related parts, services, and work tools. Additionally, Caterpillar earns financing income via its financial products segment, which offers loans, leases, and revolving charge accounts to customers and dealers for equipment purchases and leases. The company also provides insurance services, including liability, property, and cargo coverage, further diversifying its revenue streams. Its customer base includes construction firms, mining companies, energy producers, and industrial operators, with financing solutions tailored to support equipment acquisition and operational needs.

The company operates through the following segments:

  • Construction Industries: This segment supports customers in infrastructure and building construction, offering machinery such as asphalt pavers, motor graders, excavators, and wheel loaders. It serves heavy and general construction, rental, quarry, aggregates, and mining industries, with research and development focused on next-generation construction machines. The segment competes in both developed and developing markets, where customer priorities range from purchase price to long-term productivity and cost efficiency.
  • Resource Industries: This segment provides high-productivity equipment for surface and underground mining, heavy construction, and quarry and aggregates applications. Products include electric rope shovels, draglines, hydraulic shovels, and large mining trucks, alongside technology solutions like fleet management and autonomous machine capabilities. The segment emphasizes equipment reliability and total cost of ownership, catering to customers in mineral extraction and large-scale construction projects.
  • Power & Energy: This segment supplies reciprocating engines, generator sets, turbines, and electrified powertrain solutions for oil and gas, power generation, marine, rail, and industrial applications. It also offers remanufacturing services for engines and components, diesel-electric locomotives, and rail-related products. Compliance with emissions regulations is a key focus, with investments directed toward developing zero-emission power sources and sustainable technologies.
  • Financial Products: This segment, primarily conducted through Cat Financial and insurance subsidiaries, provides financing and insurance solutions to customers and dealers. Offerings include loans, leases, revolving charge accounts, and wholesale financing for inventory and rental fleets. The segment also underwrites insurance programs covering contractual liability, cargo, and equipment physical damage, supporting both Caterpillar’s operations and its dealer network.

Caterpillar holds a dominant position in its industries, competing on product performance, customer service, quality, and price. In construction and mining, its key global competitors include Komatsu, Hitachi Construction Machinery, Volvo Construction Equipment, and Deere Construction & Forestry, alongside regional players like Sany Heavy Industry and XCMG in China. In power and energy, competitors such as Cummins, Rolls-Royce Power Systems, and Siemens Energy challenge Caterpillar in engine and turbine markets, while Wabtec and Alstom compete in rail-related businesses. The company’s competitive advantages stem from its extensive dealer network, advanced technology integration, and ability to offer comprehensive solutions, including financing and aftermarket services. Its focus on operational excellence and customer-driven innovation further strengthens its market leadership.

The company’s customer base spans a broad range of industries and geographies. In construction, it serves infrastructure developers, building contractors, rental companies, and quarry operators. Mining customers include global operators extracting copper, iron ore, coal, gold, and other minerals. Power and energy clients encompass oil and gas producers, power generation companies, marine operators, and rail companies. Caterpillar also supports industrial applications through engine and power system sales. Its financial products segment caters to equipment buyers, dealers, and end-users requiring financing or insurance solutions. The company’s global reach is reinforced by its dealer network, which includes 150 independent dealers and direct sales forces for select products like turbines and locomotives.

BAC.profile_html:
Bank of America Corporation is a Delaware corporation and a bank holding company that operates as a financial holding company. It provides a full range of banking, investing, asset management, and other financial and risk management products and services to individual consumers, small- and middle-market businesses, institutional investors, large corporations, and governments worldwide. The company is one of the world’s largest financial institutions with principal executive offices located in Charlotte, North Carolina.

Bank of America Corporation generates revenue through interest income from loans and investments, fees from banking and investment services, trading profits, and asset management fees. Its revenue streams are derived from consumer banking, wealth and investment management, corporate banking, and global markets activities, serving a diverse client base across retail, commercial, and institutional sectors.

The company operates through the following segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), Global Banking, and Global Markets, with the remaining operations recorded in All Other.

  • Consumer Banking provides deposit, lending, and other banking products and services to individual consumers and small businesses through its branch network and digital platforms.
  • Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) offers investment advice, brokerage services, retirement solutions, and wealth management to individual investors and institutions through its advisory and brokerage businesses.
  • Global Banking delivers lending, treasury management, and investment banking products and services to middle-market and large corporate clients, government entities, and institutional investors globally.
  • Global Markets provides sales and trading services, risk management products, and financing solutions related to fixed income, currencies, commodities, and equities to institutional clients including corporations, governments, and financial institutions.

Bank of America Corporation operates in a highly competitive environment facing competition from banks, thrifts, credit unions, investment banking firms, brokerage houses, insurance companies, mortgage lenders, asset managers, hedge funds, private equity firms, and technology-driven financial service providers. Its competitive advantages stem from its scale, diversified business model, extensive branch and digital distribution networks, global reach, and long-standing client relationships across multiple financial service lines.

The company serves individual consumers, small- and middle-market businesses, institutional investors, large corporations, and governments. Its customer base includes retail clients accessing checking and savings accounts, small businesses utilizing business banking services, corporations relying on treasury and investment banking solutions, and institutional clients engaging in capital markets and risk management transactions.

KO.address_mailing: One Coca Cola Plaza, Atlanta, 30313 Georgia, US
KO.profile_html:
The Coca-Cola Company is a total beverage company that owns, licenses, and markets a wide range of nonalcoholic and alcoholic beverage brands across more than 200 countries and territories. The company's core operations involve producing beverage concentrates, syrups, and finished products, which are distributed through a global network of independent bottling partners, distributors, wholesalers, retailers, and its own consolidated bottling and distribution operations. The Coca-Cola Company's success is driven by its ability to connect with consumers through a diverse portfolio of brands that meet varying tastes, needs, and lifestyles worldwide.

The Coca-Cola Company generates revenue primarily through the sale of beverage concentrates, syrups, and finished beverages to bottling partners and directly to retailers, distributors, and wholesalers. Its concentrate operations involve selling flavorings and syrups to authorized bottlers, who then produce and package finished beverages for sale. Finished product operations, including consolidated and non-bottling distribution, generate revenue by selling ready-to-drink beverages such as sparkling soft drinks, water, sports drinks, juices, teas, coffees, and plant-based drinks to retailers and other intermediaries. The company also earns revenue from direct-to-consumer sales through retail stores operated by Costa and from alcohol beverage ventures in select international markets and via a firewalled subsidiary in the United States.

The company operates through the following segments:

  • EMEA: This segment encompasses the Europe, Middle East, and Africa region and includes the results of Costa (excluding the ready-to-drink business), innocent, and doğadan businesses, which were transferred from the former Global Ventures segment. It also includes revenue from ready-to-drink Costa sales through retail stores, regardless of store location, as these are reported within EMEA. Key brands in this segment include Costa, innocent, and various regional sparkling soft drink and water brands.
  • Latin America: This segment covers beverage operations across Latin American countries and includes the production and distribution of concentrate and finished products through the company's bottling partners. Major brands sold in this segment include Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Schweppes (in certain countries), and regional juice and water brands such as Del Valle and Santa Clara. The segment also supports value-added dairy and plant-based beverages like fairlife and Simply in select markets.
  • North America: This segment includes the United States and Canada and generates revenue from concentrate sales to bottling partners, fountain syrup sales to retailers and wholesalers, and finished product distribution. Key brands in this segment are Coca-Cola, Diet Coke/Coca-Cola Light, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, Sprite, Fanta, Dasani, smartwater, vitaminwater, Powerade, BODYARMOR, Minute Maid, Simply, fairlife, Core Power, and Costa ready-to-drink products where applicable. The company also manufactures and sells fountain syrups directly in this segment.
  • Asia Pacific: This segment serves markets across Asia and the Pacific, including China, India, Japan, Australia, and Southeast Asia, with a focus on concentrate and finished product sales via bottling partners. Leading brands in this segment include Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Schweppes (in certain countries), Aquarius, Ayataka, BODYARMOR, Ciel, Dasani, Fuze Tea, Georgia, glacéau smartwater, glacéau vitaminwater, Gold Peak, I LOHAS, Powerade, Topo Chico, Minute Maid, Minute Maid Pulpy, and Maaza. The segment also supports coffee and tea brands such as Costa and Georgia, and plant-based beverages like Simply and fairlife where available.
  • Bottling Investments: This segment consists of the company's consolidated bottling and distribution operations, which produce and sell finished beverages directly to retailers, distributors, and wholesalers. These operations typically generate higher net operating revenues but lower gross profit margins than concentrate operations. The segment includes bottling facilities in various global markets where the company has taken control to improve performance and efficiency. It supports the same broad portfolio of brands as the geographic segments, including Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Dasani, Minute Maid, Powerade, and BODYARMOR, depending on the location of the bottling operation.

The Coca-Cola Company holds a leading position in the global nonalcoholic beverage industry, characterized by its ownership of some of the world's most valuable and recognizable brands, including Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, and Dasani. It competes primarily with PepsiCo, Nestlé, Keurig Dr Pepper, Danone, Suntory Beverage & Food, and Red Bull, among others, in categories such as sparkling soft drinks, water, sports drinks, juices, teas, and plant-based beverages. The company's competitive advantages include its powerful brand portfolio, extensive global bottling and distribution network, sophisticated marketing capabilities, and continuous innovation in product development and packaging.

The Coca-Cola Company serves a diverse global customer base that includes individual consumers purchasing ready-to-drink beverages from retailers, convenience stores, vending machines, and foodservice outlets such as restaurants and cafes. Its business also relies on relationships with independent bottling partners, distributors, wholesalers, and large retail chains that distribute its products to end users. Additionally, the company sells directly to consumers through Costa retail locations and provides fountain syrups to foodservice establishments such as restaurants, theaters, and amusement parks for immediate beverage preparation.

DELL.address_mailing: One Dell Way, Round Rock, 78682 Texas, US
DELL.profile_html:
Dell Technologies is a global technology leader focused on delivering comprehensive and innovative technology solutions for the data and artificial intelligence (AI) era. Operating across the IT industry, the company provides integrated solutions ranging from client devices and peripherals to mission-critical infrastructure across servers, networking, and storage. Dell's core activity involves designing, deploying, and supporting secure, software-defined, and cloud-native infrastructure solutions that extend from the edge to the core and into the cloud. The company utilizes its extensive portfolio to help customers address evolving IT needs, drive business outcomes, and capture growth across its global footprint of over 170 countries.

The company generates revenue through a mix of physical hardware sales, specialized infrastructure solutions, and recurring service offerings. Primary revenue streams include the sale of personal computers and peripherals, as well as large-scale data center and cloud infrastructure components. Revenue generation is supported by the Dell Payment Solutions portfolio, which offers consumers and businesses financial flexibility through utility, subscription, as-a-Service models, leases, and loans. Furthermore, the company generates recurring revenue from services, maintenance, and usage-based offerings, which helps stabilize and grow revenue streams over multiyear agreements.

The company operates through two principal reportable business segments: the Infrastructure Solutions Group and the Client Solutions Group. These segments guide the company's product development and operational deployment across the enterprise market.

  • Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG): This segment provides comprehensive solutions enabling digital transformations by addressing needs related to AI, machine learning, data analytics, and multicloud environments. ISG solutions are built to streamline IT operations in public, private, and on-premises cloud environments. Major product categories within this segment include AI-optimized servers, which handle demanding compute-intensive workloads like AI model training; traditional servers and networking, which form the foundational layer for general-purpose workloads; and storage solutions, covering primary, unstructured, and data protection offerings.
  • Client Solutions Group (CSG): CSG offers branded personal computers, encompassing notebooks, desktops, and workstations, along with branded peripherals such as displays and docking stations. This segment focuses on optimizing performance, security, and manageability for the end-user. Major product categories are the commercial offerings, designed for complex needs like IT modernization, and the consumer offerings, which provide solutions for essential and high-end user computing experiences.

Dell Technologies holds a strong position by offering end-to-end solutions and comprehensive services that span the entire technology stack. Its competitive advantages include a robust go-to-market strategy that incorporates an extensive direct sales force and a global network of channel partners. The combination of a world-class supply chain and global services footprint allows the company to provide scalable and integrated solutions at a competitive price. While it competes with both branded and generic competitors, its ability to provide full-stack, customized solutions helps maintain market leadership.

The company serves an extremely diverse global customer base, ranging from the world's largest corporations and large enterprises to small and medium-sized businesses. Additionally, Dell Technologies serves government and not-for-profit organizations, as well as individual consumers. The scale of its operations means it supports various global entities requiring technology infrastructure.

MRK.name: Merck & Co., Inc.

MRK.address_mailing: 126 East Lincoln Avenue, P.O. Box 2000, Rahway, 07065 New Jersey, US
MRK.profile_html:
Merck & Co., Inc. is a global health care company that delivers innovative health solutions through its prescription medicines, biologic therapies, vaccines and animal health products. The company operates principally on a product basis and serves both human and animal health markets worldwide. As of December 31, 2025 it employed approximately 75,000 people across its operations.

Merck generates revenue primarily from the sale of human health pharmaceutical and vaccine products as well as animal health pharmaceuticals vaccines and health management solutions. In 2025 total company sales amounted to $65,011 million with pharmaceutical sales of $58,142 million and animal health sales of $6,354 million. Within the pharmaceutical segment the top selling products were Keytruda at $31,680 million Gardasil or Gardasil 9 at $5,233 million Januvia or Janumet at $2,544 million and ProQuad or M-M-R II or Varivax at $2,451 million. The company also earns alliance revenue from collaborations such as Lynparza and Lenvima which contributed $1,450 million and $1,053 million respectively in 2025. Animal health sales were divided between livestock products at $3,896 million and companion animal products at $2,458 million. Other revenues primarily comprising miscellaneous corporate revenues and third party manufacturing arrangements contributed $515 million in 2025.

The company operates through the following segments: Pharmaceutical and Animal Health.

  • Pharmaceutical: This segment includes human health pharmaceutical and vaccine products. Human health pharmaceutical products consist of therapeutic and preventive agents sold by prescription for the treatment of human disorders. Human health vaccine products consist of preventive pediatric adolescent and adult vaccines. Key franchises in this segment include oncology led by Keytruda immunology vaccines such as Gardasil ProQuad Vaxneuvance hospital acute care products like Bridion and Prevymis cardiometabolic and respiratory treatments including Winrevair Adempas Verquvo and Ohtuvayre virology agents such as Lagevrio Isentress Delstrigo and Pifeltro neuroscience products like Belsomra and diabetes treatments including Januvia and Janumet. In 2025 the pharmaceutical segment generated $58,142 million in sales.
  • Animal Health: This segment discovers develops manufactures and markets a wide range of veterinary pharmaceutical and vaccine products health management solutions and services and digital identification traceability and monitoring products. It serves livestock and companion animal species with products such as antibiotics vaccines parasiticides fertility management tools and nutrition supplements. In 2025 the animal health segment generated $6,354 million in sales with livestock products accounting for $3,896 million and companion animal products for $2,458 million.

Merck holds a leading position in the global pharmaceutical industry competing with other large research based companies generic manufacturers and specialized animal health firms. Its competitive advantages arise from a robust research and development pipeline a diversified portfolio of patented products strategic alliances and collaborations and extensive global manufacturing and distribution capabilities. The company invested heavily in R&D with approximately 24,700 employees engaged in research activities as of December 31, 2025 and maintains a broad clinical pipeline spanning oncology cardiovascular metabolic infectious diseases neuroscience immunology ophthalmology respiratory diseases and vaccines.

The company’s customers include drug wholesalers and retailers hospitals government agencies managed health care providers such as health maintenance organizations and pharmacy benefit managers physicians veterinarians distributors animal producers farmers and pet owners. Specific customer names are not disclosed in the filing.

Within the pharmaceutical segment the top selling products were Keytruda at $31,680 million Gardasil or Gardasil 9 at $5,233 million Januvia or Janumet at $2,544 million and ProQuad or M-M-R II or Varivax at $2,451 million. The company also earns alliance revenue from collaborations such as Lynparza and Lenvima which contributed $1,450 million and $1,053 million respectively in 2025. Animal health sales were divided between livestock products at $3,896 million and companion animal products at $2,458 million. Other revenues primarily comprising miscellaneous corporate revenues and third party manufacturing arrangements contributed $515 million in 2025. 

 The company operates through the following segments: Pharmaceutical and Animal Health.

 •  Pharmaceutical: This segment includes human health pharmaceutical and vaccine products. Human health pharmaceutical products consist of therapeutic and preventive agents sold by prescription for the treatment of human disorders. Human health vaccine products consist of preventive pediatric adolescent and adult vaccines. Key franchises in this segment include oncology led by Keytruda immunology vaccines such as Gardasil ProQuad Vaxneuvance hospital acute care products like Bridion and Prevymis cardiometabolic and respiratory treatments including Winrevair Adempas Verquvo and Ohtuvayre virology agents such as Lagevrio Isentress Delstrigo and Pifeltro neuroscience products like Belsomra and diabetes treatments including Januvia and Janumet. In 2025 the pharmaceutical segment generated $58,142 million in sales.

 •  Animal Health: This segment discovers develops manufactures and markets a wide range of veterinary pharmaceutical and vaccine products health management solutions and services and digital identification traceability and monitoring products. It serves livestock and companion animal species with products such as antibiotics vaccines parasiticides fertility management tools and nutrition supplements. In 2025 the animal health segment generated $6,354 million in sales with livestock products accounting for $3,896 million and companion animal products for $2,458 million.

 Merck holds a leading position in the global pharmaceutical industry competing with other large research based companies generic manufacturers and specialized animal health firms. Its competitive advantages arise from a robust research and development pipeline a diversified portfolio of patented products strategic alliances and collaborations and extensive global manufacturing and distribution capabilities. The company invested heavily in R&D with approximately 24,700 employees engaged in research activities as of December 31, 2025 and maintains a broad clinical pipeline spanning oncology cardiovascular metabolic infectious diseases neuroscience immunology ophthalmology respiratory diseases and vaccines. 

 The company’s customers include drug wholesalers and retailers hospitals government agencies managed health care providers such as health maintenance organizations and pharmacy benefit managers physicians veterinarians distributors animal producers farmers and pet owners. Specific customer names are not disclosed in the filing.

PG.profile_html:
The Procter & Gamble Company is a world leading multinational consumer goods company focused on providing trusted branded products of superior quality performance and value to improve the lives of consumers around the world. The company sells its products in about 180 countries and territories worldwide. Its portfolio includes personal care, cleaning, fabric care, and home care products, as well as grooming and health related goods. The firm’s purpose is to deliver superior quality and value while touching the lives of consumers with brands that are trusted across generations.

The company generates revenue by creating, manufacturing, marketing, and distributing a diversified portfolio of daily use products. It invests in research and development and consumer insights to invent new categories and to improve existing products so they meet evolving consumer needs. Marketing efforts rely on advertising, promotions, and endorsements to build brand awareness and loyalty among consumers. Products reach customers through retail stores, electronic commerce platforms, and direct to consumer channels. Continued productivity improvements free resources for further investment in research and development and marketing, while supporting the goal of sustainable balanced top and bottom line growth. The company also devotes resources to sustainability initiatives aimed at reducing its environmental footprint while helping consumers lower their own impact. These efforts include pursuing renewable electricity for operations, decreasing the use of virgin petroleum based plastic in packaging, designing packaging that is recyclable or reusable, sourcing key forest based commodities responsibly, improving water use efficiency, and supporting water restoration projects in important basins.

The Procter & Gamble Company holds a leading position in the consumer goods industry and often ranks among the top players in many product categories worldwide. It competes against a broad range of large and small established and emerging companies including well known global competitors and retailers private label brands. In many markets the company faces competition from both branded rivals and private label offerings yet it frequently maintains a significant market share or leadership role. Its integrated strategy that emphasizes superiority across product, packaging, brand communication, retail execution, and value provides a clear differentiation point. The firm’s scale, strong brand portfolio, and extensive distribution network further reinforce its competitive advantage. The company’s extensive portfolio of trademarks and patents protects its product innovations and supports its branding efforts. These intellectual property assets, combined with a strong global supply chain and deep consumer insights, enable Procter & Gamble to maintain its market leadership.

The company serves mass merchandisers, electronic commerce channels, grocery stores, membership club stores, drug stores, department stores, distributors, wholesalers, specialty beauty stores, high frequency stores, pharmacies, electronics stores, professional channels, and direct to consumer customers. Walmart Inc. and its affiliates represent approximately 16% of the company's total sales. No other single customer accounts for more than 10% of sales. The top ten customers together accounted for 43% of total net sales. The firm also sells directly to consumers through its own electronic commerce sites and brand specific web stores. Sales to Walmart and its affiliates represented approximately 16% of total revenue in both 2024 and 2025 while the top ten customers collectively contributed about 43% of net sales in those years.

UNH.profile_html:
UnitedHealth Group Incorporated is a health care and well-being company that operates through two complementary businesses, Optum and UnitedHealthcare, to provide health services, insurance, and data analytics aimed at improving access, affordability, and outcomes in the health care system.

The company generates revenue by offering health benefit plans, pharmacy benefit management services, clinical care services, and data analytics and technology solutions to employers, health plans, government agencies, and individual consumers.

The company operates through the following segments: Optum Health, Optum Insight, Optum Rx, and UnitedHealthcare.

  • Optum Health: provides patient-centered care, care management, wellness programs, consumer engagement, and health financial services, serving 95,000,000 consumers and working with providers, employers, payers, and public-sector entities through primary, specialty, surgical, chronic and behavioral health, post-acute care, telehealth, and value-based or fee-for-service arrangements.
  • Optum Insight: delivers data, analytics, research, consulting, technology, and managed services to health systems, health plans, state governments, and life sciences companies to improve performance, reduce costs, support evidence-based care, manage revenue cycles, and meet regulatory requirements.
  • Optum Rx: supplies pharmacy care services through a network of 64,000 retail pharmacies, home delivery, specialty and infusion services, managing $188 billion in pharmaceutical sales and offering utilization management, medication management, and clinical programs to health benefits providers, employer plans, unions, trusts, and public-sector entities.
  • UnitedHealthcare: offers a full range of health benefit plans, including employer-sponsored, individual, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Part D, Medicare Supplement, and Medicaid-focused products, serving 29,700,000 people through its Employer & Individual unit, 8,400,000 seniors through Medicare & Retirement, and 7,400,000 low-income individuals through Community & State, with premium revenues from CMS representing 44% of UnitedHealth Group’s total consolidated revenues.

UnitedHealth Group Incorporated ranks among the largest diversified health care companies in the United States, competing with firms such as Anthem, Cigna, Humana, and CVS Health, and maintains a competitive advantage through its integrated data analytics capabilities, extensive provider networks, and scale across insurance and care delivery.

The company serves a broad customer base that includes the U. S. Department of Health and Human Services, the Veterans Affairs Department, the Department of Defense, numerous state Medicaid programs, large national employers, health plans, and individual consumers.

HSBC.profile_html:
HSBC Holdings plc is a global banking and financial services organisation that provides a comprehensive range of products and services to personal, commercial, institutional and private banking customers worldwide. The company operates as an integrated universal bank offering retail and commercial banking, wealth management, global banking and markets, and international wealth and premier banking solutions. It leverages its international network spanning 56 countries and territories to support customers in managing complex financial needs across borders.

HSBC generates revenue primarily through net interest income, fee and other income, and trading activities across its core businesses. Revenue is derived from retail and commercial lending, deposit services, wealth management products, investment distribution, insurance, global transaction banking, capital markets, and securities services. The company serves a diverse customer base including individuals, small and medium-sized enterprises, large corporations, financial institutions, governments, and high-net-worth individuals seeking traditional banking, investment, insurance, and trade finance solutions.

The company operates through the following segments: Hong Kong, UK, Corporate and Institutional Banking, and International Wealth and Premier Banking.

  • Hong Kong: This segment comprises Retail Banking and Wealth and Commercial Banking operations of HSBC Hong Kong and Hang Seng Bank. It serves personal and commercial customers in Hong Kong with products including current and savings accounts, mortgages, personal loans, credit cards, wealth management, insurance, and trade finance. The segment maintained its leading market position in Hong Kong with a deposit market share of 25.4% and a trade finance market share of 32.6% in 2025.
  • UK: This segment includes UK Retail Banking and Wealth (including first direct and M&S Bank) and UK Commercial Banking, including HSBC Innovation Bank. It provides personal banking, business banking, wealth management, and commercial lending products to customers across the United Kingdom. The segment offers services such as mortgage lending, current accounts, business loans, wealth management solutions, and digital banking propositions including Funds on Mobile for wealth customers.
  • Corporate and Institutional Banking: This segment integrates Commercial Banking (outside the UK and Hong Kong) with Global Banking and Markets to deliver cross-border transaction banking and capital markets solutions. It provides services including global trade finance, cash management, foreign exchange, securities services, debt and equity capital markets, and wholesale credit and lending. The segment offers innovative products such as tokenised deposit services enabling real-time settlement for corporate clients in Hong Kong, Singapore, the UK, and Luxembourg.
  • International Wealth and Premier Banking: This segment comprises Premier banking outside Hong Kong and the UK, Private Banking, Asset Management, and Insurance businesses. It delivers wealth management, investment, private banking, asset management, and insurance solutions to affluent and high-net-worth customers globally. The segment operates under brands including Premier 3.0, HSBC Private Bank, HSBC Asset Management, and HSBC Insurance, with a focus on growing wealth balances in Asia and the Middle East where it manages over $1.2tn in wealth assets as of 31 December 2025.

HSBC holds a leading position in the global banking industry as one of the world’s largest banking and financial services organisations by assets and market capitalisation. The company competes with other global universal banks such as JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and BNP Paribas, differentiating itself through its extensive international network, particularly its strong presence in Asia and its historical roots in facilitating trade between Europe and Asia. Its competitive advantages include its scale, global connectivity, strong deposit base, and leading market positions in key home markets such as Hong Kong and the UK.

The company serves a broad customer base ranging from individual retail customers and small businesses to large corporations, multinational institutions, and high-net-worth individuals. Specific customer groups include personal banking clients, small and medium-sized enterprises supported through initiatives like fee-free banking, corporate clients accessing trade finance and capital markets services, institutional investors utilizing asset management and securities services, and wealth management clients across its International Wealth and Premier Banking and Hong Kong businesses. HSBC also supports approximately half of the Fortune Global 500 companies through its corporate and institutional banking relationships.

GE.name: General Electric Co
GE.sicdescription: Electronic & Other Electrical Equipment (No Computer Equip)
GE.profile_html:
General Electric Company operates as GE Aerospace and is a global aerospace leader specializing in the design, development, manufacturing, and servicing of jet engines and propulsion systems for commercial, military, and business aviation applications. The company maintains an installed base of approximately 50,000 commercial and 30,000 military engines, supporting a robust aftermarket services business that accounts for roughly 70% of its revenue. GE Aerospace serves customers in approximately 120 countries through manufacturing and service operations at 70 facilities in the United States and Puerto Rico and 62 facilities across 23 other countries.

GE Aerospace generates revenue primarily through the sale of commercial and defense engines, spare parts, and maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services offered under long-term service agreements, spare parts agreements, and time-and-material contracts. The company’s revenue is heavily weighted toward aftermarket services, which represent approximately 70% of total revenue, driven by demand from airlines, airframers, third-party MRO shops, and government agencies. Equipment sales, including new engine deliveries, contribute the remainder of revenue, supported by a global installed base requiring ongoing service and upgrades.

GE Aerospace operates through the following segments: Commercial Engines & Services and Defense & Propulsion Technologies.

  • Commercial Engines & Services: This segment designs, develops, manufactures, and services jet engines for commercial airframes, business aviation, and aeroderivative applications, including maintenance, repair, and overhaul of engines and sale of spare parts under various contractual arrangements. It powers aircraft across all commercial categories—narrowbody, widebody, and regional—through engines such as the LEAP, CFM56, CF6, GE90, GEnx, and GE9X, with the LEAP engine in significant production ramp and the GE9X slated to power the Boeing 777X. The segment benefits from its 50-50 joint venture CFM International with Safran Aircraft Engines, a key producer of the LEAP and CFM56 engines widely used in the narrowbody market.
  • Defense & Propulsion Technologies: This segment consists of Defense & Systems and Propulsion & Additive Technologies businesses, providing defense engines, avionics, power systems, and aircraft components for military and commercial customers. It includes brands such as Avio Aero, Unison, Dowty Propellers, and Colibrium Additive, which design and manufacture components like small turboprop engines, aeroengine mechanical transmissions, turbines, combustors, controls, additive manufacturing systems, propeller systems, ignition systems, sensors, and engine accessories. Avio Aero is a strategic partner in Europe, supporting defense initiatives for the Italian Ministry of Defence and contributing to programs such as the Eurofighter EJ200 engine and the Global Combat Air Programme.

GE Aerospace holds a leading position in the global aerospace propulsion industry, competing with other major engine manufacturers such as Rolls-Royce and Pratt & Whitney in commercial engines, while facing competition in defense contracts from U. S. and international contractors. Its competitive advantages stem from its large installed base, proprietary FLIGHT DECK operating model emphasizing safety, quality, delivery, and cost, and sustained investment in advanced technologies like ceramic matrix composites, additive manufacturing, and the RISE program’s Open Fan and hybrid electric systems. The company’s long-standing relationships with airframers like Boeing and Airbus, along with sole-source positions on certain aircraft models, reinforce its market strength.

GE Aerospace serves a diverse customer base including major airlines such as Qatar Airways, Emirates, ANA Holdings, Malaysia Aviation Group, Korean Air, Cathay Pacific, and Pegasus, as well as airframers Boeing and Airbus. Additional customers include third-party MRO shops, government agencies, militaries, and international partners such as Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL), which procured F404-GE-IN20 engines. The company also works with the U. S. Department of Defense and allied nations on programs involving combat engines, hypersonics, and unmanned aircraft systems.
