SAP.profile_html:
SAP SE is a global enterprise software company headquartered in Walldorf Germany. The company develops and markets a suite of integrated applications that cover finance procurement human resources supply chain customer experience and other core business functions. Its offerings are delivered through cloud subscriptions software licenses and related services. SAP SE serves organizations of all sizes across many industries worldwide.

SAP SE generates revenue primarily from fees for cloud based subscriptions to its software solutions. Additional revenue comes from software license sales maintenance and support contracts consulting implementation services and training. The company also earns income from its business technology platform and from transaction based services such as those provided through its spend management and business network offerings.

SAP SE holds a leading position in the global enterprise software market competing with firms such as Oracle Microsoft IBM and Salesforce. Its competitive advantages include a broad and deeply integrated product portfolio a strong focus on cloud transformation and artificial intelligence and a large installed base of customers that creates high switching costs. The company’s emphasis on industry specific solutions and its extensive partner ecosystem further strengthen its market stance.

SAP SE serves a diverse customer base that includes large multinational corporations mid sized enterprises and public sector organizations across sectors such as manufacturing retail healthcare finance and technology. The company has formed partnerships with firms like Accenture Perplexity Palantir Alibaba Group ADP OpenAI Amazon Web Services Google Cloud Snowflake and Mistral AI to extend its reach and enhance its offerings. These collaborations help SAP SE deliver solutions to customers in various regions and industries.

BRK.B.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc
BRK.B.profile_html:
Berkshire Hathaway Inc engages in a diverse range of business activities through its subsidiaries. The company operates primarily in insurance, rail transportation, energy, manufacturing, services, and retail. Its decentralized structure allows each business to operate independently while benefiting from strong capital allocation.

Revenue is generated from insurance premiums and investment returns, railroad freight charges, energy sales and services, manufactured goods, and retail product sales. Insurance underwriting collects premiums from policyholders and invests the float to earn interest and dividend income. BNSF earns revenue by transporting goods across its rail network, while BHE sells electricity and natural gas to utility and commercial customers.

The company operates through the following segments: Insurance underwriting, Insurance investment income, BNSF, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, Manufacturing, service and retailing, Investment gains and losses, and Other.

  • Insurance underwriting: This segment writes property and casualty, life and health insurance policies through GEICO, BH Primary, and BHRG, collecting premiums and managing claim liabilities.
  • Insurance investment income: This segment invests the insurance float in cash, equity securities, and fixed income instruments to generate interest and dividend revenue.
  • BNSF: This segment operates one of the largest North American railroads, hauling freight such as consumer products, agricultural goods, industrial items, and coal.
  • Berkshire Hathaway Energy: This segment includes regulated electric utilities, natural gas pipelines, renewable energy projects, and a real estate brokerage business, providing power and gas services to customers.
  • Manufacturing, service and retailing: This segment comprises industrial manufacturers, building and consumer product makers, service providers such as TTI and aviation businesses, and retail operators including auto dealerships and home furnishing stores.
  • Investment gains and losses: This segment reflects unrealized and realized changes in the market value of Berkshire’s equity securities portfolio, affecting earnings through price fluctuations.
  • Other: This segment includes investment income not allocated to operating units, foreign exchange gains or losses on debt, equity method earnings from holdings such as Kraft Heinz and Occidental, and acquisition related accounting charges.

Berkshire Hathaway Inc holds a leading position in several industries; GEICO is among the largest private passenger auto insurers in the United States, BNSF ranks as one of the top Class I railroads, and BHE is a major regulated utility operator. Competitive advantages stem from its strong cash flow, disciplined capital allocation, and a decentralized management model that empowers subsidiary leaders.

Berkshire serves a broad customer base that includes individual policyholders seeking auto and property insurance, shippers of agricultural and industrial goods utilizing rail freight, residential and commercial consumers of electricity and natural gas, manufacturers and retailers purchasing its manufactured products, and shoppers visiting its retail stores and service centers.

APH.name: Amphenol Corp /De/
APH.profile_html:
Amphenol Corporation is one of the world's largest designers, manufacturers and marketers of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors and interconnect systems, antennas, sensors and sensor-based products and coaxial, high-speed, fiber optic and specialty cable.

The company generates revenue through the sale of its diverse portfolio of connectivity and sensor solutions across multiple industries. Its products include connector and interconnect systems, cable assemblies, antennas, sensors, and related value-added products. Amphenol serves a broad customer base requiring reliable performance in demanding applications.

The company operates through the following segments: Communications Solutions, Harsh Environment Solutions and Interconnect and Sensor Systems.

  • Communications Solutions: This segment designs, manufactures and markets a broad range of connector and interconnect systems including high speed, radio frequency, power, fiber optic and other interconnect products; coaxial, fiber optic, power and high-speed cable; antennas; and other products. Key products include fiber optic interconnect products, high-speed interconnect products, radio frequency interconnect products, cable assemblies and harnesses, consumer device antennas, network infrastructure antennas, coaxial, fiber optic, power and specialty cable, hinges and other mechanical products, and production-related products. This segment serves end markets such as automotive, commercial aerospace, communications networks, defense, industrial, information technology and data communications, and mobile devices.
  • Harsh Environment Solutions: This segment designs, manufactures and markets a broad range of ruggedized interconnect products including connectors and interconnect systems, specialty cable, printed circuits and printed circuit assemblies and other products. Key products include harsh environment data, power, fiber optic and radio frequency interconnect products, backplane interconnect systems, cable assemblies and harnesses, cable management products, coaxial and specialty cable, and flexible and rigid printed circuit boards. This segment serves end markets such as automotive, commercial aerospace, communications networks, defense, industrial, and information technology and data communications.
  • Interconnect and Sensor Systems: This segment designs, manufactures and markets a broad range of sensors, sensor-based systems, connectors and value-add interconnect systems. Key products include busbars and power distribution systems, power interconnect products, backplane interconnect systems, cable assemblies and harnesses, and sensors for force, gas and moisture, level, position, pressure, temperature, and vibration. This segment serves end markets such as automotive, commercial aerospace, communications networks, defense, industrial, information technology and data communications.

Amphenol Corporation holds a leading position in the global interconnect industry, competing with other major manufacturers through its broad product portfolio, global scale, and focus on innovation and quality. The company benefits from diversified end-market exposure and strong relationships with customers across multiple sectors.

The company serves a diverse customer base including original equipment manufacturers and contract manufacturers in the automotive, commercial aerospace, communications networks, defense, industrial, information technology, data communications, and mobile device industries.

This segment serves end markets such as automotive, commercial aerospace, communications networks, defense, industrial, information technology and data communications, and mobile devices.

Key products include harsh environment data, power, fiber optic and radio frequency interconnect products, backplane interconnect systems, cable assemblies and harnesses, cable management products, coaxial and specialty cable, and flexible and rigid printed circuit boards. This segment serves end markets such as automotive, commercial aerospace, communications networks, defense, industrial, and information technology and data communications.

Amphenol Corporation holds a leading position in the global interconnect industry, competing with other major manufacturers through its broad product portfolio, global scale, and focus on innovation and quality. TM.profile_html:
Toyota Motor Corporation designs manufactures and sells automobiles and provides financial services worldwide. The company operates in the automotive industry and also engages in financing and other activities such as information technology services. It produces passenger cars minivans trucks buses and related parts and accessories. Toyota Motor Corporation also offers loan and lease products to support vehicle purchases.

Revenue is generated primarily from the sale of vehicles and parts through its automotive operations. The financial services segment earns income from loan and lease contracts extended to dealers and retail customers. The all other operations segment contributes revenue from information technology platforms and related services. In fiscal 2025 Toyota Motor Corporation reported total sales revenues of approximately 48 trillion yen with automotive operations accounting for the largest share.

Toyota Motor Corporation operates through the following segments: automotive operations, financial services operations, and all other operations.

  • Automotive operations include the design manufacture assembly and sale of passenger vehicles minivans and commercial vehicles such as trucks and related parts and accessories. The segment also develops connected vehicles and mobility services to create new value from data.
  • Financial services operations provide financing to dealers and their customers for the purchase or lease of Toyota vehicles. The segment offers retail installment credit leasing and wholesale financing to support inventory needs.
  • All other operations encompass information technology related businesses such as the GAZOO.com web portal and other digital services that support the companys core activities.

Toyota Motor Corporation holds a leading position in the global automotive industry with strong market shares in Japan North America Europe and Asia. The company faces competition from Volkswagen General Motors Hyundai and other major automakers. Its competitive advantages stem from the Toyota Production System which emphasizes efficiency quality and continuous improvement. Additionally Toyota's early investment in hybrid technology and its extensive global dealer network provide durability and brand loyalty.

Toyota Motor Corporation serves a diverse customer base that includes individual consumers purchasing vehicles for personal use and commercial fleets requiring trucks buses and other commercial vehicles. The company also works with thousands of independent dealers who sell its products and provide after sales service. Its financial services division extends credit to both retail buyers and corporate clients needing financing for vehicle acquisitions.

IBM.profile_html:
International Business Machines Corporation provides hybrid cloud and artificial intelligence solutions to help clients transform their operations. The company draws on its software consulting and infrastructure capabilities to deliver technology services worldwide.

IBM earns revenue by selling software subscriptions, cloud and infrastructure hardware, consulting services and financing arrangements to businesses across industries.

The company operates through the following segments: Software, Consulting, Infrastructure, and Financing.

  • The Software segment develops and sells hybrid cloud platforms, artificial intelligence tools, data management solutions and application software that enable clients to modernize workloads and drive digital transformation. It also offers security and automation features that are integrated into its software products.
  • The Consulting segment provides strategy, experience design, technology implementation and operations services to help clients redesign processes and adopt new technologies. It draws on industry expertise and IBM’s technology portfolio to deliver end to end solutions that meet business goals.
  • The Infrastructure segment supplies on premises servers, storage systems and related hardware for private and public cloud environments. It also offers life cycle services that support deployment, maintenance and optimization of infrastructure assets.
  • The Financing segment provides loans and leasing options that enable clients to acquire IBM hardware, software and services. It manages credit risk and residual value to generate returns while supporting customer purchasing power.

International Business Machines Corporation holds a leading or top tier position in each of its business segments. In the Software segment it competes with Alphabet, Amazon, BMC, Broadcom, Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP and Splunk. The Consulting segment faces competition from Accenture, Capgemini, India based service providers, management consulting firms, public accounting practices, engineering service providers and niche specialists. Infrastructure competitors include Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Intel, NetApp, Pure Storage and original device manufacturers as well as cloud service providers. Financing rivals are non captive financing entities and traditional financial institutions. IBM’s competitive advantages stem from technology innovation, product performance, pricing, quality, brand strength, breadth of offerings, skilled talent, deep client relationships and the ability to deliver measurable business value.

IBM serves a diverse set of clients that includes large enterprises, mid size companies, government agencies and educational institutions across many industries. These customers rely on the company’s hybrid cloud, artificial intelligence and infrastructure solutions to improve efficiency and drive innovation.

AXP.profile_html:
American Express is a global payments and premium lifestyle brand powered by technology. Headquartered in New York the company leverages its long standing history and global scale to deliver payments and lifestyle solutions. It operates card issuing merchant acquiring and card network businesses that serve consumers small businesses midsize companies and large corporations worldwide. The company offers credit and charge cards banking products merchant services and network solutions. Its integrated platform connects card members merchants and partners to provide a seamless commerce experience.

Revenue is generated primarily from fees associated with its card issuing business including discount revenue annual fees late fees and interest earned on cardholder balances. Banking products such as deposit accounts and loans contribute interest income and fee revenue. Merchant acquiring activities provide discount revenue from transaction processing while the global network supplies fees for processing and settling payments. Additional income comes from licensing arrangements with partners from premium travel lifestyle and expense management services and from loyalty programs such as Membership Rewards. The company also earns revenue from fees charged for foreign currency conversions and from fees associated with premium benefits such as airport lounge access.

The company operates through the following reportable operating segments: U. S. Consumer Services Commercial Services International Card Services and Global Merchant and Network Services.

  • U. S. Consumer Services: Provides credit and charge cards to consumers and small businesses in the United States offers rewards programs such as Membership Rewards and cash back provides banking products including high yield savings checking accounts and consumer loans and delivers travel dining and lifestyle benefits through partnerships with airlines hotels and restaurants.
  • Commercial Services: Offers card products and payment solutions to midsize and large corporations provides banking services such as business checking accounts and lines of credit supplies non card B2B payment and expense management tools and includes the 2025 acquisition of Center for expense management software. The segment also supports corporate travel and procurement solutions through partnerships with travel management firms.
  • International Card Services: Delivers credit and charge card products to consumers and businesses outside the United States offers localized rewards and benefits provides banking and financing options tailored to international markets and supports card linked travel and lifestyle services globally. The segment works with local banks and partners to issue cards under cobrand arrangements in regions such as Europe Asia and Latin America.
  • Global Merchant and Network Services: Builds and maintains relationships with merchants worldwide to accept American Express cards manages discount rates and settlement through the OptBlue program supplies fraud prevention tools marketing analytics and data services to merchants and operates the global payment network that processes and settles transactions with third party issuers and partners. The segment also provides value added services such as point of sale marketing and digital commerce solutions to help merchants grow sales.

American Express holds the fourth largest position among global general purpose card networks by purchase volume trailing Visa China UnionPay and Mastercard. The company differentiates itself through a closed loop integrated payments platform that connects card members and merchants directly enabling rich data analytics and personalized rewards. Its brand reputation for trust security and service combined with the premium spending characteristics of its customers gives it a competitive edge against rivals that rely on open loop models. The firm also benefits from a diversified revenue mix that reduces reliance on any single income stream and from a long history of innovation in payments technology.

The company serves a diverse set of customers including individual consumers small businesses midsize firms and large corporations across the United States United Kingdom European Union Australia Japan Canada Mexico and other regions. Cardholders tend to exhibit higher average spending and stronger credit profiles than users of competing cards. Specific partners cited in the filing include Delta Air Lines Marriott International British Airways Hilton Worldwide Holdings Coinbase Credit Saison Emburse SAP Concur and Fine Hotels and Resorts. In addition the firm works with numerous other merchants financial institutions technology providers and airline alliances to expand its network and enhance the value delivered to card members and merchants.

CRM.profile_html:
Salesforce, Inc. is a global leader in customer relationship management technology. The company offers an AI powered Agentforce 360 Platform that brings together sales, service, marketing, commerce, data management, integration, analytics and collaboration tools in a single cloud based environment. This platform enables organizations to unify customer data from disparate systems and to deploy autonomous AI agents that work alongside employees. By providing a trusted foundation for data and AI, Salesforce helps businesses create personalized experiences, automate routine tasks and improve decision making across every customer touchpoint. Founded in 1999, the company has grown to serve millions of users and to process billions of transactions each day through its scalable multi tenant infrastructure.

Salesforce generates the majority of its revenue from subscription fees for its cloud based software and platform services. Customers pay recurring charges for access to the company’s sales cloud, service cloud, marketing cloud, commerce cloud and platform products such as Data 360, MuleSoft integration tools and Tableau analytics. In addition, the company earns revenue from professional services that include implementation, consulting and training offerings. These services help customers deploy, customize and optimize Salesforce solutions. Sales are conducted primarily through a direct sales force that operates in regional hubs and through a global network of channel partners, which include system integrators, independent software vendors and consulting firms. The company also maintains an online marketplace called AppExchange where third party developers sell applications that extend the functionality of the Salesforce platform. Revenue is recognized ratably over the subscription term, providing a predictable and recurring income stream.

Salesforce holds a leading position in the global customer relationship management market, often cited as the largest pure play CRM vendor by revenue. The company competes with traditional enterprise software providers such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP Customer Experience and Oracle CX as well as with newer entrants that focus exclusively on artificial intelligence and automation. Its competitive advantage lies in the depth and breadth of its integrated platform, which combines a unified data model, AI driven automation and a rich set of industry specific solutions. The multi tenant architecture allows rapid scaling and low cost of ownership for customers. Furthermore, the extensive ecosystem of third party applications on AppExchange and the large community of developers known as Trailblazers create strong network effects that increase switching costs and reinforce brand loyalty. Continuous investment in research and development, particularly in generative AI and agentic technologies, keeps the platform at the forefront of innovation.

Salesforce serves a diverse customer base that includes businesses of all sizes and across nearly every industry vertical. Small and medium sized enterprises use the company’s Essentials and Starter suites to manage sales, service and marketing operations, while large enterprises deploy multiple clouds to support complex global processes. Industries represented in the customer base include financial services, health care, life sciences, manufacturing, retail, automotive, technology, telecommunications and government agencies. The company reports that no single customer accounted for more than ten percent of its revenue in the most recent fiscal years, indicating a well diversified revenue base. Additionally, Salesforce sells to both business to business and business to customer organizations, as well as to internal employees through employee experience solutions.

TD.profile_html:
Toronto Dominion Bank is a leading financial institution that provides a broad range of banking, wealth management, insurance and capital markets services. It is the 6th largest bank in North America by assets, with $2.1 trillion in assets as of October 31, 2025. The bank serves over 28.1 million clients across Canada the United States and internationally through its 4 core businesses. It employed an average of 102,218 full time equivalent staff in fiscal 2025. TD also ranks among North America's leading digital banks, with more than 13 million mobile active users in Canada and the United States.

The bank generates revenue primarily from interest income on loans and deposits, fee income from wealth management and advisory services, insurance underwriting premiums, and trading and advisory revenue from its wholesale banking operations. Additional income comes from service charges, credit card fees and foreign exchange activities. Interest income from loans and deposits forms the core of its earnings, while fee based revenue from wealth management, insurance underwriting and capital markets activities provides diversification.

The company operates through the following segments:

  • Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking: Provides personal banking through TD Canada Trust including chequing and savings accounts, mortgages, personal loans and credit cards, and offers commercial banking services such as business loans, lines of credit, equipment financing and commercial mortgages, alongside TD Auto Finance Canada which specializes in automotive lending and leasing across Canada.
  • U. S. Retail: Delivers retail banking services via TD Bank and its America's Most Convenient Bank® brand, offering checking and savings accounts, mortgages, personal loans, credit cards and small business financing, while TD Auto Finance U. S. provides automotive loans and leasing and TD Wealth (U. S.) delivers investment advice and retirement planning to clients in the United States.
  • Wealth Management and Insurance: Offers wealth advisory and private client services through TD Wealth (Canada), provides self directed investing platforms via TD Direct Investing, and underwrites property, casualty, life and health insurance products through TD Insurance to serve individual and institutional customers across North America.
  • Wholesale Banking: Supplies corporate and investment banking services including debt and equity underwriting, merger and acquisition advisory, and restructuring through TD Securities, while TD Cowen offers securities trading, research and brokerage capabilities to institutional investors globally.

Toronto Dominion Bank holds a strong position among North American lenders, ranking behind only the largest U. S. banks and a few Canadian peers in total assets. It competes with institutions such as Royal Bank of Canada, Bank of Montreal, JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America while differentiating itself through a diversified revenue stream, extensive digital capabilities with over 13 million mobile active users and a well recognized brand.

The bank's customer base consists of individual consumers, small and medium sized enterprises, large corporations, institutional investors and insurance policyholders. It serves more than 28.1 million clients who rely on its retail, wealth, insurance and wholesale banking solutions. It also serves high net worth individuals seeking wealth management solutions and corporate clients requiring treasury, risk management and international trade finance services.

SAN.profile_html:
Banco Santander, S. A. is a banking institution that provides financial services to a variety of clients. The filing describes the company's history and development, covering acquisitions dispositions reorganizations capital increases and recent events. It also outlines the organizational structure through Appendices I II and III and Note 1 a) to the consolidated financial statements. The company's property plants and equipment are detailed in Note 16 of the same statements. Banco Santander, S. A. operates primarily in Spain as indicated by the discussion of competition in the country. The business overview section provides insight into its economic and financial performance. Taken together these disclosures show that the firm is engaged in traditional banking activities such as taking deposits extending credit and offering ancillary services. The capital increases discussed in Note 31 are intended to bolster the company's capital adequacy and support its strategic initiatives.

The company generates revenue from its core banking operations. The filing references several notes to the consolidated financial statements that illustrate the sources of income. Note 6 Note 10 Note 20 and Note 21 break down interest income fee and commission income and other operating revenue. Capital increases disclosed in Note 31 affect the funding base and can influence the capacity to earn interest. Recent events described in Note 1 g) may also impact revenue streams through changes in business scope or market conditions. Overall the revenue model relies on the spread between lending and deposit rates as well as on fees for payment processing asset management and advisory services. Note 6 specifically details interest income while Note 10 provides a breakdown of fee and commission income from various banking services.

Banco Santander, S. A. operates in a competitive banking environment in Spain. The filing includes a dedicated section on competition in Spain that outlines the competitive landscape and the pressures faced by domestic banks. Supervision and regulation are addressed in another section indicating that the firm is subject to oversight by national and European authorities. This regulatory framework influences capital requirements risk management practices and product offerings. Selected statistical information provided in the filing allows investors to gauge the bank's market share and performance relative to peers. The combination of competition and regulation shapes the bank's strategic priorities and its ability to maintain profitability. The competition section also references the presence of both large national banks and smaller regional players that vie for market share.

The company serves a diverse customer base that includes retail clients small and medium sized enterprises large corporations and institutional investors. While the filing does not disclose specific customer names it references the branch network and the property plants and equipment note which implies a presence across various locations to serve local communities. The loan and deposit portfolios described in the financial statements notes reflect exposure to both personal and commercial banking. The range of services offered suggests that the bank caters to individuals seeking savings and mortgage products as well as businesses needing working capital trade finance and corporate lending. In sum the client base is broad and varied reflecting the universal nature of its banking operations. The bank's extensive branch network highlighted in the property plants and equipment note enables it to reach a wide audience across different geographic areas within Spain.

VZ.profile_html:
Verizon Communications Inc is a holding company that provides communications, technology, information and streaming products and services to consumers, businesses and government entities worldwide. The company operates one of the most extensive wireless networks in the United States and maintains a growing fiber optic footprint that reaches 31 U. S. states and Washington D. C. In addition to connectivity, Verizon offers devices, video services, cloud storage and security solutions designed to meet diverse customer needs.

Verizon generates revenue primarily from wireless and wireline communications services, broadband, video, equipment sales and related offerings. In 2025 the Consumer segment contributed $106.8 billion, representing about 77% of total revenue, while the Business segment contributed $29.1 billion, or roughly 21% of revenue. Consumer revenue stems from retail wireless plans, device payment programs, Fios internet and video, fixed wireless access and ancillary services such as device protection and content subscriptions. Business revenue is derived from mobility services, Internet of Things connectivity, corporate networking, security, managed network services and wholesale provision of capacity to other carriers. Together these streams serve a broad base of individual consumers, enterprises, public sector organizations and wholesale customers.

The company operates through the following segments: Verizon Consumer Group and Verizon Business Group.

  • Verizon Consumer Group provides consumer focused wireless and wireline services, including access to one of the nation’s largest 4G LTE and 5G networks, fiber optic broadband through the Fios product line, copper based DSL, fixed wireless access via 5G/4G LTE, and Fios video offerings, while also selling smartphones, tablets and wearables on device payment plans, offering device protection, cloud storage and content subscriptions, and selling wholesale network access to mobile virtual network operators that resell service under their own brands.
  • Verizon Business Group supplies wireless and wireline solutions to businesses, public sector entities and other carriers, featuring mobility plans, fixed wireless access, broadband connectivity, Internet of Things platforms, advanced communication services, corporate networking, local and long distance voice, security suites and managed network offerings, while also delivering wholesale capacity to telecommunications carriers and providing specialized services for enterprise, small medium business and government customers.

Verizon is regarded as one of the leading telecommunications providers in the United States, competing chiefly with AT&T Inc. and T Mobile US, Inc. in the wireless market. The company’s competitive advantages stem from its extensive wireless network covering roughly 147 million retail connections, its substantial holdings of low, mid and high band spectrum including C Band and millimeter wave, and its expanding fiber optic infrastructure that now reaches 31 states and the District of Columbia. Additionally, Verizon’s brand reputation, integrated product bundles and investments in network virtualization and open radio access network technologies help differentiate it from rivals.

Verizon serves a diverse customer base that includes individual consumers, small and medium sized businesses, large enterprises and government agencies. Consumer customers purchase wireless plans, home internet, video and related services, while business clients acquire mobility, IoT, networking and security solutions tailored to their operations. Government entities, ranging from federal departments to state and local authorities and educational institutions, rely on Verizon for secure communications, broadband and managed services. Wholesale customers, primarily other telecommunications carriers, buy network capacity to provide services to their own end users.

DE.profile_html:
Deere & Company manufactures agricultural, construction, and forestry equipment while providing financial services to support its equipment sales. The company operates globally with a focus on integrating advanced technology into its machinery to improve customer productivity and sustainability.

Deere & Company generates revenue through the sale of equipment and related parts and services across its three equipment segments, as well as through financing and interest income from its Financial Services segment. The company sells products to farmers, contractors, and landowners, and provides loans, leases, and warranty contracts to dealers and end-users.

The company operates through the following segments: Production & Precision Agriculture, Small Agriculture & Turf, Construction & Forestry, and Financial Services.

  • Production & Precision Agriculture focuses on large-scale farming equipment including four-wheel-drive and track tractors, harvesters for corn soy cotton and sugarcane, tillage seeding and application equipment, and related precision technology solutions.
  • Small Agriculture & Turf provides specialty utility and compact tractors, hay and forage equipment, self-propelled forage harvesters, turf and utility equipment such as riding lawn mowers commercial mowing equipment golf course equipment utility vehicles and implements for residential commercial golf and sports turf care.
  • Construction & Forestry manufactures excavators motor graders crawler dozers and loaders skid steers compact excavators compact wheel loaders backhoes articulated dump trucks milling machines recyclers slipform pavers surface miners asphalt pavers compactors rollers mobile crushers and screens skidders feller bunchers forwarders harvesters and precision forestry technology solutions.
  • Financial Services provides retail notes revolving charge accounts wholesale receivables leases and extended warranties to support equipment sales in the United States Canada and internationally through company-owned subsidiaries and joint ventures with local financial institutions.

Deere & Company holds a strong competitive position in the global agricultural equipment industry, facing rivals such as AGCO Corporation, CLAAS KGaA mbH, CNH Industrial N. V., Kubota Tractor Corporation, and The Toro Company, while maintaining advantages through brand recognition, integrated technology solutions, and a extensive dealer network. In construction and forestry, it competes with Caterpillar Inc., CNH Industrial N. V., Doosan Infracore Co., Ltd., Fayat Group, GOMACO Corporation, Hitachi Construction Machinery, Komatsu Ltd., Kubota Tractor Corporation, LGMG, Liugong, Ponsse Plc, SANY Group Co., Ltd., SDLG, Terex, Tigercat Industries Inc., Volvo Construction Equipment, and XCMG.

The company serves production-scale growers of corn soy cotton and sugarcane, dairy and livestock producers, high-value crop and small acreage farmers, turf and utility customers including golf course maintenance providers, landscapers, and residential and commercial property owners, as well as contractors in earthmoving forestry roadbuilding and material handling industries across North America, Europe, Latin America, Africa, Asia, and Australia.

DIS.profile_html:
The Walt Disney Company is a diversified worldwide entertainment company. It creates and distributes film television and streaming content operates sports networks and manages theme parks resorts and consumer products. The company serves audiences across the globe through its three core businesses.

The company generates revenue from subscription fees for its streaming services advertising sales affiliate fees from cable and satellite providers theatrical distribution of films licensing of content to television and video on demand platforms home entertainment sales music distribution stage play performances post production services merchandise licensing theme park admissions resort room nights cruise line fares vacation club sales and retail of branded merchandise. It also earns royalties from licensing its intellectual property to third parties.

The company operates through the following segments: Entertainment Sports Experiences.

  • Entertainment encompasses the company's non sports focused global film and episodic content production and distribution activities. It includes linear television networks such as ABC Disney Freeform FX and National Geographic channels direct to consumer services like Disney+ and Hulu and content sales licensing covering theatrical distribution TV video on demand home entertainment music distribution stage plays and post production services. The segment also earns revenue from intersegment allocation of consumer products merchandise royalties.
  • The Sports segment focuses on sports focused global television and streaming content production and distribution. It includes ESPN branded television channels domestic and international ESPN direct to consumer services such as ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited and sports programming aired on ABC. The segment derives revenue from affiliate and subscription fees advertising and fees from pay per view events sub licensing of sports rights and branding licensing.
  • The Experiences segment operates theme parks resorts cruise line vacation club and consumer products businesses. It includes Walt Disney World Resort Disneyland Resort Disneyland Paris Hong Kong Disneyland Resort Shanghai Disney Resort and Tokyo Disney Resort through licensing agreements. The segment also manages Disney Cruise Line Disney Vacation Club Adventures by Disney and National Geographic Expeditions and licenses characters and franchises for merchandise retail and publishing.

The Walt Disney Company holds a leading position in the global entertainment industry. It competes with other television networks cable and satellite providers streaming platforms social media and video game companies for viewers attention. In the theme park and resort sector it faces competition from other major operators lodging providers and recreational activity companies. Competitive advantages stem from its extensive library of film and television content strong brand recognition diversified revenue streams and ability to leverage intellectual property across its businesses.

The company serves a broad range of customers including multichannel video programming distributors such as Apple Amazon Walmart Comcast and DirecTV advertising agencies that purchase airtime on its networks and streaming platforms subscribers to its direct to consumer services like Disney+ Hulu and ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited theme park guests cruise ship passengers vacation club members and retail consumers who buy branded merchandise. It also licenses its characters and franchises to manufacturers game developers publishers and retailers worldwide.

SCCO.name: Southern Copper Corp/
SCCO.address_business: 7310 North 16Th St., Suite 135, Phoenix, 85020 Arizona, US
SCCO.address_mailing: 7310 North 16Th St., Suite 135, Phoenix, 85020 Arizona, US
SCCO.profile_html:
Southern Copper Corporation is an integrated producer of copper, molybdenum, zinc and silver, conducting mining, smelting and refining activities primarily in Peru and Mexico. The company extracts ore, processes it into concentrates, smelts the concentrates and refines the metal to produce copper cathodes and other metal products. Its operations encompass open‑pit and underground mines, smelters, refineries and associated infrastructure.

Revenue is generated from the sale of copper cathodes, copper rod, molybdenum concentrate, zinc concentrate, silver and gold. The company sells the majority of its output under long‑term contracts to end‑user customers, with pricing tied to prevailing commodity prices on exchanges such as COMEX and LME. By‑products such as sulfuric acid are also produced and contribute to overall sales.

The company operates through the following segments: Peruvian operations, Mexican open‑pit operations, and Mexican underground mining operations.

  • Peruvian operations: This segment includes the Toquepala and Cuajone open‑pit mines, the Ilo smelter and refinery, a precious metals plant, an industrial railroad and port facilities. It produces copper cathodes, molybdenum concentrate, silver and other materials from ore mined in the Andes.
  • Mexican open‑pit operations: This segment comprises the La Caridad and Buenavista mine complexes, associated concentrators, SX‑EW plants, a smelter, refinery, copper rod plant and precious metals facility. It yields copper, zinc, molybdenum concentrate, silver and gold from surface mines in Sonora.
  • Mexican underground mining operations: Represented by the IMMSA unit, this segment consists of five underground mines that extract zinc, lead, copper, silver and gold, together with a zinc refinery. It supplies zinc metal and related by‑products from deep‑level workings.

Southern Copper Corporation ranks among the world’s largest integrated copper producers, boasting what it describes as the largest copper reserves globally and a leading position in Peru and Mexico. Its competitive advantages stem from high vertical integration, which allows control over the entire production chain from mining to refined products, and a focus on cost control and operational efficiency to navigate copper price cycles. The company faces competition from other copper miners and from substitute materials such as aluminum and plastics, but its scale and integrated structure provide a cost advantage.

The company serves end‑user customers in industries such as construction, power generation and transmission, electronics and telecommunications, automotive manufacturing, and industrial machinery. While specific customer names are not disclosed, the sales strategy emphasizes long‑term contracts with manufacturers and fabricators that require reliable copper, zinc, molybdenum and silver supplies for their production processes.

BLK.address_business: 50 Hudson Yards, New York, 10001 New York, US
BLK.address_mailing: 50 Hudson Yards, New York, 10001 New York, US
BLK.profile_html:
BlackRock, Inc. is the world’s largest publicly traded investment management firm, overseeing $14.0 trillion in assets under management as of December 31, 2025. The company operates across more than 30 countries, serving institutional and retail clients in over 100 markets with a broad suite of investment, technology, and advisory services. BlackRock’s core activities include managing active and index strategies, private markets investments, and exchange-traded funds, alongside providing risk management and technology platforms such as Aladdin. The firm’s diversified platform spans equities, fixed income, multi-asset solutions, alternatives, digital assets, and cash management, positioning it as a comprehensive provider of asset allocation and investment solutions.

BlackRock generates revenue primarily through investment management fees, which are typically calculated as a percentage of assets under management. The company also earns performance fees on certain portfolios, securities lending revenue, and fees from its technology and subscription services, including Aladdin, eFront, and Preqin. These services cater to institutional investors, wealth managers, and financial intermediaries, with revenue models based on factors such as the value of positions managed, the number of subscriptions, and software implementation. The firm’s client base includes pension plans, sovereign wealth funds, insurance companies, corporations, and retail investors, ensuring a steady stream of recurring revenue from both advisory and technology-driven offerings.

The company operates through the following segments:

  • Investment Management: This segment encompasses BlackRock’s core asset management business, offering active, index, and private markets strategies across equities, fixed income, multi-asset, alternatives, digital assets, and cash management. The segment serves institutional and retail clients through mutual funds, ETFs, separate accounts, and pooled investment vehicles, with a focus on delivering risk-adjusted returns and tailored investment solutions. Investment performance and client inflows drive revenue, which is predominantly fee-based.
  • Technology and Subscription Services: This segment provides investment and risk management technology platforms, including Aladdin, Aladdin Wealth, eFront, Preqin, and Cachematrix. These solutions offer risk analytics, portfolio management, private markets data, and cash management tools to asset managers, insurance companies, pension funds, and wealth managers. Revenue is generated through long-term contracts, subscriptions, and implementation fees, with annual contract value growth reflecting strong client adoption and expansion.

BlackRock holds a dominant position in the global asset management industry, distinguished by its scale, diversified product offerings, and technological leadership. The company competes with other large investment managers, mutual fund complexes, insurance companies, and financial technology providers, but its competitive advantages lie in its fiduciary focus, global distribution network, and proprietary technology platforms. BlackRock’s iShares ETF franchise, with $5.5 trillion in assets, is the largest in the world, while Aladdin is a market-leading risk management and investment system used by institutional investors globally. The firm’s ability to integrate investment management with technology solutions further strengthens its market position, enabling it to capture secular trends such as the growth of ETFs, private markets, and sustainable investing.

BlackRock serves a diverse customer base, including tax-exempt institutions such as pension plans, endowments, and foundations; official institutions like central banks and sovereign wealth funds; taxable institutions such as insurance companies, corporations, and financial intermediaries; and retail investors through intermediaries like broker-dealers and financial advisors. The company’s institutional clients span defined benefit and defined contribution pension plans, with $3.9 trillion in pension assets under management, while its retail business serves individual investors through mutual funds and separately managed accounts. BlackRock’s technology platforms, including Aladdin and eFront, are utilized by asset managers, banks, and corporations worldwide, reinforcing its role as a critical infrastructure provider in the financial services industry.

ETN.address_mailing: 30 Pembroke Road, Eaton House, Dublin, Dublin 4 Ireland
ETN.profile_html:
Eaton Corporation plc is an intelligent power management company dedicated to protecting the environment and improving quality of life worldwide. The company designs manufactures and sells products for data centers utilities industrial commercial machine building residential aerospace and mobility markets. It focuses on solving power management challenges through innovation and sustainable solutions across the global electrical power value chain.

Eaton generates revenue by selling electrical components systems and services that manage power efficiently and safely. Its primary offerings include circuit breakers switchgear power distribution units lighting controls hydraulics and aerospace fuel systems. Revenue comes from diversified end markets including data centers utilities automotive commercial vehicles aerospace and residential construction serving customers in 180 countries.

The company operates through the following segments: Electrical Americas Electrical Global Aerospace Vehicle and eMobility.

  • Electrical Americas provides power management solutions for residential commercial and industrial customers across North and South America including circuit breakers switchgear lighting controls and power distribution equipment.
  • Electrical Global delivers similar power management products and services for customers outside the Americas focusing on international markets with standardized electrical infrastructure solutions.
  • Aerospace supplies fuel systems hydraulic systems actuation systems and avionics for commercial military and space aircraft emphasizing performance safety and sustainability.
  • Vehicle provides technologies for automotive commercial vehicle aftermarket and off-road applications including transmission systems turbochargers and hybrid electric vehicle components to improve efficiency and performance.
  • eMobility focuses on electrified transportation solutions such as battery management systems onboard chargers and power electronics for electric vehicles supporting the global shift to zero-emission mobility.

Eaton holds a strong competitive position in its core markets often ranked among market leaders due to product performance technology customer service and global reach. It competes with companies like Schneider Electric Siemens ABB and Rockwell Automation leveraging its broad portfolio and intellectual property to maintain differentiation.

Eaton serves a diverse customer base including original equipment manufacturers in aerospace automotive and commercial vehicle sectors utility companies data center operators industrial manufacturers and residential builders. Major customers include large aircraft manufacturers vehicle OEMs and six key electrical product buyers representing significant portions of segment sales.

ABT.address_mailing: 100 Abbott Park Road, Abbott Park, 60064-3500 Illinois, US
ABT.profile_html:
Abbott Laboratories discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells a broad line of healthcare products worldwide. The company states its mission is to help people live their healthiest possible lives. Abbott operates in more than 160 countries employing about 115,000 staff with roughly 69% based outside the United States.

Revenue comes from sales of pharmaceutical diagnostic nutrition and medical device products. Products are distributed through wholesalers distributors government agencies hospitals clinics pharmacies retailers physicians offices consumers and alternate care testing sites globally. Ongoing innovation and a global supply chain support revenue across emerging and developed markets.

The company reports financial performance through four operating segments defined by product lines. These segments are Established Pharmaceutical Products Diagnostic Products Nutritional Products and Medical Devices.

  • Established Pharmaceutical Products: This segment markets branded generic pharmaceuticals primarily outside the United States with a focus on emerging markets. Its portfolio features gastroenterology agents such as Creon cardiovascular drugs like Lipanthyl and Synthroid respiratory agents such as clarithromycin and Influvac and biologic biosimilars in oncology immunology and women s health distributed via wholesalers distributors government agencies healthcare facilities pharmacies and independent retailers.
  • Diagnostic Products: This segment provides diagnostic systems and tests used in laboratories and point of care settings worldwide. Offerings include core lab systems molecular diagnostics for HIV hepatitis and SARS CoV 2 point of care devices like i STAT rapid tests such as BinaxNOW and informatics tools for hospital and laboratory customers.
  • Nutritional Products: This segment offers pediatric and adult nutritional products including infant formula adult nutrition and enteral feeding solutions. Brands feature Similac and Ensure lines with products such as Glucerna and Pedialyte sold to consumers institutions wholesalers retailers healthcare facilities government agencies and third party distributors.
  • Medical Devices: This segment develops and sells devices for rhythm management electrophysiology heart failure vascular structural heart diabetes care and neuromodulation. Products include pacemakers defibrillators stents ventricular assist devices glucose monitors and neuromodulation stimulators sold worldwide through wholesalers hospitals ambulatory surgery centers physicians offices consumers and distributors.

Abbott Laboratories holds a diversified position in the global healthcare industry competing with other major healthcare and pharmaceutical companies. The company leverages its broad product portfolio global distribution network and ongoing investment in research and development to maintain competitive advantages. Its scale supports innovation and responsiveness to regulatory changes while strong brand recognition aids customer loyalty.

The company sells its products to wholesalers distributors government agencies hospitals clinics pharmacies retailers physicians offices consumers and alternate care testing sites worldwide. Customers span pharmaceutical distributors and government agencies diagnostic hospitals labs and public health agencies nutrition retail consumers institutions and government programs and medical device users hospitals ambulatory centers physicians and patients.

SCHW.profile_html:
The Charles Schwab Corporation is a savings and loan holding company that, through its subsidiaries, provides wealth management, securities brokerage, banking, asset management, custody, and financial advisory services. At December 31, 2025, the company reported $11.90 trillion in client assets, 38,500,000 active brokerage accounts, 5,700,000 workplace plan participant accounts, and 2,200,000 banking accounts.

Schwab generates revenue primarily through asset management fees, brokerage commissions, net interest income from its banking operations, and advisory and service fees. The company serves individual investors, institutional clients, and workplace plan participants, offering products such as mutual funds, exchange traded funds, retirement accounts, and lending services.

The company operates through the following segments: Investor Services and Advisor Services.

  • Investor Services: This segment provides retail brokerage, investment advisory, banking and trust services to individual investors, and retirement plan and business services, as well as other corporate brokerage services, to businesses and their employees.
  • Advisor Services: This segment delivers custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.

Schwab’s competitive advantages stem from its scale and size, operating efficiency derived from shared infrastructure, an integrated operating structure that combines bank, wealth, and asset management services, a strong brand and reputation for trust, a service centric culture, and a willingness to disrupt legacy practices. In the Investor Services arena, the company competes with brokerage, wealth management, and asset management firms, as well as banks, trust companies, fintech providers, and retirement service providers. In the Advisor Services arena, Schwab faces competition from institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

Schwab’s customer base includes individual investors, institutional clients, workplace plan participants, and businesses seeking brokerage and retirement services. The company also serves independent registered investment advisors, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers through its Advisor Services segment.

T.name: At&T Inc.
T.address_business: 208 S. Akard St, Dallas, 75202 Texas, US
T.address_mailing: 208 S. Akard St, Dallas, 75202 Texas, US
T.profile_html:
AT&T Inc. is a leading provider of telecommunications and technology services worldwide. The company delivers wireless voice and data services wireline broadband and voice services and video entertainment offerings through its subsidiaries. It operates a large network infrastructure that includes fiber optic cables wireless spectrum and satellite assets. AT&T Inc. serves consumers businesses and government entities across the United States and in select international markets. The firm also provides wholesale connectivity to other carriers and supports public safety communications through its FirstNet network.

The company generates revenue primarily from monthly service charges for wireless plans wireline broadband connections and legacy voice services. Equipment sales of handsets routers and other devices add to income. Service revenue from mobility business wireline and consumer wireline units accounts for the majority of total sales while equipment revenue contributes a smaller share. The Latin America segment adds wireless service fees and device sales in Mexico. In addition the company earns revenue from licensing its intellectual property and from providing managed professional services to enterprise clients.

The company operates through the following segments: Communications and Latin America.

  • The Communications segment provides wireless and wireline telecom and broadband services to consumers in the United States and to business customers worldwide. It includes the Mobility unit offering nationwide postpaid prepaid and reseller wireless service and device sales. The Business Wireline unit delivers fiber based Ethernet IP voice managed professional services and legacy copper services to enterprises. The Consumer Wireline unit supplies fiber broadband fixed wireless access and traditional voice services to residential customers.
  • The Latin America segment provides wireless voice and data services in Mexico. It serves approximately 24.7 million subscribers under the AT&T and Unefon brands offering postpaid and prepaid plans. The segment sells handsets accessories and other devices through company owned stores agents and third party retailers. Revenue comes from both service subscriptions and equipment sales in the region.

AT&T Inc. holds a strong position in the U. S. telecommunications market ranking among the top three wireless carriers alongside Verizon Communications and T Mobile US. In the wireline broadband arena it competes with large cable operators such as Comcast Charter Communications and Spectrum. The company benefits from a nationwide fiber footprint extensive spectrum holdings and a powerful brand portfolio that includes AT&T Business Cricket and AT&T PREPAID. Its scale allows it to achieve cost efficiencies in network operations and to invest heavily in next generation technologies such as 5G and fiber to the home. In Mexico its wireless operations face competition primarily from América Móvil but the company leverages its network quality and customer service to maintain market share. Overall AT&T Inc. is recognized for its reliable network coverage innovative service bundles and strong customer relationships.

The company serves a diverse customer base that includes individual consumers seeking mobile and internet connectivity small and medium sized businesses looking for reliable voice and data solutions large enterprises needing managed network and cloud services and government agencies requiring secure communications. Wholesale customers such as other telecom carriers and internet service providers also purchase capacity from AT&T Inc.'s network. No single customer accounted for ten percent or more of consolidated revenues in recent years.

NVO.name: Novo Nordisk A S
NVO.address_business: Novo Alle Dk 2880, Bagsvaerd Denmark, 00000 Denmark
NVO.address_mailing: Novo Alle Dk 2880, Bagsvaerd Denmark, 00000 Denmark
NVO.profile_html:
Novo Nordisk A/S is a global healthcare company that focuses on the discovery development manufacturing and marketing of pharmaceutical products. The company is a world leader in obesity and diabetes care and also has a rare disease business. Headquartered in Denmark Novo Nordisk employs more than 69 500 people in around 80 countries and markets its products in approximately 170 countries.

Novo Nordisk generates revenue primarily from the sale of its pharmaceutical products. Key product lines include glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists for obesity and diabetes such as Ozempic Wegovy Saxenda and Rybelsus modern and human insulins and rare disease therapies covering growth hormone and haemophilia. Sales are made to wholesalers distributors pharmacies hospitals and directly to patients in many markets.

The company operates through two business segments Obesity and Diabetes care and Rare disease.

  • Obesity and Diabetes care segment includes the development and sale of glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists for obesity and diabetes modern and human insulins and related diabetes care products.
  • Rare disease segment focuses on growth hormone therapies and haemophilia products and other treatments for rare endocrine and metabolic disorders.

Novo Nordisk holds a leading position in the global obesity and diabetes markets competing chiefly with Eli Lilly while also facing competition from biosimilar insulin manufacturers and emerging anti obesity drug developers. The company benefits from a broad product portfolio strong manufacturing capacity and a well established research and development pipeline that supports sustained market share.

Novo Nordisk serves patients with diabetes obesity and rare diseases as well as healthcare providers hospitals pharmacies and long term care facilities across the countries where it operates.

UNP.name: Union Pacific Corp
UNP.address_business: 1400 Douglas Street, Stop 0310, Omaha, 68179 Nebraska, US
UNP.address_mailing: 1400 Douglas Street, Stop 0310, Omaha, 68179 Nebraska, US
UNP.profile_html:
Union Pacific Corporation operates a freight rail network that connects 23 states in the western two thirds of the United States by rail, providing a critical link in the global supply chain. The Railroad is a Class I railroad that maintains 32,889 route miles of track linking Pacific and Gulf coast ports with Midwest and Eastern gateways and reaching all six major Mexico gateways and several Canadian border crossings. Its diversified business moves Bulk, Industrial, and Premium commodities ranging from grain fertilizer coal to automobiles and intermodal containers. The company emphasizes safe, reliable, and environmentally responsible transportation to support customers across multiple industries.

The company generates revenue primarily from freight transportation services charged for moving Bulk, Industrial, and Premium commodities across its rail network. In 2025 freight revenues totaled $23.2 billion with Bulk accounting for 33%, Industrial for 37%, and Premium for 30% of the total. The Bulk segment includes grain and grain products, fertilizer, food and refrigerated items, and coal and renewables. The Industrial segment covers construction, industrial chemicals, plastics, forest products, specialized products, metals ores, petroleum, liquid petroleum gases, soda ash, and sand. The Premium segment consists of finished automobiles, automotive parts, and merchandise transported in intermodal containers both domestic and international.

The company operates through the following segments: The Railroad.

  • The Railroad: Provides freight rail transportation across 23 states linking Pacific and Gulf coast ports with Midwest and Eastern gateways and reaching all six major Mexico gateways and several Canadian border crossings moving Bulk, Industrial, and Premium commodities such as grain, fertilizer, coal, construction materials, chemicals, automobiles, and intermodal containers while emphasizing safety, reliability, and fuel efficiency.

Union Pacific Corporation holds a leading position among U. S. Class I railroads distinguished by its extensive network that reaches all six major Mexico gateways and its status as the largest automotive carrier west of the Mississippi River. Competitors include other major railroads such as BNSF Railway, CSX Corporation, and Norfolk Southern Corporation as well as trucking and intermodal service providers. The company benefits from a strong safety record showing a 24% improvement in personal injury rate and a 19% improvement in derailment incident rate in 2025 compared with the prior year. Its focus on fuel efficiency gives it an environmental advantage moving freight by rail generates significantly lower greenhouse gas emissions than truck transport. Operational excellence initiatives aim to improve the operating ratio and return on invested capital supporting long term value creation.

Union Pacific Corporation serves a diverse customer base that includes agricultural processors, energy providers, industrial manufacturers, automotive companies, and intermodal marketing firms. Specific examples are grain processors, animal feeders, ethanol producers, power companies, steel mills, and automobile manufacturers. The company also moves commodities for food processors, beverage makers, and retail distribution centers. Additionally it supports the agricultural sector by transporting fertilizer to farms, and delivering grain to export terminals. Its intermodal business serves logistics companies, truckload carriers, and retailers that rely on containerized shipments for domestic and international trade.

The Premium segment consists of finished automobiles, automotive parts, and merchandise transported in intermodal containers both domestic and international.

The company operates through the following segments: The Railroad.

 • The Railroad: Provides freight rail transportation across 23 states linking Pacific and Gulf coast ports with Midwest and Eastern gateways and reaching all six major Mexico gateways and several Canadian border crossings moving Bulk, Industrial, and Premium commodities such as grain, fertilizer, coal, construction materials, chemicals, automobiles, and intermodal containers while emphasizing safety, reliability, and fuel efficiency.

Union Pacific Corporation holds a leading position among U. S. Class I railroads distinguished by its extensive network that reaches all six major Mexico gateways and its status as the largest automotive carrier west of the Mississippi River. Competitors include other major railroads such as BNSF Railway, CSX Corporation, and Norfolk Southern Corporation as well as trucking and intermodal service providers. The company benefits from a strong safety record showing a 24% improvement in personal injury rate and a 19% improvement in derailment incident rate in 2025 compared with the prior year. Its focus on fuel efficiency gives it an environmental advantage moving freight by rail generates significantly lower greenhouse gas emissions than truck transport. Operational excellence initiatives aim to improve the operating ratio and return on invested capital supporting long term value creation.

Union Pacific Corporation serves a diverse customer base that includes agricultural processors, energy providers, industrial manufacturers, automotive companies, and intermodal marketing firms. Specific examples are grain processors, animal feeders, ethanol producers, power companies, steel mills, and automobile manufacturers. The company also moves commodities for food processors, beverage makers, and retail distribution centers. Additionally it supports the agricultural sector by transporting fertilizer to farms, and delivering grain to export terminals. Its intermodal business serves logistics companies, truckload carriers, and retailers that rely on containerized shipments for domestic and international trade.

WELL.name: Welltower Inc.
WELL.profile_html:
Welltower Inc. is a real estate investment trust and S&P 500 company focused on rental housing for aging seniors in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada. The company's portfolio consists of over 2,500 seniors and wellness housing communities that combine housing and hospitality to serve mature renters and older adults. Welltower operates as an umbrella partnership REIT, with substantially all business conducted through Welltower OP LLC, which is exclusively controlled by Welltower Inc. The company invests in seniors housing, wellness housing, and post-acute care communities to diversify by property type, relationship, and geographic location.

Welltower generates revenue primarily through rental income from its properties across three reportable segments: Seniors Housing Operating, Triple-net, and Outpatient Medical. The Seniors Housing Operating segment contributed 78% of total revenues in 2025, the Triple-net segment 11%, and the Outpatient Medical segment 7%. Revenue is derived from leasing properties to operators and tenants under various structures, including RIDEA arrangements and triple-net leases, where tenants pay operating costs, taxes, insurance, and maintenance. The company also earns interest income from real estate loans and returns from investments in unconsolidated entities.

The company operates through the following segments: Seniors Housing Operating, Triple-net, and Outpatient Medical.

  • Seniors Housing Operating: This segment includes wellness housing, independent living, independent supportive living, continuing care retirement communities, assisted living, Alzheimer’s/dementia care, and care homes with or without nursing in the U. K. These properties assist with activities of daily living and provide social systems to promote cognitive engagement. The segment includes stand-alone properties, combination properties, and multi-service campuses, some held in joint ventures or using RIDEA structures. In 2025, management partners such as Care UK, Cogir Management Company, and Sunrise Senior Living accounted for 14%, 12%, and 10% of segment revenues, respectively.
  • Triple-net: This segment includes properties offering independent living, assisted living, continuing care retirement communities, Alzheimer’s/dementia care, care homes with or without nursing in the U. K., and long-term/post-acute care facilities. Properties are leased to operators under long-term triple-net master leases requiring tenants to pay all operating costs, utilities, taxes, insurance, maintenance, and capital expenditures. Leases typically have fixed terms of 10 to 20 years with renewal options and escalating rent structures. In 2025, approximately 96.9% of triple-net properties were subject to master leases, with Integra Healthcare Properties accounting for 16% of segment revenues and 2% of total revenues.
  • Outpatient Medical: This segment consists of triple-net leased properties leased to investment-grade healthcare providers, primarily affiliated with health systems. As of 2025, 91% of the outpatient medical portfolio was affiliated with health systems, either on or adjacent to hospital campuses or as satellite locations. Leases have a weighted-average remaining term of eight years and are often credit-enhanced by security deposits, guarantees, or letters of credit. The expense reimbursement structure varies, with 66% of leases providing full pass-through, 24% partial reimbursement, and 10% no reimbursement to tenants.

Welltower holds a leading position in the seniors housing and healthcare real estate industry as one of the largest owners and operators of senior living communities in North America and the U. K. The company competes with other REITs, private equity funds, healthcare operators, and developers in acquiring and financing healthcare and seniors housing properties. Its competitive advantages include a Data Science platform and the Welltower Business System, which support investment selection, underwriting, and operating partner standardization through shared services and technology enablement.

Welltower serves a diverse customer base including seniors seeking independent or assisted living, individuals requiring memory care or skilled nursing, and patients needing post-acute or rehabilitation services. The company’s tenants include healthcare operators such as Care UK, Cogir Management Company, Sunrise Senior Living, and Integra Healthcare Properties, which manage properties under contractual agreements. Outpatient medical properties are leased to health systems and physician groups affiliated with hospitals.

MCD.name: Mcdonalds Corp
MCD.address_business: 110 North Carpenter Street, Chicago, 60607 Illinois, US
MCD.address_mailing: 110 North Carpenter Street, Chicago, 60607 Illinois, US
MCD.profile_html:
McDonald's franchises and owns and operates restaurants that serve a locally relevant menu of food and beverages in over 100 countries. The company operates as a global quick service restaurant chain with a strong franchising model that generates the majority of its revenue from franchise fees while also operating a smaller number of company owned locations. The company continues to innovate its menu while maintaining core items that have become iconic worldwide. Its operating model emphasizes consistency, speed, and value for customers.

McDonald's generates revenue from two primary sources. First it collects rent royalties and initial fees from franchised restaurants operated under conventional franchise developmental license or affiliate arrangements. Second it records sales from company owned restaurants. Additionally the company earns other revenue from fees paid by franchisees for technology and digital platforms and from brand licensing agreements that allow the use of the McDonald's name on consumer packaged goods. Franchised revenue depends largely on the sales performance of franchisees, which in turn drives the company's cash flow and profitability.

The company operates through the following segments: United States, International Operated Markets, and International Developmental Licensed Markets & Corporate.

  • United States: This segment includes the company's operations in the United States encompassing both franchised and company owned restaurants and generating revenue from rent royalties and sales at company owned locations.
  • International Operated Markets: This segment covers markets where McDonald's directly operates restaurants often under a mix of franchise and company owned models contributing revenue from similar sources outside the United States.
  • International Developmental Licensed Markets & Corporate: This segment aggregates results from over seventy five countries where developmental license or affiliate arrangements predominate includes corporate activities and earns royalties and fees from those arrangements.

McDonald's holds a leading position in the global quick service restaurant industry competing with brands such as Burger King, Wendy's, and Yum! Brands, which operates Taco Bell, KFC, and Pizza Hut. The company's competitive advantages stem from its scale, its iconic brand, its extensive real estate holdings, and its proven franchising system that delivers consistent quality and value across diverse markets. Its size allows it to benefit from economies of scale in procurement and logistics, while its brand recognition supports pricing power and customer loyalty worldwide.

McDonald's serves individual consumers, families, and individuals seeking convenient affordable meals worldwide. Its customer base includes people of all ages who visit its restaurants for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks. The company also attracts customers through digital promotions, loyalty programs, and limited time menu items that appeal to diverse tastes and preferences.
