NEE.address_mailing: P O Box 14000, Juno Beach, 33408 Florida, US
NEE.profile_html:
NextEra Energy Inc is a leading clean energy company operating primarily through two principal businesses: Florida Power & Light Company (FPL) and NextEra Energy Resources (NEER). FPL is the largest electric utility in the United States, serving more than six million customer accounts across Florida. NEER, together with affiliated entities, is one of the largest energy infrastructure developers in the U. S., focused on developing, constructing, and operating long-lived assets. The company generates electricity, provides energy services, and invests in renewable energy projects including wind, solar, and battery storage. NextEra Energy Inc also engages in energy marketing and trading activities to optimize the value of its generation and natural gas and oil production assets.

NextEra Energy Inc generates revenue through the sale of electricity to retail and wholesale customers, energy marketing and trading operations, and the development and operation of clean energy projects. FPL earns revenue primarily from regulated electricity sales to its six million plus customer accounts in Florida, including base rates, fuel cost recovery, and storm protection plan charges. NEER derives income from the sale of electricity and energy commodities under long-term power purchase agreements, market-based sales, and tax credit monetization from wind, solar, and storage projects. The company also earns revenue from natural gas and oil production, equity method investments, and gains on the disposal of businesses or assets. Additional revenue streams include interest income, investment returns, and regulated gas transmission services.

The company operates through the following segments: FPL and NEER.

  • FPL: This segment provides regulated electric utility service to more than six million customer accounts in Florida. It generates, transmits, distributes, and sells electricity under the authority of the Florida Public Service Commission. FPL operates under rate agreements that allow for the recovery of costs and a targeted return on equity, including mechanisms like the Reserve Surplus Amortization (RSA) and Revenue Stabilization Mechanism (RSM).
  • NEER: This segment develops, constructs, owns, and operates long-lived assets primarily in the clean energy space, including wind, solar, and battery storage projects. It also engages in natural gas and oil production, energy marketing and trading, and regulated electric and gas transmission activities. NEER operates through subsidiaries and affiliates and monetizes clean energy tax credits such as Production Tax Credits (PTCs) and Investment Tax Credits (ITCs). The segment includes ownership interests in projects like Duane Arnold, Symmetry, and Caliber acquisitions.

NextEra Energy Inc holds a leading position in the U. S. utility and renewable energy sectors, competing with other major utilities and independent power producers such as Duke Energy, Southern Company, and Dominion Energy. Its competitive advantages include scale, a strong growth trajectory in renewable energy development, and a favorable regulatory framework supporting clean energy investments. The company benefits from access to capital markets, a history of consistent dividend growth, and one of the largest clean energy generation pipelines in the country. NEER’s ability to monetize tax credits and optimize asset performance through active management enhances its market position relative to peers.

NextEra Energy Inc serves over six million retail customer accounts in Florida through FPL, primarily residential, commercial, and industrial users. NEER serves wholesale customers including utilities, municipalities, cooperatives, and corporate entities under long-term power purchase agreements. The company also provides energy services to market participants through its trading and marketing operations. Specific customer names are not disclosed in the filing, but the customer base includes a broad range of energy consumers and counterparties across the United States.

RIO.name: Rio Tinto Plc
RIO.address_business: 6 St James'S Square, London, Sw1Y 4Ad, 00000 United Kingdom
RIO.address_mailing: Rio Tinto Services Inc., 80 State Street, Albany, 12207-2543 New York, US
RIO.profile_html:
Rio Tinto engages in the mining and processing of minerals and metals worldwide. Its core activities span the entire lifecycle from exploration and development to mining, processing, marketing, and asset repurposing. The company operates as a diversified producer of essential materials critical to global infrastructure and the energy transition.

Rio Tinto generates revenue primarily through the sale of iron ore, copper, aluminium, bauxite, alumina, lithium, and industrial minerals such as salt and borates. Revenue is derived from contracts with customers and adjusted for provisionally priced receivables. The company serves a global customer base including steelmakers, automotive manufacturers, construction firms, and technology companies involved in electrification and renewable energy.

The company operates through the following segments: Aluminium & Lithium, Copper, and Iron Ore.

  • Aluminium & Lithium: This segment encompasses the production of bauxite, alumina, aluminium, and lithium carbonate equivalent. Rio Tinto's aluminium operations include integrated smelters such as Boyne Island and Tiwai Point, which utilize advanced AP60 technology for low-carbon production. The segment also features lithium assets from the Rincon project in Argentina and the full integration of Arcadium Lithium, adding operations at Olaroz, Hombre Muerto, and Nemaska.
  • Copper: This segment focuses on the mining, refining, and sale of copper and associated by-products such as gold. Key operations include the Oyu Tolgoi underground and open-pit mines in Mongolia, the Kennecott mine in Utah, and the Escondida mine in Chile via a joint venture with BHP. The segment benefited from the divestment of a 30% interest in the Winu copper-gold project to Sumitomo Metal Mining, which generated a pre-tax gain of $196 million.
  • Iron Ore: This segment integrates Rio Tinto’s Pilbara operations in Western Australia, the Iron Ore Company of Canada, and the Simandou project in Guinea. The Pilbara Blend is produced from major assets including Hamersley, Hope Downs, Western Range, and Robe River Iron Associates. Simandou represents a transformative infrastructure initiative delivering high-grade iron ore via a new rail and port system, positioning Rio Tinto to serve evolving demand in the Global Steel market.

Rio Tinto maintains a leading position in the global mining industry as one of the world’s largest diversified resource companies. Its competitive advantages stem from scale, operational excellence, and a disciplined approach to capital allocation. The company differentiates itself through its integrated value chain, world-class assets, and growing presence in energy transition metals like lithium and copper, competing with peers such as BHP, Vale, and Glencore.

Rio Tinto serves a broad customer base that includes steel producers, automobile manufacturers, electronics and renewable energy firms, and construction companies worldwide. Specific customers are not named in the filing, but the company references its role in supplying materials for low-carbon steel, electric vehicle batteries, and grid infrastructure. Its products are fundamental to industrial and technological supply chains across regions including Greater China, the United States, Europe, and Japan.

SMFG.name: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc.
SMFG.profile_html:
Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc. is a Japanese financial holding company that oversees the SMBC Group. It provides a broad range of financial services including commercial banking leasing securities consumer finance asset management and related activities. The company is one of the three largest financial groups in Japan and maintains a significant domestic and international presence.

Revenue is generated primarily from interest income on loans and deposits fees and commissions from banking securities and leasing activities and income from asset management and consumer finance operations. The company serves corporate clients retail customers high net worth individuals small and medium sized enterprises and government entities.

The company operates through the following segments: Wholesale Business Unit Retail Business Unit Global Business Unit Global Markets Business Unit and Other Business which includes system development data processing management consulting economic research and asset management.

  • Wholesale Business Unit provides comprehensive solutions primarily for corporate clients in Japan including financing investment management risk hedging settlement mergers and acquisitions advisory digital services and leasing services.
  • Retail Business Unit offers financial services to consumers in Japan such as wealth management settlement consumer finance housing loans and related products.
  • Global Business Unit supports the global activities of Japanese companies operating overseas non Japanese companies financial institutions government agencies public corporations and retail clients in various countries providing banking securities derivatives and leasing services.
  • Global Markets Business Unit delivers solutions through foreign exchange derivatives bonds stocks asset liability management portfolio management foreign currency funding and sales and trading activities.
  • Other Business encompasses system development data processing management consulting economic research through The Japan Research Institute and asset management services via SMDAM and TT International Asset Management Ltd.

Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc. holds a leading position among Japanese financial institutions ranking alongside Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and Mizuho Financial Group as one of the three largest groups in the country. Its competitive strengths stem from a diversified portfolio of banking leasing securities and consumer finance operations a strong domestic branch network and an expanding overseas presence. The group benefits from brand recognition derived from its historic Sumitomo and Mitsui roots and its focus on integrated financial solutions.

The company serves a broad customer base that includes large corporations small and medium sized enterprises high net worth individuals retail consumers and government agencies. Its retail operations cater to individual customers seeking wealth management housing loans consumer finance and payment services while its wholesale division supports corporate financing investment and risk management needs.

PFE.address_mailing: 66 Hudson Boulevard East, New York, 10001-2192 New York, US
PFE.profile_html:
Pfizer Inc. is a research-based global biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, manufacture, marketing, sale, and distribution of biopharmaceutical products worldwide. The company applies science and global resources to deliver therapies that extend and significantly improve lives by addressing wellness, prevention, treatments, and cures for some of the most feared diseases. Pfizer collaborates with healthcare providers, governments, and local communities to expand access to reliable and affordable healthcare across developed and emerging markets.

Pfizer generates revenue primarily through the manufacture and sale of its biopharmaceutical products, including medicines and vaccines. The company believes its products provide value by improving disease treatment, enhancing health and wellness, increasing productivity, and reducing healthcare costs such as emergency room visits and hospitalizations. Pfizer seeks to maximize patient access and evaluates pricing and contracting arrangements with payors to minimize adverse revenue impacts within legal and pricing frameworks.

The company operates through the following segments: Biopharma, PC1, and Pfizer Ignite.

  • Biopharma: This segment is engaged in the discovery, development, manufacture, marketing, sale, and distribution of biopharmaceutical products worldwide. It includes the commercialization of Pfizer’s entire product portfolio through divisions such as Pfizer U. S. Commercial, Pfizer International Commercial, and Global Hospital and Biosimilars. Key products in this segment include Eliquis, Nurtec ODT/Vydura, Zavzpret, the Prevnar family, Comirnaty, Abrysvo, FSME/IMMUN-TicoVac, Nimenrix, Trumenba, Paxlovid, Xeljanz, Enbrel (outside the U. BA.profile_html:
The Boeing Company is one of the world’s major aerospace firms, organized around the products and services it offers. It develops, produces, and markets commercial jet aircraft, military aircraft and weapons systems, and provides sustainment and support services for aerospace platforms worldwide.

The company generates revenue primarily from the sale of commercial jetliners to airlines, from contracts for defense and space systems with government and commercial customers, and from service agreements that cover maintenance, upgrades, training, and logistics for both commercial and defense fleets. Its revenue streams are diversified across aircraft production, defense contracts, and aftermarket services.

The company operates through the following segments: Commercial Airplanes (BCA), Defense, Space & Security (BDS), and Global Services (BGS).

  • Commercial Airplanes (BCA): This segment develops, produces and markets commercial jet aircraft principally to the commercial airline industry worldwide, offering a family of jetliners including the 737 narrow-body and the 767, 777 and 787 wide-body models, with ongoing development of the 777X program and 737-7 and 737-10 derivatives.
  • Defense, Space & Security (BDS): This segment engages in the research, development, production and modification of manned and unmanned military aircraft and weapons systems for strike, surveillance and mobility, including fighter and trainer aircraft, vertical lift such as rotorcraft and tilt-rotor aircraft, and commercial derivative aircraft like anti-submarine and tanker aircraft; it also works on strategic defense and intelligence systems, satellite systems, and space exploration.
  • Global Services (BGS): This segment provides services to commercial and defense customers worldwide, sustaining aerospace platforms through supply chain and logistics management, engineering, maintenance and modifications, upgrades and conversions, spare parts, pilot and maintenance training, technical documents, and digital solutions and analytics.

Boeing holds a leading position in the global aerospace industry as one of the two dominant manufacturers of large commercial aircraft alongside Airbus, while facing emerging competition from Chinese entrants. In the defense and space sector, it competes with major contractors such as General Dynamics Corporation, Lockheed Martin Corporation, Northrop Grumman Corporation, RTX Corporation, and SpaceX, as well as non‑U. S. firms like BAE Systems and Airbus Group that have expanded their North American operations. The company’s competitive advantages stem from its broad product portfolio, integrated services network, extensive intellectual property, and long‑standing relationships with government and commercial customers.

The company serves a diverse customer base that includes commercial airlines worldwide, the U. S. Department of Defense and other federal agencies such as NASA and the Department of Homeland Security, allied foreign governments, and defense contractors. It also provides aftermarket services to airlines, leasing companies, and maintenance providers that operate its aircraft fleets.

COP.address_mailing: Shipping & Receiving Center, 16930 Park Row Dr., Houston, 77084 Texas, US
COP.profile_html:
ConocoPhillips is an independent exploration and production company that focuses on finding producing and selling crude oil natural gas natural gas liquids and bitumen worldwide. The company conducts operations in fourteen countries and maintains a diverse portfolio that includes unconventional plays in North America conventional assets in North America Europe Africa and Asia global liquefied natural gas developments oil sands in Canada and an inventory of exploration prospects. Headquartered in Houston Texas ConocoPhillips employed approximately eleven thousand four hundred people worldwide and reported total assets of about one hundred twenty two billion dollars as of September 30 2025.

ConocoPhillips generates revenue primarily by selling the hydrocarbons it produces. The company sells crude oil natural gas natural gas liquids and bitumen to refiners petrochemical plants utilities and industrial customers around the globe. In addition ConocoPhillips earns income from long term contracts for liquefied natural gas offtake and from the marketing of third party volumes under its trading and transportation activities. Revenue is also derived from gains on asset sales and from royalties received on properties where it retains an overriding interest.

The company operates through the following segments: Alaska Lower 48 Canada Europe Middle East and North Africa Asia Pacific Other International and Corporate and Other.

  • Alaska segment explores for produces transports and markets crude oil natural gas liquids and natural gas from assets mainly located on the Alaska North Slope including the Greater Kuparuk area and the Western North Slope with projects such as Willow.
  • Lower 48 segment consists of onshore operations in the contiguous United States covering major shale plays such as the Delaware Basin Eagle Ford Midland Basin and Bakken as well as conventional fields and includes marketing and trading activities for the produced hydrocarbons.
  • Canada segment focuses on oil sands development at Surmont in Alberta and on the Montney unconventional play in British Columbia while also managing associated commercial operations.
  • Europe Middle East and North Africa segment includes offshore interests in the Norwegian sector of the North Sea and the Norwegian Sea as well as producing assets in Qatar Libya Equatorial Guinea and terminalling operations in the United Kingdom.
  • Asia Pacific segment comprises operations in China Malaysia Australia and commercial activities in Singapore Japan focusing on offshore fields and onshore developments such as Bohai Bay in China and Gumusut in Malaysia.
  • Other International segment covers residual activities from prior operations in countries where the company no longer maintains active exploration or production interests.
  • Corporate and Other segment encompasses corporate functions such as general and administrative expenses technology investments interest expense and other income items that are not allocated to individual operating segments.

ConocoPhillips holds a strong position among the world's largest exploration and production companies based on its production volumes and proved reserves. The company competes with major integrated oil corporations such as ExxonMobil Chevron TotalEnergies and BP as well as with independent peers like EOG Resources and Pioneer Natural Resources. Competitive advantages include a low cost of supply portfolio a diversified asset base across multiple geographies a disciplined investment framework and a robust balance sheet that supports through cycle dividend payments and share repurchases.

ConocoPhillips sells its production to a broad range of customers that include crude oil refiners natural gas utilities petrochemical manufacturers and industrial firms that use hydrocarbons as feedstock or fuel. The company also supplies liquefied natural gas to utilities and power generators under long term purchase agreements. While specific counterparty names are not disclosed in the filing the customer base spans North America Europe Asia and the Middle East.

DHR.profile_html:
Danaher Corporation is a global science and technology innovator that designs, manufactures, and markets products and services for the life sciences, diagnostics, and biotechnology sectors. The company enables scientific discovery, healthcare diagnostics, and the development and production of life-saving therapies through its advanced instrumentation, consumables, software, and integrated solutions. Danaher operates with a focus on innovation and operational excellence to support research, clinical decision-making, and biotherapeutic manufacturing worldwide.

Danaher generates revenue primarily through the sale of equipment, consumables, software, and related services across its three core business segments. Its products are used in laboratory research, clinical testing, and biopharmaceutical manufacturing processes. Revenue is derived from both product sales and recurring service contracts, with a strong emphasis on consumables that drive ongoing customer engagement. The company serves a diverse customer base including hospitals, clinical laboratories, research institutions, pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, and public health organizations globally.

Danaher operates through the following segments: Biotechnology, Life Sciences, and Diagnostics.

  • The Biotechnology segment provides equipment, consumables, and services for bioprocessing and discovery applications, supporting the research, development, and manufacturing of biological medicines such as monoclonal antibodies, vaccines, and cell and gene therapies. Its solutions are used by biopharmaceutical companies to advance therapies from early discovery through large-scale production.
  • The Life Sciences segment offers instruments, consumables, software, and services used to study biological molecules and cells, including DNA, RNA, proteins, and metabolites. Its products support basic research, drug discovery, and development, with applications in genomics, proteomics, cell analysis, and filtration technologies for industrial and scientific use.
  • The Diagnostics segment supplies clinical instruments, consumables, software, and services used in hospitals, physician offices, reference laboratories, and critical care settings to diagnose disease and guide treatment decisions. Its offerings include systems for hematology, immunodiagnostics, molecular testing, and pathology, enabling timely and accurate clinical insights.

Danaher holds a leading position in the life sciences and diagnostics industries, competing with major diversified healthcare and science companies such as Thermo Fisher Scientific, Roche, Siemens Healthineers, and Becton Dickinson. Its competitive advantages stem from a decentralized operating model, continuous investment in innovation through the Danaher Business System, and a strong portfolio of differentiated brands that enable rapid response to market needs and technological change.

The company serves hospitals, clinical and reference laboratories, physician offices, pharmaceutical and biotechnology manufacturers, academic and government research institutions, and public health agencies. Its customers rely on Danaher’s products for diagnostic testing, life science research, and the development and manufacturing of biologics and advanced therapies across the globe.

BBVA.profile_html:
Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S. A. is a customer-centric global financial services group founded in 1857, operating in the banking and financial services industry. The company provides a broad range of services including retail banking, asset management, wholesale banking, insurance, and digital banking solutions, with a strong focus on enhancing customer experience through online and mobile channels. BBVA places sustainability at the core of its strategy, integrating environmental and social considerations into its business operations and product offerings.

BBVA generates revenue primarily through net interest income from lending activities, fee and commission income from banking and asset management services, and trading income from financial markets. The company earns interest from loans and advances to customers, including mortgages, consumer loans, corporate financing, and public sector lending. Additionally, BBVA generates revenue from off-balance sheet funds such as mutual funds and pension funds, insurance premiums, and services related to corporate and investment banking, including capital markets and advisory services. Its revenue streams are diversified across its global operations, serving individual customers, small and medium-sized enterprises, large corporations, and public institutions.

The company operates through the following segments: Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, and Rest of Business.

  • Spain includes all banking and non-banking activities in Spain excluding those in the Corporate Center. It encompasses the Spanish Retail Network serving individual customers, private banking, small businesses, and domestic market clients; Corporate and Business Banking managing small and medium-sized enterprises, corporations, and public institutions; Corporate and Investment Banking handling large corporations, multinational groups, trading floor operations, and distribution activities in Spain; and other units including the insurance business in Spain (BBVA Seguros), asset management unit managing Spanish mutual funds and pension funds, lending to real estate developers, foreclosed real estate assets, and certain proprietary portfolios and structural interest-rate positions of the euro balance sheet not included in the Corporate Center.
  • Mexico comprises the banking, insurance, and asset management business conducted in Mexico by BBVA Mexico, including its agency in Houston. It provides retail and corporate banking services, insurance products, and asset management solutions to customers in Mexico, supported by a growing digital platform and mutual fund offerings that cater to higher-return investment demand.
  • Turkey consists of the activities of Garanti BBVA as an integrated financial services group operating in banking, insurance, and asset management in Turkey. It includes corporate, commercial, SME, payment systems, retail, private, and investment banking, along with subsidiaries in pension and life insurance, leasing, factoring, brokerage, asset management, and international operations in Romania and the Netherlands.
  • South America includes the Group’s banking, finance, insurance, and asset management business primarily in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela. It covers retail and corporate banking operations across these countries and insurance businesses in Argentina, Colombia, and Venezuela, with a focus on adapting to local economic conditions including hyperinflation environments in certain markets.
  • Rest of Business mainly includes wholesale banking activities in Europe (excluding Spain), the United States, and Asia through BBVA branches, as well as the Group’s digital banks in Italy and Germany. It serves institutional and corporate clients through cross-border lending, deposit taking, and financial market activities, supported by digital banking initiatives in European markets.

BBVA holds a strong position as one of the largest financial institutions in the eurozone and a leading bank in Spain, Mexico, and South America. It competes with major global and regional banks such as Santander, CaixaBank, BNP Paribas, HSBC, and Citigroup. The company’s competitive advantages include its diversified geographic footprint, early and sustained investment in digital transformation, strong brand recognition in key markets, and a balanced business model that combines traditional banking strengths with innovative fintech capabilities. Its focus on sustainability and responsible banking further differentiates it in an increasingly ESG-conscious investment landscape.

BBVA serves a diverse customer base including individual retail customers, small and medium-sized enterprises, large corporations, multinational groups, and public sector institutions. The company provides services to private banking clients, mortgage and consumer loan borrowers, credit card users, investors in mutual funds and pension funds, and policyholders through its insurance subsidiaries. Its digital platforms attract tech-savvy users seeking convenient, mobile-first banking experiences across its global markets.

UBS.profile_html:
UBS Group AG is a global financial services firm that provides wealth management, personal and corporate banking, asset management, and investment banking solutions to clients worldwide.

The company generates revenue primarily through fees and commissions from wealth management services, net interest income from lending and deposit activities, asset management fees, and trading and advisory revenues from its investment banking operations.

The company operates through the following segments: Global Wealth Management, Personal & Corporate Banking, Asset Management, Investment Bank, and Non core and Legacy.

  • Global Wealth Management provides advisory and discretionary portfolio management, investment funds, lending, and deposit services to high and ultra high net worth individuals and select institutional clients across the Americas, Asia Pacific, EMEA, and Switzerland.
  • Personal & Corporate Banking offers mortgages, loans, deposit products, payment services, and foreign exchange solutions to private, corporate, and institutional clients primarily in Switzerland.
  • Asset Management delivers investment capabilities including fund management, portfolio management, and alternative investment strategies to institutional and wholesale clients globally.

TJX.name: Tjx Companies Inc /De/
TJX.profile_html:
The TJX Companies, Inc. is the leading off price apparel and home fashions retailer in the United States and worldwide. It operates more than 5,200 stores and six ecommerce sites that offer a constantly changing assortment of branded, designer and quality merchandise at prices generally 20% to 60% below those of full price retailers.

The company generates revenue primarily from the sale of apparel, footwear, accessories and home fashions in its physical stores and through its ecommerce platforms. It purchases merchandise opportunistically to offer brand name and designer goods at discounted prices, which attracts a broad range of customers seeking value. Sales are driven by the frequent turnover of inventory and the treasure hunt shopping experience that encourages repeat visits.

The company operates through the following segments: Marmaxx, HomeGoods, TJX Canada, and TJX International.

  • Marmaxx operates the TJ Maxx and Marshalls chains in the United States, offering family apparel, footwear, accessories including beauty and jewelry, home fashions such as home basics, decorative accessories and giftware, and other merchandise through 2,603 stores and two ecommerce sites, tjmaxx.com and marshalls.com.
  • HomeGoods operates the HomeGoods and Homesense chains in the United States, providing an eclectic assortment of home fashions including furniture, rugs, lighting, soft home, decorative accessories, tabletop and cookware, as well as expanded pet and gourmet food departments from 963 HomeGoods stores and 79 Homesense stores.
  • TJX Canada runs the Winners, HomeSense and Marshalls chains in Canada, with Winners offering leading off price family apparel and home fashions, HomeSense providing home decor, furniture and seasonal home merchandise, and Marshalls delivering family apparel, footwear and home fashions from 316 Winners stores, 162 HomeSense stores and 111 Marshalls stores.
  • TJX International operates the TK Maxx and Homesense chains in Europe and the TK Maxx chain in Australia, with TK Maxx present in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, Poland, Austria, the Netherlands and, starting in March 2026, Spain through 673 stores and ecommerce sites tkmaxx.com, tkmaxx.de and tkmaxx.at, Homesense serving the United Kingdom and Ireland with 74 stores, and TK Maxx in Australia operating 88 stores.

The TJX Companies, Inc. holds a leading position in the off price retail sector, competing with department stores, specialty retailers, discount chains and online platforms that sell apparel and home fashions. Its competitive advantages include a flexible buying model that allows rapid inventory turnover, a strong global supplier network, and a treasure hunt shopping experience that drives frequent customer visits.

The company serves a broad range of consumers across income levels who seek value priced apparel, footwear, accessories and home fashions.

BUD.industry_secondary:
['Non-Alcoholic Beverages' 'Spirits and Wine'
 'Restaurant and Retail Software']
BUD.profile_html:
Anheuser-Busch InBev SA/NV is the world’s largest brewer by volume and one of the world’s top ten consumer products companies by revenue. The company produces markets distributes and sells a diversified portfolio of well over 400 beer and other malt beverage brands. Its brand list includes global names such as Budweiser Corona Stella Artois and Michelob ULTRA as well as numerous multi country and local labels. Operations span more than 40 countries with production facilities positioned close to consumer demand. As of 31 December 2025 the firm employed approximately 137 000 people and reported beer volumes of 484 million hectoliters. The company's history traces back more than 600 years of brewing tradition in Belgium and the United States. Over time it has built a portfolio that covers premium mainstream and value segments to suit different drinking occasions. Continuous investment in brewing technology and quality control supports the consistency of its products across markets.

Revenue is generated chiefly from the sale of beer and non beer beverages to wholesale distributors retailers and hospitality operators. The beer portfolio comprises core premium super premium and value segment brands that are sold in kegs cans bottles and draught formats. Non beer offerings consist of carbonated soft drinks spirits based beverages and energy drinks that are distributed through the same logistics network. Additional income streams arise from licensing arrangements digital commerce services and business to business platforms that support retailers and wholesalers. In 2025 total revenue amounted to USD 59.3 billion while non beer activities contributed roughly 11 percent of that total. The non beer segment has grown faster than the beer segment in recent years driven by rising demand for ready to drink cocktails and hard seltzers. Digital initiatives such as the BEES platform and direct to consumer channels generated over USD 1.3 billion of revenue in 2025. Licensing agreements with third party bottlers and distributors also add a modest but steady flow of income to the company.

Anheuser-Busch InBev SA/NV holds the number one market share position in more than 30 countries worldwide. According to IWSR data as of January 2026 the company ranks first in total beer volume ahead of Heineken China Resources and Carlsberg. Its competitive advantages derive from a truly global footprint that balances exposure to developed and developing markets. The scale of its operations enables strong negotiating power with suppliers and efficient allocation of marketing investments. A deep portfolio of over 400 brands provides flexibility to meet diverse consumer occasions and preferences. Continuous investment in innovation and digital tools further strengthens its ability to respond to changing trends. The firm leverages its extensive distribution network to launch new products quickly and efficiently across regions. Strong brand equity and consumer loyalty allow it to command premium pricing in many markets. Operational excellence programs such as Voyager Plant Optimization help reduce costs while maintaining quality standards. These factors together position Anheuser-Busch InBev as a leader in the global beer industry.

The company serves a broad customer base that includes wholesale distributors retail chains hospitality venues and institutional accounts. Specific partners named in the filing are Coca Cola PepsiCo and Red Bull. In Latin America the firm maintains long term agreements with PepsiCo for the bottling and distribution of brands such as Gatorade Lipton Ice Tea and H2OH. In North America it has distribution arrangements with Red Bull GmbH to sell energy drinks across several states. Additionally the firm works with numerous independent wholesalers and retailers who purchase its products for resale to end consumers. In Europe it supplies major supermarket chains and hospitality groups with its beer portfolio under long term supply contracts. In Asia Pacific the company partners with local distributors to reach modern trade outlets and traditional mom and pop stores. The company also provides beverages to sports venues music festivals and other large scale events through temporary distribution agreements. Its customer base spans individual consumers who buy single cans or bottles as well as large institutions that order pallets or truckloads. This diverse reach helps stabilize demand and supports the firm's goal of serving consumers on multiple occasions.

GLW.address_business: One Riverfront Plaza, Corning, 14831 New York, US
GLW.address_mailing: One Riverfront Plaza, Corning, 14831 New York, US
GLW.profile_html:
Corning Incorporated is a materials science company specializing in glass science ceramic science and optical physics to develop products for diverse industries. The company combines deep manufacturing and engineering expertise with research and development to create category-defining materials that transform sectors such as optical communications mobile consumer electronics display automotive solar semiconductor and life sciences. Corning leverages its long history of invention to solve complex challenges for customers worldwide.

Corning generates revenue by inventing making and selling products derived from its materials science capabilities. Primary revenue sources include optical communication fibers and cables display glass for televisions and devices specialty glass for mobile devices automotive glass and emissions control components life science laboratory equipment and polycrystalline silicon for solar applications. The company serves customers across technology industrial manufacturing and scientific sectors globally.

The company operates through the following segments: Optical Communications Display Specialty Materials Automotive Life Sciences and Hemlock and Emerging Growth Businesses.

  • Optical Communications provides optical fiber and cable solutions for telecommunications networks data centers and enterprise infrastructure supporting high-speed internet and cloud connectivity.
  • Display manufactures glass substrates for liquid crystal displays organic light-emitting diode displays and other visual technologies used in televisions smartphones tablets and monitors.
  • Specialty Materials produces advanced glass and ceramic products including cover glass for mobile devices glass for aerospace and defense applications and materials for semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Automotive supplies glazing solutions for passenger and commercial vehicles as well as emissions control technologies such as gasoline and diesel particulate filters for environmental systems.
  • Life Sciences offers laboratory products including cell culture microplates microfluidic devices and bioprocessing equipment used in drug discovery diagnostics and medical research.
  • Hemlock and Emerging Growth Businesses focuses on polycrystalline silicon production for solar energy and other emerging materials technologies under development.

Corning holds a leading position in several niche markets where its material science expertise creates high barriers to entry. The company competes with firms such as Schott AG in specialty glass Sumitomo Electric Industries in optical fiber and Asahi Glass in display substrates. Its competitive advantages stem from over 170 years of innovation in glass formulation proprietary manufacturing processes and a sustained investment in research and development that enables rapid response to evolving customer needs.

Corning serves a diverse customer base including telecommunications carriers original equipment manufacturers in consumer electronics and automotive semiconductor manufacturers solar panel producers pharmaceutical companies and research laboratories. Specific customers referenced in the filing include Samsung Display Co Ltd which participates in a share repurchase agreement with Corning.

SONY.name: Sony Group Corp
SONY.profile_html:
Sony Group Corporation is a diversified multinational conglomerate headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with operations spanning electronics, entertainment, financial services, and technology solutions. The company develops, manufactures, and markets a broad portfolio of products and services that include gaming hardware and software, music recordings and publishing, motion pictures and television content, televisions and audio-visual equipment, cameras, mobile devices, image sensors, and insurance and banking services. Sony Group Corporation operates globally through a network of subsidiaries and maintains a strong brand presence across consumer and professional markets.

Sony Group Corporation generates revenue through the sale of its products and services across multiple business segments. Revenue is derived from gaming consoles and software, network subscriptions, digital content distribution, recorded music sales, music publishing royalties, motion picture and television production and distribution, consumer electronics such as televisions and cameras, mobile communications devices, semiconductor image sensors, and financial products including life and non-life insurance policies and banking services. The company serves both individual consumers and business customers worldwide through direct sales, retail channels, online platforms, and partnerships with distributors and service providers.

The company operates through the following segments: Game & Network Services (G&NS), Music, Pictures, Entertainment Technology & Services (ET&S), Imaging & Sensing Solutions (I&SS), Financial Services, and All Other.

  • The Game & Network Services (G&NS) segment involves the production and sales of PlayStation hardware, digital software and add-on content, network services, and peripheral devices. Sony Interactive Entertainment LLC leads product development, marketing, distribution, and customer service for gaming consoles, bundled software, first-party and third-party titles, and online services such as the PlayStation Network.
  • The Music segment encompasses Recorded Music, Music Publishing, and Visual Media and Platform businesses. Recorded Music includes the global distribution of physical and digital music through Sony Music Entertainment and Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) Inc., along with revenue from live performances and merchandising. Music Publishing involves the management and licensing of musical compositions through Sony Music Publishing LLC, which administers rights and collects royalties. Visual Media and Platform includes animation production, game applications, and related services operated primarily by Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) Inc. and its affiliates such as Aniplex Inc.
  • The Pictures segment covers Motion Pictures, Television Productions, and Media Networks. Motion Pictures includes worldwide production, acquisition, and distribution of live-action and animated films through Sony Pictures Entertainment Inc., which owns studios such as Columbia Pictures, TriStar Pictures, and Sony Pictures Animation. Television Productions involves the creation and distribution of scripted and unscripted series, game shows, and made-for-television movies. Media Networks operates television networks and direct-to-consumer streaming services globally, including Crunchyroll for anime content and SonyLIV in India.
  • The Entertainment Technology & Services (ET&S) segment includes Televisions, Audio and Video, Still and Video Cameras, smartphone, and internet-related service businesses. Sony Corporation leads research, development, design, manufacturing, sales, distribution, and customer service for televisions, audio equipment, interchangeable lens and compact digital cameras, consumer and professional video cameras, mobile phones and accessories, and broadband network services through Sony Network Communications Inc.
  • The Imaging & Sensing Solutions (I&SS) segment focuses on complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors, display devices, lasers, and large-scale integration systems. Sony Semiconductor Solutions Corporation and its subsidiary Sony Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation lead product development, manufacturing, marketing, and sales of image sensors used in smartphones, digital cameras, security systems, factory automation, and automobiles.
  • The Financial Services segment primarily represents individual life insurance, non-life insurance, and banking operations in Japan through Sony Financial Group Inc., which wholly owns Sony Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Sony Assurance Inc., and Sony Bank Inc. Sony Life provides death protection and investment-oriented insurance products via its Lifeplanner sales specialists and independent agents. Sony Assurance offers automobile, fire, medical, and overseas travel insurance through direct marketing via internet and telephone. Sony Bank provides internet-based asset management, mortgages, and foreign currency deposits to individual customers.
  • All Other consists of various operating activities, including disc manufacturing and recording media businesses outside Japan. The Sony DADC group provides Ultra HD Blu-ray, Blu-ray Disc, DVD, and CD replication services along with digital and physical supply chain solutions. Sony Storage Media Solutions Corporation sells storage media products through its own sales force and Sony’s sales subsidiaries supporting the G&NS, ET&S, and I&SS segments.

Sony Group Corporation maintains a major competitive position in its core industries due to its strong brand recognition, product innovation, high-quality design, extensive global distribution network, and integrated ecosystem of hardware, software, and services. In gaming, it competes with Microsoft and Nintendo, leveraging exclusive titles and PlayStation Network services. In music, it faces Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group, relying on its global artist roster and publishing catalog. In pictures, it competes with Walt Disney Studios, Warner Bros., and Paramount, benefiting from its studio facilities and global reach. In televisions and audio-visual products, it contends with Samsung, LG, and Bose, emphasizing premium image quality and sound technology. In image sensors, it is a leading supplier alongside Samsung and OmniVision, known for high-performance CMOS sensors in mobile devices. In financial services, it competes with Japan Post Insurance, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, and Dai-ichi Life Holdings, differentiating through digital banking and consultant-driven insurance models.

Sony Group Corporation serves a diverse global customer base that includes individual consumers purchasing gaming consoles, music, movies, televisions, cameras, and smartphones; enterprise clients using image sensors in industrial and automotive applications; policyholders acquiring life and non-life insurance products in Japan; and banking customers utilizing Sony Bank’s digital asset management and mortgage services. The company also supplies storage media and disc replication services to business customers in media, entertainment, and data storage industries. Specific customer names are not disclosed in the filing, but Sony’s products and services reach end users through retail stores, online platforms, carrier partnerships, and direct-to-consumer channels across the Americas, Europe, China, Asia-Pacific, and other international markets.

UBER.name: Uber Technologies, Inc
UBER.profile_html:
Uber Technologies, Inc. operates a technology platform that connects riders with drivers for transportation services, eaters with restaurants and retailers for food and grocery delivery, and shippers with carriers for freight movement. The platform is supported by a global network of drivers, consumers, merchants, shippers, and carriers, along with proprietary technology for matching, routing, and payments. Uber’s services are available in over 70 countries and more than 15,000 cities worldwide, primarily in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia Pacific.

The company generates revenue primarily by taking a percentage of the gross bookings facilitated through its Mobility, Delivery, and Freight platforms. This core revenue is complemented by subscription fees from the Uber One membership program, which offers discounts and benefits across rides, deliveries, and grocery services. Advertising sales to brands and merchants, including sponsored placements in the Uber and Uber Eats apps, also contribute to revenue. Additionally, fees from financial partnership products and other value added services add to the overall income stream.

The company operates through the following segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. Each segment addresses a large, fragmented market and leverages the same underlying technology and network to drive synergies across the platform.

  • Mobility: Connects consumers with a variety of transportation options including ridesharing, carsharing, micromobility, vehicle rentals, public transit, and taxis. This segment also includes financial partnership products and advertising services that enhance the overall offering.
  • Delivery: Enables consumers to order meals, groceries, alcohol, and other retail items for delivery or pickup via Uber Eats and Uber Direct. The segment also provides advertising solutions for merchants and has expanded to include white label delivery as a service offerings.
  • Freight: Provides an on demand digital marketplace that matches shippers with carriers, offering real time booking, transparent pricing, and end to end visibility for freight shipments. The service operates principally in North America and Europe and serves customers ranging from small businesses to large enterprises.

BX.name: Blackstone Inc.
BX.address_business: 345 Park Avenue, New York, 10154 New York, US
BX.address_mailing: 345 Park Avenue, New York, 10154 New York, US
BX.profile_html:
Blackstone is the world's largest alternative asset manager. It seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies and assets in which it invests. As of December 31 2025 it reported approximately 1.3 trillion dollars in total assets under management across strategies that include real estate private equity infrastructure life sciences growth equity credit real assets secondaries and hedge funds. The firm employs a solutions oriented approach and leverages its scale diversified business long investment record rigorous process and strong client relationships to perform in various market conditions. Blackstone invests on behalf of pension funds insurance companies and individual investors aiming to fulfill its fiduciary duty by creating long term value. It strengthens portfolio companies real estate assets and other investments to help them thrive in the global economy. The firm had about 5285 employees including 268 senior managing directors with headquarters in New York and offices worldwide.

Blackstone generates revenue primarily through management fees and performance revenues. Management fees are charged as a percentage of assets under management or committed capital and are earned across its investment vehicles including private funds registered funds CLOs BDCs REITs and separately managed accounts. Performance revenues consist of incentive fees and carried interest that are paid when investment returns exceed predefined hurdles. The firm also receives advisory and transaction fees for services such as acquisitions origination and other deal related activities. In addition Blackstone invests its own capital alongside investor funds which can generate additional returns. These fee structures align the firm's interests with those of its clients and provide a steady stream of income tied to both asset levels and investment performance.

The company operates through the following segments: Real Estate Private Equity Credit & Insurance and Multi-Asset Investing.

  • The Real Estate segment manages approximately 319.3 billion dollars in assets under global real estate strategies. It operates as one integrated business with teams in the Americas Europe and Asia. Activities include opportunistic investments through Blackstone Real Estate Partners core plus strategies via Blackstone Property Partners and the non listed REIT Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust. The segment also runs debt strategies via Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies which invest in commercial mortgage loans and related securities across public and private markets. The business targets logistics data centers rental housing hospitality office retail properties and real estate operating companies seeking risk adjusted returns.
  • The Private Equity segment oversees about 416.4 billion dollars in assets and includes corporate private equity infrastructure secondaries capital markets services and private wealth platforms. Corporate private equity pursues global buyouts across sectors with funds such as Blackstone Capital Partners and sector focused strategies like Blackstone Energy Transition Partners. Infrastructure strategies consist of Blackstone Infrastructure Partners for institutional investors and Blackstone Infrastructure Strategies for individual investors. The secondaries business comprises Strategic Partners Fund Solutions and GP Stakes which acquire interests in existing funds and take minority stakes in general partners. Capital markets services provide placement and advisory functions. Private wealth platforms offer individuals access to private equity infrastructure and other alternatives through products such as Blackstone Total Alternatives Solution.
  • The Credit & Insurance segment manages roughly 443.0 billion dollars in assets and provides corporate and asset based credit solutions. It ranks among the largest managers of collateralized loan obligations and private credit. The segment is organized into private corporate credit liquid corporate credit and infrastructure and asset based credit strategies. Private corporate credit includes mezzanine direct lending and stressed/distressed funds. Liquid corporate credit focuses on CLOs and related funds. Infrastructure and asset based credit covers energy sustainable resources and loans secured by physical or real estate collateral. The insurance arm offers investment management for insurers and reinsurers seeking liability matched and capital efficient portfolios.
  • The Multi Asset Investing segment manages around 96.2 billion dollars in assets and is the world's largest discretionary allocator to hedge funds. It builds multi asset portfolios across public and private markets aiming for risk adjusted returns. The segment is divided into Absolute Return Multi Strategy Total Portfolio Management and Public Real Assets platforms. Absolute Return targets consistent performance across market environments. Multi Strategy pursues opportunistic asset agnostic investing. Total Portfolio Management oversees large scale total portfolios. Public Real Assets managed by Harvest Fund Advisors invests in publicly traded energy infrastructure renewables and master limited partnerships in North America.

Blackstone holds a leading position as the world's largest alternative asset manager with approximately 1.3 trillion dollars in AUM. It competes globally on the basis of investment performance transaction execution access to capital talent retention reputation product range innovation and pricing. The firm's scale diversified platform across multiple asset classes long investment track record rigorous investment process and strong client relationships are cited as key advantages that help it withstand varied market conditions and attract capital from institutional and individual investors.

Blackstone serves a diverse client base that includes public and corporate pension funds insurance companies sovereign wealth funds endowments foundations and high net worth as well as retail individual investors. Through its private wealth offerings the firm provides access to alternative strategies for accredited investors seeking diversification and long term growth. The company's investor relationships are built on its fiduciary focus and its ability to deliver returns across multiple market environments.

NOW.address_mailing: 2225 Lawson Lane, Santa Clara, 95054 California, US
NOW.profile_html:
ServiceNow, Inc. delivers solutions that help public and private organizations govern, secure and manage artificial intelligence and digitalize and streamline workflows to drive collaboration, productivity and better experiences across the enterprise. The company offers a cloud based platform that integrates AI, data and workflow automation to create intelligent processes. Its core technology enables organizations to connect insights from AI models to operational systems where work gets done. ServiceNow, Inc. serves a broad range of industries by providing tools that improve IT operations, customer service, HR, finance and other back office functions.

ServiceNow, Inc. generates revenue primarily through subscription fees for access to its platform and related products. Customers pay for modules covering technology operations, customer relationship management, core business processes and creator tools. The company also offers consumption based pricing for certain AI and data services when usage exceeds included service credits. Professional services, customer support and the ServiceNow Impact offering contribute additional revenue streams. The majority of sales come from enterprise customers seeking to automate workflows and enhance productivity.

The company operates through the following segments: Technology, Customer Relationship Management and Industry, Core Business, and Creator and Other.

  • Technology segment includes products that help IT departments manage infrastructure, security, risk and service delivery. It covers IT asset management, IT operations management, IT service management, operational technology management, risk management and security operations. These tools enable organizations to monitor devices, detect vulnerabilities, automate incident response and ensure compliance with policies.
  • Customer Relationship Management and Industry segment provides solutions for front office customer service, field service, sales and order management and industry specific workflows. It includes customer service management, field service management, sales and order management and tailored offerings for sectors such as financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, public sector, retail, technology and telecommunications. These products help organizations manage customer interactions, optimize resource allocation and improve service efficiency.
  • Core Business segment supports human resources, legal, finance, facilities and related back office functions. It comprises HR service delivery, legal and contract operations, source to pay operations and workplace service delivery. These products automate routine tasks such as onboarding, leave management, contract handling, procurement and facility maintenance while providing visibility across processes.
  • Creator and Other segment offers low code development tools, data fabric capabilities and privacy and security controls. It includes App Engine, Workflow Data Fabric, RaptorDB and platform privacy and security products. These tools enable users to build custom applications, integrate internal and external data and protect sensitive information in the cloud.

ServiceNow, Inc. holds a strong position in the enterprise software market as a provider of a unified platform that combines AI, data and workflow automation. The company competes with large vendors such as Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, Salesforce and Workday as well as with niche AI focused entrants and custom built solutions. Its competitive advantages stem from long term relationships with customers, deep knowledge of how work flows across organizations and a cloud based architecture that supports scalability and security. The ability to connect AI generated insights to operational processes differentiates ServiceNow from pure AI analytics providers.

ServiceNow, Inc. serves approximately eight thousand seven hundred enterprise customers across a wide range of industries. Its customer base includes global energy companies, major digital sports entertainment platforms, tax compliance software providers and numerous government agencies. The company reports that a growing share of revenue comes from sales to public sector clients. These organizations rely on ServiceNow to automate workflows, improve service delivery and enhance productivity.

PBR.name: Petrobras - Petroleo Brasileiro Sa
PBR.address_business: Avenida Republica Do Chile 65, Rio De Janerio Rj Br
PBR.address_mailing: Avenida Republica Do Chile 65, Rio De Janerio Rj Br
PBR.profile_html:
Petrobras - Petroleo Brasileiro Sa is an integrated energy company engaged in the exploration, production, refining, transportation, marketing, and distribution of oil, natural gas, and related products. The company operates primarily in Brazil and maintains a significant presence across the entire hydrocarbon value chain, from upstream field development to downstream retail sales. Its core activities include developing offshore and onshore hydrocarbon reserves, processing crude oil into refined fuels, and supplying energy products to domestic and international markets.

Petrobras generates revenue through the sale of crude oil, natural gas, refined petroleum products such as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel, as well as petrochemical feedstocks and lubricants. The company serves a diverse customer base that includes industrial consumers, transportation companies, power generators, and retail distributors. Revenue is derived from both domestic sales within Brazil and export operations targeting international markets, particularly in the Americas and Europe.

The company operates through the following segments: Exploration and Production, Refining, Transportation and Marketing, Gas and Low Carbon Energies, and Corporate and Other Activities.

  • The Exploration and Production segment focuses on the discovery, development, and production of crude oil and natural gas reserves, primarily in Brazil’s offshore basins including the pre-salt fields, and includes activities such as drilling, reservoir management, and field operations.
  • The Refining, Transportation and Marketing segment encompasses the refining of crude oil into transportation fuels and other petroleum products, the logistics of transporting crude and products via pipelines, tankers, and storage facilities, and the marketing and distribution of these products through a network of branded retail outlets and wholesale channels.
  • The Gas and Low Carbon Energies segment is involved in the production, processing, trading, and commercialization of natural gas, as well as the development of low-carbon energy solutions including biofuels, wind power, solar energy, and carbon capture initiatives aimed at supporting the energy transition.
  • The Corporate and Other Activities segment includes functions such as corporate governance, financial management, strategic planning, legal affairs, and centralized services that support the operational segments but do not generate significant standalone revenue.

Petrobras holds a dominant position in Brazil’s oil and gas industry as the nation’s largest producer and a key player in Latin America’s energy sector. The company competes with international majors such as ExxonMobil, Chevron, and TotalEnergies in upstream operations, while facing competition from regional refiners and distributors in downstream markets. Its competitive advantages include extensive offshore expertise, particularly in deep-water and pre-salt environments, a fully integrated value chain, and significant scale in reserves and refining capacity.

The company serves a broad customer base encompassing industrial manufacturers, agribusinesses, utility providers, transportation fleets, and commercial enterprises across Brazil. It also supplies fuel and lubricants to aviation and maritime sectors. Retail consumers are served through its extensive network of service stations operating under the Petrobras brand, which fuels millions of vehicles daily throughout the country.

MFG.name: Mizuho Financial Group Inc
MFG.profile_html:
Mizuho Financial Group, Inc. is a Japanese financial holding company that provides banking, trust banking, securities and related financial services. The company operates primarily in Japan but also maintains a substantial presence in Asia, the Americas and Europe through its subsidiaries and branches.

Revenue is generated from interest earned on loans and deposits, fees for trust and asset management services, commissions from securities trading and underwriting, and income from other financial activities such as advisory and transaction banking. The firm serves a broad range of customers including individual consumers, small and medium sized enterprises, large corporations, financial institutions and public sector entities. Its diversified business model allows it to capture income across multiple product lines and geographic regions.

The company operates through the following segments: Retail & Business Banking Company, Corporate & Investment Banking Company, Global Corporate & Investment Banking Company, Global Markets Company, Asset Management Company.

  • Retail & Business Banking Company: This segment serves individual customers, small and medium sized enterprises and middle market corporations by offering integrated banking, trust banking and securities consulting, loan products, asset management support and succession planning services.
  • Corporate & Investment Banking Company: This segment provides customized financing, fund management, equity and bond underwriting, mergers and acquisitions advisory, real estate and pension solutions to large companies, financial institutions and public sector bodies in Japan.
  • Global Corporate & Investment Banking Company: This segment supports Japanese companies operating abroad and non Japanese companies with cross border financing, LCM DCM structures and advisory services that leverage the group’s global network.
  • Global Markets Company: This segment engages in sales and trading of securities, derivatives and other market products, provides risk hedging and asset management services, and conducts ALM and investment activities for institutional and retail investors.
  • Asset Management Company: This segment manages assets for individuals and institutional investors through its subsidiary Asset Management One Co., Ltd. and offers investment products, advisory services and solutions that incorporate environmental, social and governance considerations.

Mizuho Financial Group, Inc. ranks among Japan’s three largest banking groups, often referred to as a mega bank, and holds a significant share of the domestic market for corporate lending, retail banking and securities underwriting. The firm competes with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, other regional banks, trust banks, securities houses and a range of non bank financial providers. Its competitive strengths stem from a full service platform that combines banking, trust banking and securities capabilities, a strong international franchise and a focus on sustainability initiatives that enhance its reputation with clients and investors.

The company’s customer base encompasses millions of individual retail clients, hundreds of thousands of corporate borrowers and a wide variety of institutional investors. Specific partners referenced in the filing include Rakuten Card Co., Ltd., Golub Capital and State Street Corporation, illustrating its relationships with payment processors, alternative asset managers and global custodians. In addition, Mizuho serves government agencies, public sector entities and numerous multinational corporations that rely on its cross border financing and advisory expertise.

UL.profile_html:
Unilever PLC is a global consumer goods company that manufactures and markets a broad portfolio of products across beauty and wellbeing, personal care, home care, foods, and ice cream. The company operates in both developed and emerging markets, leveraging its scale and brand strength to serve consumers worldwide. Its business model focuses on driving growth through power brands, innovation, and category-focused organisation to meet evolving consumer needs.

Unilever generates revenue primarily through the sale of its consumer goods to retailers, distributors, and other business customers worldwide. The company's turnover, which reached €60.8 billion in 2024, consists of sales of goods after deducting discounts, sales taxes, and estimated returns. Revenue is driven by its 30 power brands, which account for over 75% of turnover and are concentrated in 24 top markets representing around 85% of total sales.

The company operates through the following segments: Beauty & Wellbeing, Personal Care, Home Care, Foods, and Ice Cream.

  • Beauty & Wellbeing: This segment primarily includes sales of hair care products such as shampoo, conditioner, and styling aids, as well as skin care products including face, hand, and body moisturisers. It also encompasses Prestige Beauty and Wellbeing offerings. Key brands in this segment include Dove, Tresemmé, and Vaseline, which are recognised for their strong market presence and consumer trust across multiple regions.
  • Personal Care: This segment focuses on sales of skin cleansing products like soap and shower gels, deodorants, and oral care items such as toothpaste, toothbrushes, and mouthwash. It serves daily hygiene needs through trusted brands that are widely distributed. Notable brands in this segment include Lifebuoy, Rexona, and Signal, which are leaders in their respective categories and support the segment's consistent performance.
  • Home Care: This segment primarily involves sales of fabric care products such as washing powders and liquids, rinse conditioners, and a wide range of home and hygiene cleaning products. It addresses household cleaning and maintenance needs through effective and trusted solutions. CB.name: Chubb Ltd
CB.profile_html:
Chubb Limited is a global insurance and reinsurance organization headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, that serves a diverse client base across 54 countries and territories. The company provides commercial and consumer property and casualty (P&C) insurance, accident and health (A&H) coverage, reinsurance, and life insurance products. As of December 31, 2025, Chubb reported total assets of $272 billion and shareholders’ equity of $74 billion. Its operations encompass risk management, loss control, engineering, and specialized lines such as directors and officers, aviation, energy, and surety. Chubb emphasizes underwriting discipline, seeking to earn profits through prudent risk selection rather than pursuing volume for its own sake.

Chubb generates revenue primarily from three sources: P&C underwriting income, investment income, and life segment income. In 2025, consolidated net premiums earned amounted to $53.0 billion, reflecting premiums collected from its broad portfolio of insurance contracts. Investment income is derived from a disciplined, investment‑grade fixed‑income portfolio supplemented by limited partnerships and funds, with a focus on maintaining liquidity and credit quality. Life segment income includes both insurance contract earnings from mortality and morbidity risks and investment contract fees from policyholder deposits. Together, these streams drive the company’s profitability and support its capital‑return objectives.

The company operates through the following segments: North America Commercial P&C Insurance, North America Personal P&C Insurance, North America Agricultural Insurance, Overseas General Insurance, Global Reinsurance, and Life Insurance.

  • North America Commercial P&C Insurance: provides P&C and A&H insurance and services to large, middle‑market, and small commercial businesses in the U. S., Canada, and Bermuda. This segment includes commercial insurance, major accounts, wholesale specialty, and Bermuda high‑excess lines, each targeting distinct client groups and risk profiles.
  • North America Personal P&C Insurance: offers homeowners, automobile, valuable articles, personal excess liability, travel, cyber, and recreational marine insurance to affluent and high‑net‑worth individuals and families in the U. S. and Canada. The segment focuses on high‑value personal lines that exceed the capabilities of mass‑market carriers.
  • North America Agricultural Insurance: delivers crop insurance, primarily Multiple Peril Crop Insurance and crop‑hail, through Rain and Hail, and farm‑and‑ranch specialty P&C coverages via the Chubb Agribusiness unit in the U. S. and Canada. It also supplies commercial agribusiness coverages for companies that manufacture, process, or distribute agricultural products.
  • Overseas General Insurance: encompasses Chubb International’s retail commercial and consumer lines, the wholesale specialty business of Chubb Global Markets, and the international supplemental A&H business. Operations span Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Asia, and Latin America, offering both admitted and surplus‑lines products through brokers, agents, and digital platforms.
  • Global Reinsurance: provides traditional and non‑traditional reinsurance coverage worldwide through Chubb Tempest Re units in Bermuda, the USA, International, and Canada. The segment focuses on property catastrophe, casualty, and specialty lines, leveraging Chubb’s capital strength and analytical capabilities to serve primary insurers.
  • Life Insurance: comprises international life operations (Chubb Life), including Huatai Life, Chubb Life Re, and Chubb Benefits, offering protection and savings products such as term life, universal, unit‑linked, annuities, and asset management services. The segment’s core markets are in Asia, with additional presence in Egypt and select Latin American countries through joint distribution models.

Chubb ranks among the largest global property and casualty insurers, distinguished by its diversified product mix, strong capital base, and consistent underwriting discipline. The company competes with major multinational insurers such as Allianz, AXA, Zurich Insurance Group, and Berkshire Hathaway, as well as regional players and Lloyd’s syndicates in specific lines. Its competitive advantages include sophisticated risk selection, a reputation for superior claims service, a global platform that enables multinational account servicing, and the ability to offer integrated P&C, A&H, and life solutions. This breadth of offerings and geographic reach provides stability across market cycles and supports long‑term book‑value growth.

Chubb serves multinational corporations, mid‑size and small businesses, affluent and high‑net‑worth individuals, and consumers purchasing personal lines such as homeowners and automobile coverage. The company also supplies accident and health programs to employers and affinity groups, and provides reinsurance to primary insurers seeking capacity protection. Its client base spans a wide range of industries, including construction, manufacturing, technology, finance, and healthcare, reflecting Chubb’s ability to tailor solutions to varied risk profiles.

PLD.address_mailing: Pier 1 Bay 1, San Francisco, 94111 California, US
PLD.profile_html:
Prologis, Inc. is a self administered and self managed real estate investment trust that owns manages and develops high quality logistics facilities worldwide.

The company generates revenue primarily from rental income collected from tenants under operating leases and from fees earned for managing properties and providing development and asset management services to its joint venture partners.

The company operates through the following segments: Real Estate and Strategic Capital.

  • Real Estate segment includes rental operations and development activities. It earns rent from tenants leasing logistics space and generates income from developing new properties including logistics facilities and data centers that are leased to customers or contributed to joint ventures.
  • Strategic Capital segment provides asset management property management leasing acquisition construction management and disposition services to unconsolidated joint ventures and earns fees including promote income based on the performance of those ventures.

Prologis, Inc. holds a leading position in the global logistics real estate market with a presence in twenty countries across four continents. Its competitive advantages include a large scale portfolio of approximately 1.3 billion square feet strategic locations near major consumer markets a diversified tenant base and a platform of services under the Prologis Essentials brand that addresses operational energy and sustainability needs. The company also benefits from a strong balance sheet low leverage and access to capital through its joint venture partnerships.

The company serves a diverse base of more than four thousand customers ranging from multinational corporations to regional and local logistics providers. Its top tenants include Amazon Home Depot FedEx UPS DHL Walmart and other major retailers and logistics firms that occupy significant portions of its leased space.
