BMY.address_mailing: Route 206 And Province Line Road, Princeton, 08543 New Jersey, US
BMY.profile_html:
Bristol-Myers Squibb Company is engaged in the discovery, development, licensing, manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of innovative medicines that help patients prevail over serious diseases. The company operates as a biopharmaceutical firm focused on transformational therapies in oncology, hematology, immunology, cardiovascular, neuroscience and other therapeutic areas where it aims to create long-term value.

Bristol-Myers Squibb generates revenue primarily through the sale of its portfolio of innovative medicines across multiple therapeutic areas. Key products include Opdivo, Yervoy, Orencia, Reblozyl, Breyanzi, Opdualag, Camzyos, Zeposia, Abecma, Sotyktu, Krazati, Cobenfy, Eliquis, Revlimid, Pomalyst, Sprycel and Abraxane. These medicines are sold worldwide to wholesalers, distributors, specialty pharmacies, retailers, hospitals, clinics, government agencies and, to a lesser extent, directly to patients.

The company operates through a single segment engaged in the discovery, development, licensing, manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of innovative medicines.

  • The single segment encompasses all activities related to the discovery, development, licensing, manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of innovative medicines that help patients prevail over serious diseases.

Bristol-Myers Squibb competes with other global research-based drug companies, smaller research companies with limited therapeutic focus and generic drug manufacturers. The company leverages its scale, resources and capability as a large pharmaceutical firm combined with the speed, agility and innovation focus typical of the biotech industry to maintain a competitive advantage in developing transformational medicines.

Bristol-Myers Squibb serves wholesalers, distributors, specialty pharmacies, retailers, hospitals, clinics, government agencies and patients.

NET.profile_html:
Cloudflare Inc provides a cloud based network that delivers security performance and reliability services to organizations worldwide. Its platform integrates application services SASE developer tools and consumer products to help customers secure and optimize their internet facing applications and infrastructure.

The company generates revenue primarily through subscriptions to its paid plans including enterprise contracted customers and pay as you go customers. Revenue comes from its suite of products covering application security and performance SASE network and security solutions developer based compute storage and AI offerings and consumer services. Sales are made via direct sales channel partners and a self service web portal.

The company operates through the following segments.

  • Application Services provides security and performance solutions such as web application firewall bot management DDoS mitigation API security SSL TLS encryption content delivery load balancing DNS and related tools to protect and accelerate internet applications.
  • SASE Platform combines Zero Trust network services like Magic WAN Magic Transit Magic Firewall and Secure Web Gateway with access controls to deliver secure connectivity and security for corporate networks.
  • Developer based Solutions offers serverless compute storage databases AI and media tools including Workers R2 KV D1 Vectorize Queues Stream and Images to enable developers to build and run applications on Cloudflare's network.
  • Consumer Offerings provides free and paid consumer products such as the 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver WARP VPN and domain registrar to give individuals a private and performant internet experience.

Cloudflare is a leader in the connectivity and edge cloud market competing with traditional network hardware vendors point solution providers and major public cloud providers. Its competitive advantages include a globally distributed network an integrated security and performance suite a developer friendly programmable platform and a free tier that drives network scale and lowers costs.

The company serves a diverse range of customers across industries and geographies including technology healthcare financial services retail manufacturing government and non profit organizations. As of December 31 2025 it had approximately 332,000 paying customers in over 190 countries with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue. It also serves millions of free users through its consumer products.

PH.name: Parker-Hannifin Corp
PH.profile_html:
Parker Hannifin Corporation is a global leader in motion and control technologies. The company designs manufactures and provides aftermarket support for highly engineered solutions that serve markets such as aerospace and defense in plant and industrial equipment transportation off highway energy and HVAC and refrigeration. Parker Hannifin Corporation operates through a decentralized structure that fosters close customer relationships and employee engagement. Its business system known as The Win Strategy TM guides goals for engaged people customer experience profitable growth and financial performance.

Parker Hannifin Corporation generates revenue by selling hundreds of thousands of individual part numbers across its two business segments. The firm derives income from the sale of motion control components fluid handling products sealing solutions valves pumps actuators filters and related aftermarket services. Revenue comes primarily from original equipment manufacturers and distributors who serve the replacement markets. In fiscal year 2025 the company reported net sales of approximately nineteen point nine billion dollars with the Diversified Industrial Segment contributing sixty nine percent and the Aerospace Systems Segment contributing thirty one percent.

The company operates through the following segments: Diversified Industrial and Aerospace Systems.

  • Diversified Industrial Segment sells highly engineered differentiated products to original equipment manufacturers and distributors who serve aftermarket replacement markets. The segment serves aerospace and defense off highway in plant industrial equipment energy transportation and HVAC and refrigeration verticals. Its product portfolio includes vibration control high purity sealing coatings cryogenic valves and fittings HVAC/R controls and monitoring elastomeric fabric reinforced metal and precision cut seals hydrogen and natural gas filters electric and hydraulic pumps and motors industrial air and gas filtration electric and hydraulic valves miniature pumps and valves electromagnetic interface shielding pneumatic actuators regulators and valves electromechanical and hydraulic actuators power take offs electronics drives and controllers process filtration solutions engine filtration solutions rubber to substrate adhesives fluid condition monitoring sensors and diagnostics fluid conveyance hose and tubing structural adhesives high pressure connectors fittings valves and regulators thermal management high purity fittings valves and regulators. The segment offers both standard and custom engineered products marketed through field sales employees and independent distributors worldwide.
  • Aerospace Systems Segment sells highly engineered differentiated airframe and engine components and systems to original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket users primarily in the commercial aerospace and defense markets. The segment serves commercial transport regional transport defense fixed wing helicopters business jets and energy platforms. Its product line includes avionics fuel systems and components electric and hydraulic braking systems fuel tank inerting systems electric power hydraulic pumps and motors electromechanical actuators hydraulic valves and actuators engine exhaust systems and components pneumatics fire detection and suppression seals flight control systems sensors fluid conveyance and thermal management. Marketing is conducted through regional sales organizations that sell directly to original equipment manufacturers and end users worldwide.

Parker Hannifin Corporation holds a strong position in the motion and control industry due to its broad product range and global footprint. The company faces hundreds of competitors across its various markets with competition varying by product line end market and geography. In the Diversified Industrial Segment Parker competes on product quality innovation customer experience manufacturing and distribution capability aftermarket support and price competitiveness and is considered a market leader in many major markets for its core products. Primary global competitors in this segment include Bosch Rexroth AG Danaher Corporation Danfoss A/S Donaldson Company Inc Emerson Climate Technologies Inc Emerson ASCO Festo AG Co Freudenberg NOK Gates Corporation IMI Norgren SMC Corporation Swagelok Company and Trelleborg AB though none of these rivals covers the full breadth of Parker offerings. In the Aerospace Systems Segment the company leverages advanced technology engineering capabilities quality delivery service and price competitiveness to win original equipment business and aftermarket support on aircraft programs. Key competitors in this segment are Crane Co Eaton Corporation plc Honeywell International Inc Moog Inc RTX Corporation Safran S A Senior plc Triumph Group Inc and Woodward Inc. Across both segments Parker advantages stem from its wide ranging core technology portfolio covering hydraulics pneumatics electromechanical filtration fluid and gas handling process control engineered materials and climate control as well as its Win Strategy business system interconnected technology deep customer partnerships application engineering expertise global distribution network and decentralized operating structure.

Parker Hannifin Corporation serves a broad base of original equipment manufacturers and distributors that together represent several hundred thousand customer locations worldwide. The company’s customers span aerospace and defense manufacturers industrial equipment builders transportation vehicle producers off highway machinery makers energy sector firms and HVAC and refrigeration equipment suppliers. In addition Parker provides aftermarket parts and services to end users who maintain and operate the equipment supplied by its OEM clients.

PGR.profile_html:
Progressive Corporation is a provider of personal and commercial automobile insurance, specialty property-casualty insurance, and related services. The company operates primarily in the United States insurance market, offering a range of products through independent agents, direct-to-consumer channels, and online platforms. It focuses on underwriting profitability while maintaining a strong brand presence through distinctive advertising and marketing efforts.

Progressive Corporation generates revenue primarily through the collection of insurance premiums from policyholders across its personal and commercial lines businesses. Revenue is derived from writing policies that provide coverage for auto, home, condo, renters, motorcycle, boat, and commercial vehicles, among other risks. The company also earns investment income from its fixed-income and equity portfolios, which supports overall financial performance.

The company operates through the following segments: Personal Lines and Commercial Lines.

  • Personal Lines: This segment provides insurance products for individual consumers, including personal auto, homeowners, condo, renters, motorcycle, boat, and umbrella policies. The Personal Lines segment is distributed through independent insurance agents, direct response via phone and internet, and online quote and purchase platforms. Progressive offers well-known brands and services such as the Snapshot program, which uses telematics to personalize rates based on driving behavior, and the Name Your Price® tool, which helps customers find coverage within their budget.
  • Commercial Lines: This segment provides insurance solutions for businesses, including commercial auto, general liability, property, workers' compensation, and specialty coverages for industries such as transportation, contracting, and retail. The Commercial Lines segment serves customers through independent agents and brokerage channels, focusing on small to medium-sized businesses. Progressive offers trademarked offerings like the Progressive Commercial brand and specialized programs for transportation network company drivers and fleet operators.

Progressive Corporation holds a competitive position as one of the largest auto insurers in the United States, known for its innovative use of technology and data in underwriting and customer engagement. The company competes with major national carriers such as State Farm, Allstate, and GEICO, as well as regional insurers and emerging insurtech firms. Its competitive advantages include a strong direct-to-consumer platform, advanced predictive modeling, and a commitment to underwriting discipline reflected in its target combined ratio.

Progressive Corporation serves a diverse customer base that includes individual consumers seeking personal auto and property insurance, as well as small and medium-sized businesses requiring commercial coverage. The company reaches customers through independent agents, direct sales via phone and website, and mobile applications. Specific customer groups include transportation network company drivers, fleet operators, contractors, and retail business owners who rely on Progressive for tailored insurance solutions.

NEM.profile_html:
Newmont Corporation is primarily a gold producer with significant operations and assets across the United States, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Ghana, Suriname, Argentina, Dominican Republic, Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Mexico, and Canada. In addition to gold, the company extracts copper, silver, lead, and zinc as byproducts of its mining activities. Newmont reports attributable proven and probable gold reserves of 118.2 million ounces, measured and indicated gold resources of 88.1 million ounces, and inferred gold resources of 60.6 million ounces. It also maintains an aggregate land position of approximately 19,200 square miles (49,800 square kilometers). In November 2023, Newmont completed the acquisition of Newcrest, adding additional gold and copper assets in Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia to its portfolio. As part of a portfolio optimization program announced in February 2024, the company has divested several non core assets, including Telfer, CC&V, Musselwhite, Éléonore, Porcupine, Akyem, and the Coffee development project, with most sales completed by the end of 2025. As the world’s leading gold company, Newmont emphasizes sustainable and responsible mining practices to create long term value for shareholders and host communities.

Newmont generates revenue from the sale of gold, copper, silver, lead, and zinc concentrates and refined metals to smelters, refiners, banks, jewelers, and industrial users worldwide. The company’s sales volumes depend on the amount of metal produced at its mines and the prevailing market prices for each commodity. Revenue is recognized when control of the product transfers to the customer, which typically occurs upon delivery or under provisional pricing arrangements that are later finalized based on average market prices. Newmont also earns incidental income from services such as contract mining and toll processing, although metal sales constitute the overwhelming majority of total revenue. The inclusion of Newcrest’s operations has increased the company’s overall production capacity and diversified its geographic revenue streams. Revenue from copper and by product metals contributes a smaller but notable share of total sales.

The company operates through the following segments.

  • Nevada Gold Mines: This segment represents Newmont's 38.5% proportionate interest in the Nevada Gold Mines joint venture, which includes multiple gold producing mines in Nevada, United States, and is not directly managed by Newmont.
  • Ahafo North: This segment comprises the Ahafo North gold project in Ghana, which achieved commercial production in October 2025 and involves the extraction and processing of gold ore.

Newmont holds a leading position in the global gold industry, often ranked as the top producer by annual output. Its principal competitors include Barrick Gold Corporation, AngloGold Ashanti Ltd., Gold Fields Limited, and Kinross Gold Corporation. Competitive advantages stem from its large and diversified reserve base, extensive geographic footprint, operational scale, and commitment to sustainable mining practices. The company’s size allows it to achieve cost efficiencies and invest in long term projects. The production of copper, silver, lead, and zinc as byproducts provides additional revenue streams that complement gold sales. Newmont’s commitment to safety and environmental stewardship supports its social license to operate in diverse jurisdictions.

Newmont's customer base consists of smelters, refiners, banks, jewelers, and industrial users that purchase its metal concentrates and refined products. Smelters and refiners transform the concentrates into pure metal for further processing, while banks may acquire gold bullion for investment or reserve purposes. Jewelers use gold and silver for fabrication of finished goods, and industrial users employ the metals in electronics, dentistry, and other applications. The company serves a diversified international clientele across multiple sectors, reducing reliance on any single customer or region. Long term contracts and spot market sales both feature in Newmont’s revenue mix. The company maintains relationships with a range of counterparties, including major financial institutions and industrial manufacturers.

SNOW.profile_html:
Snowflake delivers a cloud based platform that enables organizations to consolidate data into a single source of truth run analytics develop artificial intelligence applications and share data securely. The platform is built on an architecture that separates storage, compute, and cloud services allowing each layer to scale independently. It runs on three major public clouds across fifty three regional deployments worldwide. Snowflake’s AI Data Cloud connects customers, partners, developers, data providers, and data consumers to break down silos and derive value from a growing number of data sets. The storage layer ingests massive amounts of varied data, the compute layer provides dedicated resources for concurrent queries, and the cloud services layer enables secure use of AI within applications.

Revenue is generated primarily through a consumption based model where customers pay for storage, compute, and cloud services usage. The company offers product categories that include analytics, data engineering, artificial intelligence, applications, collaboration, and transactions. In the fiscal year ended January 31 2026 Snowflake recorded total revenue of $4.7 billion representing a twenty nine percent increase over the prior year. Revenue for the fiscal years ended January 31 2025 and January 31 2024 was $3.6 billion and $2.8 billion respectively each reflecting twenty nine percent year over year growth. Net loss was $1.3 billion for the fiscal year ended January 31 2026 and $1.3 billion for the prior year and $838.0 million for the fiscal year ended January 31 2024. The company also reports a high net revenue retention rate indicating that existing customers increase their usage over time.

Snowflake competes in the cloud data platform market against large public cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. Other competitors include legacy database vendors, specialized observability providers, and emerging entrants. The company differentiates itself through a purpose built cloud architecture that can ingest structured, semi structured, and unstructured data at scale. It supports multiple workloads on a single platform enabling seamless sharing of data across public clouds and regions without moving underlying data. Snowflake offers transparent consumption based pricing and elastic scaling that matches demand. Its platform provides interoperability with open formats, tools, and programming languages including Python, Java, and Scala. Customers benefit from a consistent experience across multiple public clouds without being locked into a single provider. The service includes built in security features such as encryption, role based access control, and multi factor authentication. These capabilities help Snowflake maintain a strong position in a rapidly evolving industry.

Snowflake serves organizations of all sizes across a broad range of industries including financial services, advertising, media and entertainment, retail and consumer goods, healthcare and life sciences, manufacturing, technology, telecom, travel and hospitality, and the public sector. As of January 31 2026 the company reported 13,328 total customers up from 10,996 a year earlier. Among these customers 790 were listed in the Forbes Global 2000 and they contributed approximately 43% of revenue for the fiscal year ended January 31 2026. The number of customers generating more than $1.0 million in trailing twelve month product revenue rose from 576 to 733 over the same period. Snowflake’s net revenue retention rate stood at 125% as of January 31 2026 indicating expansion within the existing customer base. Snowflake also provides industry specific offerings such as the AI Data Cloud for financial services, healthcare, and retail to address specialized needs.

COF.profile_html:
Capital One Financial Corporation is a diversified financial services holding company with banking and non-banking subsidiaries. It operates as a global payments provider and diversified financial institution delivering a broad array of financial products and services to consumers, small businesses, and commercial clients through digital channels, branch locations, cafés, and other distribution channels. Its principal operating subsidiary is Capital One National Association. The company is one of the nation’s largest banks based on deposits and the largest issuer of credit cards in the United States based on outstanding credit card loan balances as of December 31, 2025.

Capital One Financial Corporation generates revenue primarily from lending to consumer and commercial customers net of funding costs associated with deposits, long-term debt, and other borrowings. It also earns non-interest income consisting of discount and interchange income net of reward expenses, and service charges and other customer-related fees. Revenue is derived from credit card products, debit cards, bank lending, treasury management, depository services, auto loans, consumer lending products, personal loans, and services from the Global Payment Network which includes the Discover Network, PULSE Network, Diners Club International, and Network Partners.

The company operates through the following segments: Credit Card, Consumer Banking, and Commercial Banking.

  • Credit Card: Consists of domestic consumer card lending, personal loans, domestic small business card lending, and international card businesses in the United Kingdom and Canada.
  • Consumer Banking: Consists of deposit gathering and lending activities for consumers and small businesses, national auto lending, and services offered by the Global Payment Network.
  • Commercial Banking: Consists of lending, deposit gathering, capital markets, and treasury management services to commercial real estate and commercial and industrial customers, typically serving companies with annual revenues between $20 million and $2 billion.

Capital One Financial Corporation operates in a highly competitive environment across all business segments. Its Credit Card business competes with international, national, regional, and local issuers of Visa and Mastercard credit cards, as well as American Express, private-label card brands, and to a certain extent, debit card issuers. Consumer Banking and Commercial Banking compete with national, state, and direct banks, savings and loan associations, credit unions, automotive finance companies, commercial banking companies, and other financial services providers. Following the acquisition of Discover, the company now competes in the global payments industry against traditional competitors and emerging alternative payment providers. Competitive advantages include product quality and range, transaction execution, innovation, price, and for payment network businesses, the strength, reach, pricing, and capabilities of network offerings to merchants, acquirers, and issuers.

The company serves consumers, small businesses, and commercial clients across the United States and internationally through its operations in the United Kingdom and Canada. Its customer base includes individual consumers, small business owners, and commercial entities such as companies in the commercial real estate and commercial and industrial sectors with annual revenues typically between $20 million and $2 billion.

MPC.profile_html:
Marathon Petroleum Corp is a leading integrated downstream and midstream energy company. It operates one of the nation’s largest refining systems with approximately 3.0 million barrels per day of crude oil refining capacity. The company distributes its refined products through one of the largest terminal operations in the United States and a large private domestic fleet of inland petroleum product barges. Its integrated midstream energy asset network links producers of natural gas and NGLs from major supply basins to domestic and international markets. Marathon Petroleum Corp is also one of the largest producers and marketers of renewable diesel in the United States.

Marathon Petroleum Corp generates revenue by refining crude oil and other feedstocks at its refineries and by purchasing refined products and ethanol for resale. It sells refined products to wholesale marketing customers domestically and internationally to spot market buyers to independent entrepreneurs operating Marathon branded outlets and to direct dealers under long term supply contracts mainly for the ARCO brand. The Midstream segment earns revenue by gathering transporting storing and distributing crude oil refined products including renewable diesel and other hydrocarbon based products principally for the Refining & Marketing segment via pipelines terminals towboats and barges. It also gathers treats processes and transports natural gas and transports fractionates stores and markets NGLs. The Renewable Diesel segment earns revenue by processing renewable feedstocks into renewable diesel marketing the product and distributing it through the Midstream segment and third parties. It sells renewable diesel to wholesale marketing customers spot market buyers and direct dealers under long term supply contracts mainly for the ARCO brand.

The company operates through the following segments: Refining & Marketing Midstream Renewable Diesel.

  • Refining & Marketing refines crude oil and other feedstocks at refineries located in the Gulf Coast Mid Continent and West Coast regions purchases refined products and ethanol for resale and distributes refined products through transportation storage distribution and marketing services provided largely by the Midstream segment It sells refined products to wholesale marketing customers domestically and internationally to spot market buyers to independent entrepreneurs operating Marathon branded outlets and to direct dealers under long term supply contracts mainly for the ARCO brand.
  • Midstream gathers transports stores and distributes crude oil refined products including renewable diesel and other hydrocarbon based products principally for the Refining & Marketing segment via pipelines terminals towboats and barges It also gathers treats processes and transports natural gas and transports fractionates stores and markets NGLs The Midstream segment primarily reflects the results of MPLX MPLX is a diversified large cap master limited partnership formed in 2012 that owns and operates midstream energy infrastructure and logistics assets and provides fuels distribution services As of December 31 2025 Marathon Petroleum Corp owned the general partner of MPLX and approximately 64 percent of the outstanding MPLX common units.
  • Renewable Diesel processes renewable feedstocks into renewable diesel markets the product and distributes renewable diesel through the Midstream segment and third parties It sells renewable diesel to wholesale marketing customers spot market buyers and direct dealers under long term supply contracts mainly for the ARCO brand The Dickinson North Dakota renewables facility has capacity to produce 184 million gallons per year of renewable diesel from corn oil soybean oil fats and greases Marathon Petroleum Corp owns an aggregation facility in Cincinnati Ohio and a pretreatment facility in Beatrice Nebraska that supply renewable agricultural feedstocks to the Dickinson and Martinez facilities The Martinez renewable diesel joint venture is a 50 50 partnership with Neste Corporation that refines renewable feedstocks into renewable diesel with capacity of 730 million gallons per year The Green Bison Soy Processing joint venture with Archer Daniels Midland Company has ADM owning 75 percent and MPC owning 25 percent and can produce about 600 million pounds of refined soybean oil annually enough feedstock for about 75 million gallons of renewable diesel per year.

Marathon Petroleum Corp holds a strong position as one of the largest refiners in the United States with a refining capacity that ranks among the top in the country. It is also recognized as a leading wholesale supplier of gasoline and distillates to resellers and consumers. Its extensive terminal network and large inland barge fleet give it competitive advantage in product distribution. The integrated midstream assets provide reliable logistics for crude oil natural gas and NGLs supporting both its own refining operations and third party customers. In the renewable diesel sector Marathon Petroleum Corp is among the largest producers and marketers benefiting from its owned facilities and joint ventures that generate valuable regulatory credits. Key competitors include other major integrated oil companies independent refiners and marketing firms as well as companies that supply alternative fuels such as ethanol biodiesel and electric vehicle charging services.

Marathon Petroleum Corp serves a diverse customer base that includes wholesale marketing companies spot market traders independent entrepreneurs who run Marathon branded outlets and direct dealers who sell fuel under the ARCO brand. Its refined gasoline and distillates are sold to retailers transporters and industrial users. Propane is supplied to home heating customers and to industrial petrochemical consumers. Heavy fuel oil finds markets in utility companies and ship bunkering operations. Asphalt is sold to asphalt paving contractors resellers government entities such as states counties cities and townships and asphalt roofing shingle manufacturers. NGLs and petrochemicals are delivered to chemical plants agricultural processors and fuel blending companies.

Key competitors include other major integrated oil companies independent refiners and marketing firms as well as companies that supply alternative fuels such as ethanol biodiesel and electric vehicle charging services.

ACN.profile_html:
Accenture plc is a leading solutions and global professional services company that helps enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and leveraging AI to create value across the enterprise. The company brings together the talent of approximately 779,000 people, proprietary assets and platforms, and deep ecosystem relationships to deliver solutions and services. Accenture’s strategy focuses on being the reinvention partner of choice for clients, the most AI-enabled and client-focused organization, and a great place to work.

Accenture generates revenue primarily from Consulting and Managed Services delivered to Forbes Global 2000 companies, governments, and government agencies. The company serves more than 9,000 clients, including three-quarters of the Fortune Global 100 and 500, with long-term relationships spanning 10+ years for 195 of its top 200 clients. Revenue is derived from industry-specific solutions across five industry groups and geographic markets, supported by investments in strategic acquisitions, research and development, and learning and professional development.

Accenture operates through the following segments: Strategy and Consulting, Technology, Operations, Song, and Industry X.

  • Strategy and Consulting: This segment works with C-suite executives, leaders, and boards to help organizations reinvent nearly every part of their enterprise, set strategic priorities, build their digital core, reinvent processes, and reimagine their workforce. It drives greater growth, enhances competitiveness, and delivers sustainable 360° stakeholder value. The segment is supported by proprietary assets and platforms that enable faster transformation and increased resilience.
  • Technology: This segment helps clients build their digital core including AI, data, cloud, systems integration, application management, security, intelligent platform services, infrastructure services, software engineering services, automation, and global delivery centers. It continuously innovates solutions and services through early adoption of new technologies such as advanced AI, generative, agentic and physical AI, robotics, 5G, edge computing, and quantum computing. The segment also invests in R&D for new and existing technologies and emerging technologies through Accenture Ventures.
  • Operations: This segment operates business processes on behalf of clients for specific enterprise functions including finance and accounting, sourcing and procurement, supply chain, marketing and sales, human resources, and industry-specific services such as platform trust and safety, banking, insurance, network, and health services. It helps organizations with reinvented operations enabled by SynOps, Accenture’s proprietary AI-powered, cloud-enabled platform that empowers people with data, processes, automation, and a broad ecosystem of technology partners. Experience from operations informs strategy and consulting capabilities to better serve clients.
  • Song: This segment helps clients create new, hyper-personalized experiences and services intelligently designed to foster loyalty and drive growth by making customer interactions more compelling, useful, and simple. It spans design, digital products, marketing, sales, commerce, and customer service, helping brands amplify value by making products, services, and experiences clear and inspiring. The segment leverages AI-powered customer service innovations to make support more responsive and accessible, and uses connected customer strategy, AI, data, ecosystem partnerships, and program management to solve client challenges effectively.
  • Industry X: This segment combines digital capabilities with deep engineering and manufacturing expertise to help clients reinvent and reimagine the products they make and how they make them. It includes capabilities for digitally transforming capital projects from plant and asset construction to public infrastructure, power grids, and data centers. The segment uses data and transformative technologies such as advanced AI, artificial reality/virtual reality, advanced robotics, and digital twins, and collaborates closely with technology ecosystem partners to achieve compressed transformations.

Accenture holds a leading position in the global professional services industry, competing with large multinational IT service providers, offshore IT service providers, accounting firms, consultancies, advertising agency holding companies, engineering services providers, technology start-ups, and in-house IT departments. The company believes no other competitor offers the full range of services at scale, which uniquely positions it in the market. Its competitive advantage stems from its global delivery capability, deep industry expertise across five industry groups, proprietary assets and platforms, strong ecosystem partnerships, and significant investments in AI, innovation, and talent development.

Accenture serves approximately 9,000 clients, including a significant portion of the Fortune Global 100 and 500, with 195 of its top 200 clients maintaining partnerships for 10 or more years. The company has 305 Diamond clients, representing its largest relationships. Key client sectors include Communications, Media & Technology, Financial Services, Health & Public Service, Products, and Resources, with specific clients such as healthcare providers, banks, insurers, retailers, manufacturers, energy companies, and government agencies including the U. S. federal government through Accenture Federal Services.

VLO.address_business: P.O. Box 696000, San Antonio, 78269-6000 Texas, US
VLO.address_mailing: P.O. Box 696000, San Antonio, 78269-6000 Texas, US
VLO.profile_html:
Valero Energy Corporation is an international manufacturer and marketer of transportation fuels, renewable diesel, and ethanol. The company refines crude oil into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, and other petroleum based products, produces renewable diesel from feedstocks such as used cooking oil and animal fats, and manufactures ethanol and corn based co products from corn. Its operations include refineries, renewable diesel plants, and ethanol plants primarily located in the United States, supplying both domestic and export markets. In the first quarter of 2026, Valero’s refining throughput averaged 2,914 thousand barrels per day, renewable diesel sales averaged 3,027 thousand gallons per day, and ethanol production averaged 4,619 thousand gallons per day. The company also maintains an extensive logistics network comprising pipelines, terminals, and storage facilities that facilitate the transportation of crude oil to its refineries and the distribution of refined products to markets.

Valero Energy Corporation generates revenue mainly from the sale of refined petroleum based products including gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel, as well as renewable diesel and ethanol, together with corn based co products. These products are sold to wholesale distributors, retail outlets, blending companies, and industrial users. A portion of its revenue is derived from exporting refined fuels and renewable diesel to international markets.

The company operates through the following segments: Refining, Renewable Diesel, and Ethanol.

  • Refining: This segment processes crude oil into transportation fuels such as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel, and also yields other petroleum based products.
  • Renewable Diesel: This segment produces renewable diesel from renewable feedstocks including used cooking oil, animal fats, and other sustainable sources.
  • Ethanol: This segment manufactures ethanol and corn based co products from corn feedstock.

Valero Energy Corporation ranks among the largest independent refiners in the United States and is a notable producer of renewable diesel and ethanol. It competes with other major independent and integrated refiners as well as renewable fuel producers. The company’s competitive advantages stem from its integrated operations across refining, renewable diesel, and ethanol, its substantial throughput volumes, its diversified product portfolio that helps mitigate market volatility, and its extensive infrastructure comprising refineries, renewable diesel plants, ethanol plants, and associated logistics assets. In addition, Valero’s renewable diesel and ethanol plants contribute to its production of low carbon fuels.

Valero Energy Corporation sells its products primarily to wholesale distributors, retail outlets, and blended fuel wholesalers, as well as to industrial users and other energy companies. Its customer base is concentrated in the refining industry and among wholesalers and retailers of petroleum based products, which helps ensure steady demand for its fuels and co products. Its products are sold to customers throughout the United States and to various overseas markets.

LMT.name: Lockheed Martin Corp
LMT.profile_html:
Lockheed Martin Corp is a global aerospace and defense technology company that designs manufactures and sustains advanced systems for national security and scientific exploration. The company operates in the aerospace and defense industry providing integrated solutions across air land sea space and cyber domains.

Lockheed Martin Corp generates revenue mainly from long term contracts with the U. S. Government and allied nations for the design production and sustainment of military aircraft missile systems helicopters space satellites and related services. The company also earns income from logistics training and support contracts that accompany its delivered systems.

The company operates through the following segments: Aeronautics, Missiles and Fire Control (MFC), Rotary and Mission Systems (RMS), and Space.

  • Aeronautics is engaged in the research design development manufacture integration sustainment support and upgrade of advanced military aircraft including combat and air mobility aircraft unmanned air vehicles and related technologies. The segment also holds contracts with the U. S. Government for various classified programs. Major programs include the F-35 Lightning II multi role fifth generation stealth fighter the C-130 Hercules international tactical airlifter the F-16 Fighting Falcon combat proven multi role fighter and the F-22 Raptor air dominance and multi role fifth generation stealth fighter. The F-35 program is the largest contributor to total sales and to Aeronautics sales. In addition the segment runs Advanced Development Programs also known as Skunk Works that focus on future systems such as unmanned and manned aerial systems and next generation capabilities for air dominance hypersonics intelligence surveillance reconnaissance situational awareness and air mobility. Aeronautics also invests in network enabled activities that allow separate systems to work together to increase effectiveness and it continues to insert new technologies into existing aircraft designs.
  • Missiles and Fire Control provides air and missile defense systems tactical missiles and precision strike weapon systems logistics fire control systems mission operations support readiness engineering support and integration services. The segment also holds contracts with the U. S. Government for various classified programs. Major programs include the Patriot Advanced Capability Three (PAC 3) and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) air and missile defense programs. Additional programs are the Multiple Launch Rocket System (MLRS) Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) Joint Air to Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM) Long Range Anti Ship Missile (LRASM) Hellfire and Joint Air to Ground Missile (JAGM) tactical and strike missile programs. The Javelin program is a one person portable anti tank and multi target precision weapon system produced jointly with RTX Corporation. The segment also supplies the Apache fire control system the Sniper Advanced Targeting Pod (SNIPER) and the Infrared Search and Track (IRST21) sensors along with global sustainment programs. It provides the Special Operations Forces Global Logistics Support Services (SOF GLSS) program and conducts hypersonics programs with the U. S. Air Force and the U. S. Army.
  • Rotary and Mission Systems designs manufactures services and supports various military and commercial helicopters sea and land based missile defense systems radar systems laser systems sea and air based mission and combat systems command and control mission solutions cyber solutions simulation and training solutions and services and supports surface ships. The segment also holds contracts with the U. S. Government for various classified programs. Major lines of business include Sikorsky helicopter programs such as the Black Hawk Seahawk and CH-53K King Stallion heavy lift helicopters and the Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) utilized by the U. S. Air Force. Integrated warfare systems and sensors (IWSS) programs such as the Aegis Combat System (Aegis) that serve as an air and missile defense system for the U. S. Navy and international customers and are also a sea and land based element of the U. S. missile defense system and the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) Multi Mission Surface Combatant (MMSC) and River Class Destroyer (RCD) programs that provide surface combatant ships for the U. S. Navy and international customers designed to operate in shallow waters and the open ocean. Command control communications computers cyber combat systems intelligence surveillance and reconnaissance (C6ISR) programs such as the Command Control Battle Management and Communications (C2BMC) program that provides an air operations center for the Ballistic Missile Defense System for the U. S. Government undersea combat systems programs largely serving the U. S. Navy and Australia's Joint Air Battle Management System (AIR 6500). Training logistics and simulation (TLS) programs that provide sustainment services and simulators with associated training to U. S. military and foreign government customers. Effective January 2026 the IWSS and C6ISR lines of business within RMS were restructured and renamed Sensors Effectors & Mission Systems (SEMS) and Mission Integrated Command and Control (MIC2). This includes realignment of various programs such as Aegis and RCD moving from what was historically IWSS to MIC2 which more closely aligns with C6ISR. SEMS and MIC2 will therefore incorporate an updated mix of existing program portfolios designed to accelerate mission focused solutions and enhance our customers experience.
  • Space is engaged in the research and design development engineering and production of satellites space transportation systems and strategic advanced strike and defensive systems. The segment provides network enabled situational awareness and integrates complex space and ground global systems to help customers gather analyze and securely distribute critical intelligence data. Space also handles various classified systems and services in support of vital national security systems. Major programs include the Trident II D5 Fleet Ballistic Missile (FBM) program with the U. S. Navy for the only submarine launched intercontinental ballistic missile currently in production in the United States. The Next Generation Overhead Persistent Infrared (Next Gen OPIR) system provides the U. S. Space Force with enhanced worldwide missile warning capabilities. The Next Generation Interceptor (NGI) program with the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) utilizes next generation propulsion and sensors to provide homeland missile defense. The Orion Multi-Purpose Crew Vehicle (Orion) is NASA's next generation exploration class crewed vehicle for human exploration to the Moon and throughout the solar system. The Global Positioning System (GPS) III program modernizes the GPS satellite system for the U. S. Space Force. Hypersonics programs with the U. S. Army and the U. S. Navy focus on designing developing and building hypersonic strike weapons. The Transport and Tracking Layer programs consist of multiple tranches of small satellites that support the proliferated space architecture with constellations of missile warning and communications satellites for the Space Development Agency.

Lockheed Martin Corp holds a leading position in the global aerospace and defense sector competing primarily with Boeing General Dynamics L3Harris Technologies Northrop Grumman and RTX Corporation. The industry is marked by long operating cycles and intense competition for government contracts. The company's competitive advantages stem from its technical excellence reliability safety and cost competitiveness of its products and services. It also benefits from strong technical and management capability a proven ability to innovate and develop new products that improve mission performance and adapt to evolving threats. Successful program execution and on time delivery of complex integrated systems further strengthen its market standing. Lockheed Martin Corp leverages its reputation and customer confidence built on past performance and its ability to manage customer relationships effectively. Its global footprint and accessibility to customers allow it to serve both domestic and international markets. The firm often collaborates with competitors through teaming arrangements to offer comprehensive solutions while also participating as a subcontractor on other contracts.

Lockheed Martin Corp serves primarily agencies of the U. S. Government and allied nations. Its customer base includes the U. S. Army the U. S. Navy the U. S. Air Force the U. S. Marine Corps NASA the Missile Defense Agency the Space Development Agency and various international governments and foreign military sales partners. The company also works with commercial customers for certain space and technology projects.

HDB.profile_html:
HDFC Bank Ltd is a new-generation private sector bank in India that provides a comprehensive range of financial services to customers across metro, urban, semi-urban and rural markets. The company’s principal business activities are retail banking, wholesale banking, treasury services and insurance services. Through its retail banking division, HDFC Bank Ltd offers deposit products, loans including housing loans and loans to small and medium enterprises, credit cards, debit cards, third-party mutual funds and insurance products, bill payment services and other related offerings. Its wholesale banking operations deliver commercial and transactional banking services such as working capital finance, trade services, transactional services, cash management and structured solutions that combine cash management with vendor and distributor finance to facilitate supply chain management for corporate customers, including construction finance. The treasury services segment manages the bank’s balance sheet, including liquidity and interest rate risks, and provides customer-driven services such as advisory services related to foreign exchange and derivative transactions for corporate and institutional customers, supplemented by proprietary trading in Indian Government securities. Since the completion of the Transaction with HDFC Limited on July 1, 2023, HDFC Bank Ltd has also been engaged in life and general insurance, asset management and securities broking products and services through its specialized subsidiaries and joint venture.

HDFC Bank Ltd generates revenue primarily through interest income from its lending activities, fees and commissions from banking and financial services, and trading income from its treasury operations. Retail banking contributes significantly to revenue through interest on loans such as home loans, auto loans, personal loans and loans to small and medium enterprises, as well as fees from credit and debit card services, third-party mutual fund distribution and insurance product sales. Wholesale banking generates revenue from interest on working capital loans, trade finance fees, cash management services and structured supply chain solutions. The treasury services segment earns revenue from proprietary trading in government securities, foreign exchange and derivative transactions, along with advisory fees for corporate and institutional clients. Following the Transaction, the company’s subsidiaries and joint venture contribute additional revenue streams: HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited provides long-term life insurance solutions, HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited offers general insurance products, HDFC Asset Management Company Limited manages a comprehensive suite of savings and investment products as one of India’s largest mutual fund managers, and HDFC Securities Limited provides brokerage accounts across equity, gold and debt asset classes via online, mobile, telephone and branch platforms. HDB Financial Services Limited, the NBFC subsidiary, offers mortgage loans, commercial vehicle loans, consumer loans, gold loans and business process outsourcing solutions, further diversifying the company’s income sources.

The company operates through the following segments: retail banking, wholesale banking, treasury services and insurance services.

  • Retail banking: This segment provides deposit products, loans including housing loans and loans to small and medium enterprises, credit cards, debit cards, third-party mutual funds and insurance products, bill payment services and other related offerings. The segment serves individual customers, small businesses and semi-urban and rural populations through a wide network of branches and digital channels. HDFC Bank Ltd leverages its brand strength and advanced technology platforms to deliver high-quality retail banking services across India.
  • Wholesale banking: This segment offers a wide range of commercial and transactional banking services, including working capital finance, trade services, transactional services and cash management. The company is also a leading provider of structured solutions in India that combine cash management services with vendor and distributor finance to facilitate supply chain management for corporate customers. Since the completion of the Transaction, the segment has expanded to include construction finance for corporate clients. These services are delivered to large corporations, institutions and mid-sized enterprises seeking customized financial solutions.

BMO.profile_html:
Bank of Montreal is a highly diversified financial services provider based in North America, offering a broad range of personal and commercial banking, wealth management, global markets, and investment banking products and services directly and through Canadian and non-Canadian subsidiaries, offices, and branches.

The company generates revenue through interest income from lending activities, fees from wealth management and investment services, trading and capital markets revenues, and service charges across its banking operations, serving individual, commercial, and institutional clients.

The company operates through the following segments: Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking; U. S. Banking; Wealth Management; and Capital Markets; supported by Corporate Services, including Technology and Operations.

  • Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking provides deposit taking, lending, and other banking services to individuals and businesses in Canada through branches, automated banking machines, and digital platforms.
  • U. S. Banking delivers banking, financing, investing, and cash management services across the United States primarily through BMO Bank N. A. and BMO Harris Central N. A.
  • Wealth Management offers investment advisory, asset management, financial planning, and insurance products to retail and institutional clients through entities including BMO Nesbitt Burns Inc. and other wealth management subsidiaries.
  • Capital Markets provides investment banking, global markets, corporate lending, and equity and debt underwriting services through BMO Capital Markets Corp. and related investment dealer entities in Canada and the United States.

Bank of Montreal holds a strong position in the North American financial services industry, competing with major banks such as Royal Bank of Canada, Toronto-Dominion Bank, JPMorgan Chase, and Bank of America, leveraging its integrated cross-border platform and diversified revenue streams as key competitive advantages.

The company serves individual consumers, small and medium-sized enterprises, large corporations, institutional investors, and government entities across its operating segments.

BP.name: Bp Plc
BP.address_business: 1 St James'S Square, London, Sw1Y 4Pd United Kingdom
BP.address_mailing: 1 St James'S Square, London, Sw1Y 4Pd United Kingdom
BP.profile_html:
Bp Plc is an integrated energy company engaged in the exploration production refining marketing and trading of hydrocarbons and renewable energy sources. The corporation operates across the full value chain from upstream field development to downstream product distribution. Its activities include the extraction of crude oil and natural gas the processing of these resources into fuels lubricants and petrochemicals and the generation of power from wind solar and biofuel assets. Bp Plc maintains a global presence with operations in Europe the Americas Africa Asia and Australasia. Bp Plc possesses a long history and development trajectory as documented in the filing’s history and development section. The firm’s organizational structure is detailed in the filing’s organizational structure section indicating a complex arrangement of subsidiaries and functional units. Additionally the filing’s property plants and equipment section outlines the extensive tangible assets that support its operational capabilities. Bp Plc seeks to align its traditional oil and gas operations with investments in low carbon technologies to address changing energy market expectations.

Bp Plc generates revenue primarily through the sale of crude oil natural gas refined petroleum products petrochemicals and renewable energy certificates. Upstream operations deliver earnings from the production and sale of hydrocarbons extracted from offshore and onshore fields. Downstream operations earn income from refining crude oil into gasoline diesel jet fuel and lubricants as well as from marketing these products to retail and wholesale customers. The company also earns fees from trading physical and financial energy contracts and from licensing its technology and brand. Additionally Bp Plc receives income from its renewable portfolio including wind farms solar installations and biofuel production facilities.

Bp Plc holds a position among the largest integrated energy corporations often referred to as supermajors. Its principal competitors include ExxonMobil Shell Chevron TotalEnergies and Chevron. The company differentiates itself through its extensive global infrastructure its strong brand recognition and its capability to manage complex projects across diverse geographies. Bp Plc invests heavily in research and development to improve extraction efficiency lower emissions and advance alternative energy solutions. Its scale allows it to achieve cost advantages in procurement logistics and risk management while maintaining flexibility to adapt to market shifts and regulatory changes.

Bp Plc serves a broad range of customers that includes individual motorists commercial transport operators industrial manufacturers airlines shipping companies and governmental agencies. Retail customers purchase fuels and lubricants at the company’s service station network. Industrial clients acquire feedstocks for plastics fertilizers and other chemical processes. Aviation and marine sectors obtain specialized jet fuel and marine diesel from Bp Plc’s dedicated supply channels. The corporation also supplies natural gas to utilities and power generators for electricity production and heating purposes.

SPGI.address_mailing: 55 Water Street, New York, 10041 New York, US
SPGI.profile_html:
S&P Global Inc. is a global, diversified provider of benchmarks, data, analytics and workflow solutions in the global capital, energy and commodity, and automotive markets. The company serves asset managers, investment banks, commercial banks, insurance companies, exchanges, trading firms and issuers in capital markets; producers, consumers, traders and intermediaries in energy, chemicals, shipping, metals, carbon and agriculture; and manufacturers, suppliers, dealerships, service shops and customers in automotive markets. S&P Global delivers its products and services through third-party and proprietary distribution channels worldwide.

S&P Global generates revenue primarily through subscription-based offerings, transaction fees, and non-subscription services across its five businesses. Subscription revenue comes from data platforms, analytics software, price assessments, and index-linked products delivered via feed, web, or API channels. Transaction revenue includes fees for credit ratings on new debt issuances, bank loans, and advisory services. Non-subscription revenue stems from conferences, consulting engagements, perpetual software licenses, and usage-based royalties from commodity exchanges and derivatives trading.

The company operates through the following segments: S&P Global Market Intelligence, S&P Global Ratings, S&P Global Energy, S&P Global Mobility, and S&P Dow Jones Indices.

  • S&P Global Market Intelligence: This segment provides multi-asset-class data and analytics integrated with purpose-built workflow solutions for trading and investment professionals, government agencies, corporations and universities. Its capabilities support performance tracking, alpha generation, investment idea generation, competitive analysis, valuation and credit risk management. Key product lines include the Capital IQ platforms (S&P Capital IQ Pro, Capital IQ, Office and Mobile), Wall Street Office, Enterprise Data Manager, Information Mosaic, iLevel, RatingsXpress®, RatingsDirect® and Credit Analytics.
  • S&P Global Ratings: This segment is an independent provider of credit ratings, research and analytics on corporate and government debt issuers worldwide. Its forward-looking opinions assess issuers’ ability and willingness to meet financial obligations and the credit quality of individual debt issues such as corporate or municipal bonds. Ratings serves investors, corporations, governments, municipalities, commercial and investment banks, insurance companies, asset managers and other debt issuers through a global network spanning over 25 countries.
  • S&P Global Energy: This segment delivers essential price data, analytics, industry insights and software services for energy and commodity markets including petroleum, gas, power & renewables, petrochemicals, metals & steel, agriculture and other commodities. Its business lines consist of Energy & Resources Data & Insights, Price Assessments (including benchmarks and forward curves), Upstream Data & Insights, and Advisory & Transactional Services. Revenue is generated through subscriptions to market data and insights, sales usage-based royalties from licensing price data to exchanges, and non-subscription sources like conferences and consulting.
  • S&P Global Mobility: This segment serves the full automotive value chain including vehicle manufacturers (OEMs), suppliers, mobility service providers, retailers, consumers and finance and insurance companies. It offers analytics to predict future buyers, targeted marketing, vehicle history data for used car transactions, insights and forecasts spanning product planning to aftermarket, and reports and data feeds for lenders and insurers. Mobility operates across new and used car markets, providing forecasting, market reporting, predictive analytics, marketing automation software and vehicle history services.
  • S&P Dow Jones Indices: This segment maintains a wide variety of valuation and index benchmarks for investment advisors, wealth managers and institutional investors. It provides transparent benchmarks to support decision making, collaborates with the financial community to create innovative products, and offers tools to monitor world markets. Revenue is derived from asset-linked fees (such as ETFs and mutual funds based on its benchmarks), sales usage-based royalties from exchange traded derivatives, index-related licensing fees for OTC derivatives and retail-structured products, and data and customized index subscription fees.

S&P Global holds a leading position in its core markets as a highly differentiated provider of critical financial and market infrastructure. The company benefits from strong brand recognition, particularly in credit ratings through S&P Global Ratings and in benchmarks through S&P Dow Jones Indices, where its indices are widely referenced across global investment products. Its competitive advantages include proprietary data sets, advanced analytics platforms, deep industry expertise and entrenched workflow integrations with major financial institutions, energy traders and automotive OEMs.

S&P Global serves a diverse global customer base including asset managers, investment banks, commercial banks, insurance companies, exchanges, trading firms and issuers; energy producers, consumers, traders and intermediaries; and automotive manufacturers, suppliers, dealerships, service shops and consumers. Specific customer types referenced in the filing include investment managers, private equity firms, corporations, professional services firms, government agencies, regulators, OEMs, leading automotive suppliers, top North American dealerships, lenders and insurance companies supporting underwriting and claims management activities.

BTI.name: British American Tobacco p.l.c.
BTI.profile_html:
British American Tobacco p.l.c. is a leading multi-category consumer goods business that provides tobacco and nicotine products to millions of adult consumers worldwide. The Group operates a globally integrated supply chain and manufactures a diverse portfolio spanning combustibles, smokeless products, and oral nicotine offerings. Its core activities include the production, marketing, and distribution of cigarettes, heated tobacco products, vapour products, and modern and traditional oral nicotine products across over 140 markets.

British American Tobacco p.l.c. generates revenue primarily through the sale of its tobacco and nicotine product portfolio to adult consumers via retail channels globally. The company's revenue is derived from four main product categories: Combustibles, New Categories (which include Vapour, Heated Products, and Modern Oral), Traditional Oral, and Other. In 2025, Combustibles contributed £20,201 million or 78.9% of total revenue, New Categories generated £3,621 million or 14.1%, Traditional Oral amounted to £1,043 million or 4.1%, and Other accounted for £745 million or 2.9%, resulting in total revenue of £25,610 million.

British American Tobacco p.l.c. operates through the following segments: Combustibles, New Categories, Traditional Oral, and Other.

  • Combustibles: This segment includes the manufacture and sale of cigarettes and other tobacco products such as cigarillos and fine cut tobacco. The Group sold 465 billion cigarette sticks and 12 billion other tobacco products (stick equivalents) in 2025. Its combustible brands include internationally recognised names such as Dunhill, Kent, Lucky Strike, Pall Mall, and Rothmans, along with regional and local brands tailored to specific markets.
  • New Categories: This segment encompasses the Group’s smokeless and reduced-risk product portfolio, including Vapour, Heated Products (HPs), and Modern Oral products. Vapour products are led by the global brand Vuse, which is the #1 brand in the rechargeable closed system vapour category in tracked channels. Heated Products are centred around the flagship brand glo, with premium innovations like glo Hilo and glo Hilo Plus offering dual-heating technology. Modern Oral products are dominated by the Velo brand, including innovations such as Velo Plus and Velo Shift, which are nicotine pouches placed between the gum and upper lip.
  • Traditional Oral: This segment focuses on snus and snuff products, which are moist forms of oral tobacco placed between the lip and gum for nicotine absorption. Traditional Oral products are available in loose form or as pouches and are marketed under specific regional brands. As of the date of the Form 20-F, Traditional Oral brands are currently available in 3 markets, reflecting the niche but established nature of this category in select regions.
  • Other: This segment includes revenue from ancillary activities not directly tied to the core product categories, such as contract manufacturing, royalties, and other minor business lines. While specific brand names are not highlighted in this segment, it supports the Group’s overall operations through supplementary income streams. The Other segment contributed £745 million to total revenue in 2025, representing 2.9% of the Group’s overall sales.

British American Tobacco p.l.c. holds a leading position in the global tobacco and nicotine industry, ranking among the world’s largest tobacco companies by volume and revenue. The Group competes with major international players such as Philip Morris International, Japan Tobacco International, and Imperial Brands, while maintaining strong market positions in key geographies through its diversified portfolio. Its competitive advantages include a globally integrated supply chain, deep consumer insights, a broad brand portfolio spanning multiple price points and categories, and ongoing investment in reduced-risk products to align with evolving consumer preferences and regulatory trends.

British American Tobacco p.l.c. serves millions of adult consumers worldwide who use tobacco and nicotine products. The company’s customer base consists entirely of adult users of cigarettes, heated tobacco, vapour products, and oral nicotine products across its operating regions. While the filing does not disclose specific individual customer names due to the consumer-facing nature of its business, the Group distributes its products through retail outlets including convenience stores, supermarkets, tobacco specialists, and online channels in over 140 markets.

While specific brand names are not highlighted in this segment, it supports the Group’s overall operations through supplementary income streams. The Other segment contributed £745 million to total revenue in 2025, representing 2.9% of the Group’s overall sales.

British American Tobacco p.l.c. holds a leading position in the global tobacco and nicotine industry, ranking among the world’s largest tobacco companies by volume and revenue. The Group competes with major international players such as Philip Morris International, Japan Tobacco International, and Imperial Brands, while maintaining strong market positions in key geographies through its diversified portfolio. Its competitive advantages include a globally integrated supply chain, deep consumer insights, a broad brand portfolio spanning multiple price points and categories, and ongoing investment in reduced-risk products to align with evolving consumer preferences and regulatory trends.

British American Tobacco p.l.c. serves millions of adult consumers worldwide who use tobacco and nicotine products. The company’s customer base consists entirely of adult users of cigarettes, heated tobacco, vapour products, and oral nicotine products across its operating regions. While the filing does not disclose specific individual customer names due to the consumer-facing nature of its business, the Group distributes its products through retail outlets including convenience stores, supermarkets, tobacco specialists, and online channels in over 140 markets.

MO.profile_html:
Altria Group, Inc. is a leading producer of tobacco products for consumers aged 21 and older in the United States. The company pursues a vision of moving beyond smoking by responsibly transitioning adult smokers to smoke free alternatives while competing for existing smoke free nicotine consumers and exploring new growth opportunities. Its wholly owned subsidiaries include Philip Morris USA Inc. which manufactures and sells cigarettes; John Middleton Co. which manufactures and sells machine made large cigars; UST LLC through its subsidiary U. S. Smokeless Tobacco Company LLC which manufactures and sells moist smokeless tobacco; Helix Innovations LLC and its foreign affiliates which manufacture and sell oral nicotine pouches; and NJOY LLC which manufactures and sells e vapor products. Altria Group, Inc. operates primarily within the United States and generates substantially all of its revenue from domestic customers.

Altria Group, Inc. generates revenue principally from the sale of its tobacco and nicotine products to wholesalers, distributors and large retail organizations including chain stores. The company’s cigarette business delivers revenue from brands such as Marlboro sold through Philip Morris USA Inc. Its cigar business contributes revenue from machine made large cigars such as Black & Mild sold by John Middleton Co. Revenue from moist smokeless tobacco comes from brands like Copenhagen and Skoal sold by U. S. Smokeless Tobacco Company LLC. Oral nicotine pouches sold under the on! brand by Helix Innovations LLC also generate revenue. E vapor products sold by NJOY LLC, including the NJOY ACE line, add to the company’s sales. Additional revenue is derived from domestic sales and distribution services provided by Altria Group Distribution Company and support services from Altria Client Services LLC, though these are internal to the consolidated entity.

The company operates through the following segments: smokeable products, oral tobacco products, and e vapor products.

  • Smokeable products include combustible cigarettes manufactured and sold by Philip Morris USA Inc. and machine made large cigars manufactured and sold by John Middleton Co. The Marlboro brand remains the top selling cigarette brand in the United States while Black & Mild is the principal cigar brand. In 2025 cigarette shipment volume was 61.8 billion units and cigar shipment volume was approximately 1.8 billion units.
  • Oral tobacco products consist of moist smokeless tobacco manufactured and sold by U. S. Smokeless Tobacco Company LLC under the Copenhagen Skoal and Red Seal brands and oral nicotine pouches manufactured and sold by Helix Innovations LLC under the on! brand. In 2025 shipment volume for the oral tobacco products segment was 732.4 million units.
  • E vapor products are manufactured and sold by NJOY LLC which contracts with third party importers to supply its devices and liquids. The NJOY ACE product is the principal offering and has received marketing granted orders from the U. S. Food and Drug Administration. In 2025 NJOY sold its e vapor products to customers across the United States.

Altria Group, Inc. holds a leading position in the United States tobacco market as the largest cigarette manufacturer and a top producer of moist smokeless tobacco and machine made large cigars. The company competes with other major tobacco groups such as Reynolds American Inc. a subsidiary of British American Tobacco PLC and Imperial Brands PLC as well as smaller niche players in the cigar and oral nicotine categories. Its competitive advantages stem from a portfolio of iconic brands including Marlboro Copenhagen Skoal Black & Mild on! and NJOY ACE extensive scale in manufacturing and distribution and deep expertise in navigating federal state and local tobacco regulations. Additionally the company’s investments in Anheuser Busch InBev SA/NV and Cronos Group Inc. provide diversification beyond traditional tobacco though these are accounted for under the equity method.

Altria Group, Inc. sells its products to wholesalers including distributors and to large retail organizations such as chain stores convenience stores and other outlets that serve adult tobacco consumers. The company’s customer base consists primarily of these downstream channels which then make the products available to retail consumers aged 21 and older. No specific customer names are disclosed in the filing.
